items.d: The 30th anniversary book fair around the Chiang Mai University library: publishers, shops, books, food, postcards, toys; there are tables of second-hand books, with lots of English textbooks and children’s books.
items.a: CMU Main Library, Chiang Mai University

items.d: Flow arts classes: spinning poi, fire fans, the Dragon Staff, hula hoops and double hoops; suitable for beginners, booking in advance.
Tasty smoothies and coffee, lovely owners and the dog Mumu; you can also rent a scooter here, with a massage next door.
A light show with a musical fountain, lights, music and fireworks, daily from November 27 to January 3. Free entry.
One of the biggest music festivals in Northern Thailand: two days, several stages and more than 40 artists, among them Jeff Satur, Three Man Down, Slot Machine, Big Ass, Scrubb and Tilly Birds.
items.a: Royal Train Garden Resort, Hang Dong
items.p: 1 600 ฿ for both days (Final Call until November 27 23:59), regular price 2 000 ฿

items.n: Nakadia — a techno party at Warm Up Café
items.d: The Thai techno DJ Nakadia for one night at Warm Up Café, also SWILL’O, FØSTER and LIMITLESS; the venue holds 100 people.
A hip-hop party with DJ sets and live performances, headlined by Khuli Chana; all the money raised goes to the education of displaced children on the Thai–Myanmar border. Adults only.
items.a: RED CNX, 3rd floor, Huay Kaew Road
items.p: 250 ฿ online, 500 ฿ at the door, 150 ฿ for local students

items.n: Jing Jai Market × You Ni Market
items.d: Makers from the Malaysian You Ni Market are guests at Jing Jai Market for the first time.
Free morning Sound Healing classes at Jirung Health Village with a 15-minute walk around the grounds; places are limited, booking required.
The annual flowering season at Royal Park Rajapruek, this year for the park's 20th anniversary: seasonal flowers, themed gardens, orchids, pavilions and walking routes; good for an outing with kids.
items.p: for foreigners: adult 200 ฿, child 100–140 cm 150 ฿, under 100 cm free

items.n: Chiang Mai Border Run & Visa Run Service
items.d: A same-day border run to Laos that also works with a DTV. You can pay for the bus only, without an escort. Travelers on a tourist visa without a return ticket for the next day may be kept overnight in Laos.
items.p: 4300 baht all-inclusive with an escort (VIP bus); bus only — 1800 baht online + 200 baht to the driver; fee at the Laos border 500 baht with a DTV, 2000 baht for “providing” for others; a third overland border run on a tourist visa via another bridge — 9500 baht
items.h: departs at 6:30 from Burger King on Tha Phae, back in town around 18:00

items.d: A vintage market at Jing Jai Market.
An exhibition of crafts and products inspired by local traditions, made by Thai and Japanese students.
An evening market in a minimalist rustic style at Jing Jai Market.
A big holiday market at Jing Jai Market with a Christmas atmosphere and lots of events.
A Christmas market of treats at Jing Jai Village.
You can join in and dance to random music at Jing Jai Market.
A holiday program at Jing Jai Market: music, entertainment and shopping.

A small place for bowls and salads: quality ingredients, generous portions, good prices, and the calories and macros of the dishes are listed. Geared to takeaway and delivery — there is one table inside.

A Facebook group where local sellers offer fresh produce and ready-cooked food with free delivery; handy if you have no kitchen at home. Tip: write to the sellers in Thai so they don’t raise the price.
items.p: ready-cooked chicken breast, 1 kg — 120–140 baht, free delivery

items.d: A house with a big garden and 3 bedrooms about 2 km from Lanna International School: a kitchen with a gas stove, a living room, a washing machine outside. Rented whole or by the room, lease until June 6, 2027.
items.p: room — 10 000 ฿/month + a share of the utilities; whole house — 30 000 ฿/month, deposit 60 000 ฿

items.d: A nice restaurant for dinner, Burmese food in a fusion style.
A flower festival from November 27 to January 3: huge flower arrangements, winter flowers and orchids, illuminations, light shows, a water screen, music, food and cultural events. Free entry.
items.a: Chiang Mai PAO Park (สวน อบจ.เชียงใหม่)

items.n: HOKA Chiang Mai Thailand by UTMB
items.d: An international trail running competition on November 27–29; the first part of the program is in Doi Inthanon National Park, and lots of runners from all over the world are expected. From the Chiang Mai events calendar for November 21–29, 2026.
items.a: Doi Inthanon; Chiang Mai PAO Park

items.d: After renovation, a playground for children and parents has opened, with sports areas for adults, a shady garden, non-alcoholic and Thai craft beer, and food; free entry.

items.n: Opening of the family playground at WILDSIDE Garden
items.d: The opening of Chiang Mai's first playground where kids and parents are active together: a playground, workout zones for adults, a garden, drinks and food. Entry is free.

items.n: Arsenic pollution of the Kok and Sai rivers
items.d: Residents of Tha Ton (Mae Ai) have lived with the pollution of the Kok River for three years: they buy water for drinking and household use, and arsenic levels in people are rising; the pollution is linked to mining in Myanmar.
A festival for the opening of Rimping Sankamphaeng: more than 200 food and drink stalls, a camping area, live music, kids' activities and contests.
The Ministry of Culture calls on everyone to wear traditional Thai clothes on December 2, when UNESCO considers the bid to add the Chud Thai costume to the Intangible Cultural Heritage list.
Reopened after a revamp: a modern interior, indoor and outdoor areas; new steaks, burgers, pasta with shrimp and spinach, salads, soups and desserts on the menu.

items.n: Southern border provinces and OTOP fair
items.d: A fair of goods from the southern provinces (Satun, Songkhla, Pattani, Yala, Narathiwat) and OTOP from all over the country: produce, southern cuisine, seafood, spices, sweets, tea, handicrafts and fabrics.
A new sports club on the grounds of a condominium: fitness, pool, sauna, contrast therapy, yoga room, co-working and a rooftop garden; 500 ฿ off a monthly membership for the first three months.
items.p: adult monthly 2 000 ฿, kids (1–12) 650 ฿; day pass 250 ฿, child 80 ฿

items.d: Live saxophone in the park by half.cnx again, on Sunday, December 6.

A punk night at Yoda's CNX Gallery: Death By System, Olek, Self Sex, Phased Plasma Rifle, Määräys and Two and the Queen. The Australian Celtic punk band The Rumjacks, billed as the headliner, cancelled (post of November 19). Tickets through the organisers on Facebook.

The Loy Krathong parade in the municipality's program: from Tha Phae Gate along Tha Phae Road across the Ping River to Chiang Mai city hall; 26 floats compete for the royal cup. The actual start may be badly delayed.
items.a: Tha Phae Gate – Tha Phae Road – Chiang Mai Municipality Office

items.d: In late November sapodilla shows up at Chiang Mai's markets.
items.p: 80 on the price card at the market

items.n: Russian House at Chiang Mai Design Week 2026 (Russian Warmth: Living Traditions)
items.d: The Russian Warmth pavilion: 150–200 works by 20–25 Russian brands and makers, master classes in needlework and matryoshka dolls, a tea party with a samovar, evening music, trying on kokoshniks, talks, and fairy-tale evenings for kids on weekends.
items.a: Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center
items.p: free entry; master classes free with advance registration

items.d: The world of scents at Chiang Mai Design Week: more than 50 local brands, perfume compositions and natural ingredients; Balance Imbalance, an immersive exhibition about Chiang Mai through smells, and the Scents Asia Awards competition.
Traditional Yi Peng lanterns reimagined: Saa paper, ceramics and 3D printing. A Chiang Mai Design Week project.
items.a: Sri Lanna Thai Women’s Culture Promotion Association

items.d: A modern look at northern Thai fabrics, patterns and craft techniques: designers rethink the local textile heritage. A Chiang Mai Design Week project.
items.a: Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center

items.d: A Chiang Mai Design Week project about how old and unwanted materials turn into design objects.
items.a: Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center

items.d: A Chiang Mai Design Week project where pop culture, music, design and the Lanna cultural heritage meet.
items.a: Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center

items.d: An international Chiang Mai Design Week project on sustainable design, textiles, eco-friendly materials and cultural heritage.

items.n: POP MARKET at Chiang Mai Design Week 2026
items.d: A market of local designers, makers and creative entrepreneurs: handmade goods and original pieces where traditional techniques meet modern design.
A collective of Northern Thai designers experiments with materials and forms, making a space for creative exchange. A Chiang Mai Design Week project.
The Chiang Mai Design Week music program with Northern Thai artists and creative communities.
A wellness day party at JT Forest for Loy Krathong: a DJ set by Sandesh, a pool, a sauna and an ice bath, and you can dance barefoot in nature.
items.a: Hang Dong, JT Forest, Nam Phrae

items.d: Traditional Thai clothing rental with makeup and hair styling, for dressing up for a festival.
White-and-pink and purple magnolias bloom at the Royal Agricultural Station Angkhang; the bloom usually lasts from November to January.
The venue of the CAD lantern festival; its reviews on the map are paradoxical, “a real anti-ad”.
A good cleaner in the Hang Dong area, reachable through LINE.
A WhatsApp group with housing rental listings in Chiang Mai, monthly and short-term.
Chansom Bridge by Kad Luang: a beautiful view of Yi Peng, lights and the festive atmosphere of old Chiang Mai.

items.n: Yi Peng in the ancient town of Wiang Tha Kan
items.d: Yi Peng at the Wiang Tha Kan archaeological site: Buddhist sermons, the story of Prince Vessantara, a traditional maze, Lanna dance and music, Bok Fai Dok fireworks and the Kad Mua Khua Hom market. According to a report from the scene, lanterns are handed out for free, and there's a slide and a trampoline for kids.
items.a: Wiang Tha Kan Archaeological Site, San Pa Tong

items.d: A bathhouse under construction at Prasert Land, Nimman Soi 6.

items.n: How to watch the CAD lantern release without a ticket
items.d: An expat's tip: ride a scooter to CAD Cultural Center Lanna and walk a bit past the main entrance, from where you can see the release over the fence; lanterns are sold on the way. Because of traffic jams a scooter is better; you can also ask people who are leaving for their ticket.

A dental clinic recommended for its honest approach: the dentist checked the nerve, found it alive and charged just 200 baht, while another clinic had quoted 20 000 baht for a restoration plus urgent nerve removal.
A nice new breakfast cafe in Mae Hia: coffee in different roasts, and the owner used to be a barista in Melbourne.

items.n: Wanted: a tall foreigner for a cultural show
items.d: A tall foreign man of about 20–29 is wanted for a cultural performance and festive procession: he will stand on a platform or palanquin carried by the participants. Rehearsal November 27, performance November 28; details from the organizer, Pom.

A morning event: a Mat Pilates class, a talk on longevity (Lifespan vs Healthspan), functional age tests with a review of the results, a coffee break and brunch. The price includes a mat, a voucher for a vitamin D test at 50% off and gifts; only 15 spots, registration until November 27.

items.n: Free sky lantern release at Wat Doi Ti temple
items.d: Wat Doi Ti temple in Lamphun invites everyone to the traditional sky lantern release (Khom Loi); entry and participation are free, and lanterns can be bought from local sellers to support the temple.
items.a: Wat Doi Ti (วัดดอยติ)

items.n: Contaminated aquatic animals in the Kok River
items.d: On November 23, 2026 the Department of Fisheries found contamination above the limits (including arsenic) in 10 species from the Kok River: shrimp, snails, mussels, bottom-dwelling fish. The advice is not to eat them; for fish of the middle and upper water layers, not to eat the internal organs.
A space for meetups and events from a big list of interesting places in Chiang Mai; the post gives only the name and a map link.

items.n: Hana Garden แม่ริม
items.d: A cafe in Mae Rim with homemade burgers and a view of the fields; sometimes a rabbit runs around nearby.

items.n: Blues Jam Night at Soi Dog Blues
items.d: An evening of live blues with special guests Jo & Oliver: happy hour, open mic, a house band and a blues jam that musicians can join.
items.h: November 22: 18:00–20:00 happy hour, 20:00 open mic, 20:30 house band with Jo & Oliver, 21:15 blues jam

items.n: Meet Winnie the Pooh, Tigger and Eeyore at Central Chiangmai Airport
items.d: Meet and take photos with the Disney characters Winnie the Pooh, Tigger and Eeyore in the event area on the 4th floor. Queue tickets are needed; they are handed out about 30 minutes before each session, and one pass is for up to 4 people.

Rental of cars (economy, sedans, crossovers and SUVs, minivans, pickups, premium) and scooters, daily and long-term. Free delivery and return at the airport, a hotel or any address in Chiang Mai, 24/7 support; the company says all its cars have First Class insurance.

items.n: Hom Saeng Hom Jai: a traditional Yi Peng
items.d: A Loy Krathong festival in the Lanna tradition in the Night Bazaar area: Yi Peng lantern displays, krathong-making workshops and a place to float them, Lanna candles and Phang Prathip lights, shows, souvenirs and handmade crafts, the “Little Noppamas” contest, food, and a new photo spot, “Song Wat CNX”. Parking is on the opposite side.

items.n: Where to dance salsa, bachata and kizomba in Chiang Mai
items.d: A roundup of places for Latin dancing: studios with classes, Latin parties and social dance, dancing in the park and by the pool, the Afro-Latin Festival and free Zumba. Schedules change, so check dates with the organizers.
Salsa and bachata classes for beginners and improvers, group and private lessons. Events and schedule on the danz.ly page.
The dance venue of SBK Chiang Mai: salsa, bachata, kizomba and Urban Kiz classes, workshops and special events.
A bar in One Nimman with regular Latin nights: zouk classes and social dance on Tuesdays, a bachata class and an SBK party (salsa, bachata, kizomba) on Wednesdays.
items.h: Tue — zouk; Wed — bachata class and SBK party

items.d: Sunday meetups at One Nimman: an open salsa, bachata and kizomba class, followed by social dance.
items.p: 100 ฿ for the class and party, 80 ฿ for the party only

items.d: Home to Latin Season Social Dance, evenings for Latin dance lovers.
Meetups for kizomba lovers in Huay Kaew Arboretum park. New dates and times are posted in the Kizomba Chiang Mai WhatsApp group.

items.n: Latin Pool Party at Travelodge Nimman
items.d: Dance classes and a pool party with salsa, bachata and kizomba. New dates on the Bailamos Chiangmai page.
The fifth international festival: Afro-Latin dance workshops with international teachers, salsa, bachata and kizomba, DJ parties, a pool party.
Group Zumba classes at Decathlon. Free, with registration in advance on the Decathlon page.
Listed in the roundup's Zumba section; classes Monday to Wednesday and on Saturday mornings.

items.n: Loy Krathong: where to go and how to celebrate
items.d: Options: Lamphun on Tuesday or Wednesday (a temple with wish lanterns, krathongs and sky lanterns by the river) or a loud evening by the Ping River in Chiang Mai. Paid events are expensive and aimed at tourists; book transport in advance.

items.n: Temple in Lamphun for Loy Krathong
items.d: The temple where the author suggests starting Loy Krathong in Lamphun: you can write a wish on a lantern and hang it under the temple ceiling.
A driver for a Loy Krathong trip; speaks Thai only.
A driver's contact for a Loy Krathong trip, from the author's list.
Red songthaew hire for group trips, including Loy Krathong.
A songthaew driver for group trips, including Loy Krathong.
The Rimping supermarket often has a promotion on ripe sweet bananas for smoothies and baking: a second bunch free, a hefty bunch for about 40 baht.
Italian ice cream; stamp cards have appeared — the 11th ice cream is free; people praise the mango one with pieces of dried mango and the friendly staff.

An astronomy evening by NARIT: more than 30 telescopes (Saturn's rings, the Moon, the Pleiades, Andromeda), photographing the Moon through a telescope with a phone, Planet Garden, workshops, a lecture on Saturn, music.
items.a: Chiang Mai PAO Park, Chang Phueak
items.p: free admission; a glow stick is free upon registration

items.n: Yi Peng: an evening of sky lanterns at Doze Hostel
items.d: An evening at the Doze Hostel grounds in Mae On with a sky lantern release: you can write your name or a wish on a lantern. Free entry; a transfer from Chiang Mai for 490 baht round trip (meet at 15:30 at Doze Hostel, back around 21:00), paid in cash at the hostel.
items.p: free entry; transfer 490 baht per person round trip
items.h: November 24, lantern release at 20:00, grounds open until 22:00

items.n: Traditional CMU students' climb up Doi Suthep
items.d: The traditional procession of Chiang Mai University (CMU) students to the temple on Doi Suthep; the Faculty of Fine Arts walked in traditional Lanna costumes.

items.n: Yi Peng decorations at Tha Phae Gate and the Mae Kha canal
items.d: The city is decorated with lanterns and festive decorations for Yi Peng: the Tha Phae Gate area and the Mae Kha canal (Khlong Mae Kha). A nice place for a walk and beautiful photos.

The final round of the Toyota Gazoo Racing season: Toyota One Make Race races, a drift show, GR Hot Lap, a free test drive of Toyota 4×4 off-roaders on a track with an artificial mountain, GR Kart, meet the racers, a THE TOYS concert, a food zone. Free entry.

A branch of TYREPLUS, a chain of tire centers and car services: MICHELIN and BFGoodrich tires, wheel alignment, balancing, puncture repair, brakes, battery, suspension. The author changed tires here: two DESTONE RA01 195/50 R16 for 4700 ฿, labor free; the post has this branch’s price list.
items.p: wheel alignment 300–500 ฿; balancing 150–250 ฿ per wheel; tire fitting 150–200 ฿ per wheel; puncture repair from 100 ฿; brake pads 300–400 ฿; oil change (labor) 300 ฿; Safety Check 500 ฿; nitrogen 50 ฿ per wheel

items.d: A branch of TYREPLUS, a chain of tire centers and car services: MICHELIN and BFGoodrich tires, wheel alignment, balancing, puncture repair, brakes, battery, suspension.
items.a: Chang Phueak, by Chang Phueak market

items.d: A branch of TYREPLUS, a chain of tire centers and car services: MICHELIN and BFGoodrich tires, wheel alignment, balancing, puncture repair, brakes, battery, suspension.

items.a: Chiang Mai–Lampang Road, opposite Lanna Hospital

items.n: TYREPLUS: branches in Chiang Mai and approximate prices
items.d: A list of TYREPLUS branches in and around Chiang Mai and an approximate price list of the Hang Dong branch: wheel alignment, balancing, tire fitting, puncture repair, brakes, oil change. Example: a DESTONE RA01 195/50 R16 tire costs 2350 ฿.
A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: An intimate studio in a traditional wooden house. Classes: Vinyasa, Yin Yoga, Sound Healing.
items.a: Old City, Phra Pok Klao Road, Lane 4/1

items.d: A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: Classes for different levels. Styles: Hatha, Vinyasa, Yin, Power Yoga, meditation.
A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: Classes: Hatha Yoga, Yin Therapy, flexibility and recovery sessions.
A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: Group classes and workshops. Classes: Hatha, Vinyasa, Yin, Advanced Asana, Sound Healing.
A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: They teach handstands too.
A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: A studio on the second floor of a building. Group yoga classes.

A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: A yoga hall on the second floor. You can practice asanas and work on balance and handstands with a teacher. There has been a Russian teacher too.
A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: Hatha, Yin Yoga, Yoga Flow classes. Evening yoga on the roof with a view of the temples.
items.a: Old City, 248/14 Manee Nopparat Road, second floor

items.d: A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: A separate yoga hall in the grounds of Suan Chang Puak, surrounded by greenery.
items.a: Old City, Muen Dam Phra Khot Road, Chang Phueak

items.d: A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: Classes: Ashtanga, Hatha Vinyasa, Yin, Restorative, Mobility Flow, Healthy Spine, Deep Stretching.

A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: A bright studio with big windows and a view of the mountains. Classes: Vinyasa Flow, Hatha Flow, Gentle Flow, Stretching, Chair Yoga, Sound Bath.
items.a: Nimman, Sai Nam Phueng Alley, Nimman

items.d: A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: Styles: Hatha, Yin, Restorative, Power Yoga, Ashtanga Vinyasa, Pranayama and Meditation.
A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: Classes focused on movement, breathing and body work.
A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: Classes: Vinyasa, Ashtanga, Aerial Yoga, Chair Yoga and Sound Healing.
items.a: Nimman, PT Residence, Siri Mangkalajarn Road

items.d: A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: A minimalist studio. Classes: Hatha Flow, Vinyasa Mobility, Yin Yoga, Sound Healing.
A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: A space for yoga, movement and body practices. There are also dance classes and contact improvisation.
items.a: Mali Place, third floor, Mae Hia

items.d: A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: A yoga space with a beautiful hall and a calm atmosphere. Classes: Hatha, Yin, Stretching, Meditation, Breathwork and Sound Healing.
A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: A space for yoga and wellness practices.
A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: A space for yoga classes.
A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: A studio with different yoga styles, including Aerial Yoga.
A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: Yoga classes for different levels.
A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: Different teachers, a beautiful new hall.

items.n: Baan Rai Nai Fun Organic Garden
items.d: A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: They hold yoga classes, yoga events and tai chi here.

A place for yoga from a roundup of “25 places in Chiang Mai”: The studio of teacher Kru Dutchi. Practice for those who want to work on difficult asanas, arm balances, backbends and inversions. Also Vinyasa and Ashtanga Fusion.
A yoga school in Kad Farang: classes 5–6 times a week at 9 am; the author has been coming here for two years.

items.n: Yoga in Chiang Mai: 25 places to practice
items.d: A roundup of 25 places for yoga in Chiang Mai by area (Old City, Nimman and Suthep, Mae Hia, Hang Dong, Chang Phueak): from vinyasa and ashtanga to hatha, yin yoga, stretching and meditation; plus regular free yoga in the park.

items.n: Free yoga in the park in the square
items.d: Regular free yoga classes in the park in the square (the Old City).
A tire shop recommended by a subscriber: a perfectionist who keeps everything in perfect order.
A Christmas market and winter festival at One Nimman styled as Santa’s factory: festive decorations, handmade gifts by local makers, food and treats, marshmallows toasted over the fire.

items.n: The WellNest Sessions II — Mountains & Magic
items.d: A music day at WellNest in the mountains: DJs (Nantawan DJ, Gypsy Rituals, PhoeBeats and others, live saxophone), a pool, saunas and ice baths, lounge areas, food and drinks including Markie Beer. No time limit on staying; a big parking lot.
A festival of light in Doi Saket: light installations, music and cultural performances; the Nimman Street Orchestra will play (the exact time is not published).
An evening of jazz and Christmas spirit at Your Father CNX; tables are booked through the venue’s Facebook page.

A Christmas get-together by Velvet Wellness Club: Pilates, a gingerbread house workshop, treats, champagne and wine (soft drinks too), a photographer, gifts for participants. Dress code: pink, red and white. 5% off for a repost.
items.a: The Consul’s Garden / Le Coq d’Or Restaurant

items.n: The Spectacular Lanna Light, Sound & Multimedia Show
items.d: An evening show at Tha Phae Gate with fire, light effects, music and traditional Lanna art, for the Yi Peng festival.
A bar in Nimman from a roundup of 25 bars and nightlife spots in the area, for lovers of cocktails, music, dancing and an evening atmosphere.

A release of three lanterns per person, traditional performances, music, fireworks, a temple visit and dinner; a transfer from Chiang Mai and back.

items.p: free entry and a welcome drink

items.n: Chiang Mai: a big list of interesting places
items.d: A big roundup of Chiang Mai places with map links: cafes, bakeries, rooftop and wine bars, galleries, event spaces, malls, weekend markets, unusual things to do and places in Chiang Dao.

A cozy cafe with a European interior and vintage touches, already decorated for Christmas: coffee, caffeine-free drinks, matcha, pastries and desserts. Drinks from 30 ฿; 10% off a drink with the Basque cheesecake.
items.p: drinks from 30 ฿; 10% off a drink ordered with the Basque Burnt Cheesecake

items.n: Loy Krathong x Kad Mua at Alt_PingRiver
items.d: A festive Lanna evening by the Ping River: Kad Mua, a traditional northern market with local food and sweets, a krathong making workshop, games. Lanna-style dress is welcome; those who buy a ticket by November 21 enter a gift draw.
items.p: 350 ฿ per person, snacks and krathong materials included

items.n: Lanna Lanterns at Wat Lok Moli
items.d: Festive lanterns in the grounds of the old temple Wat Lok Moli. Free entry.

items.n: Tam Phaang Prateep — Lighting the Sky
items.d: A festival of lights at Wat Chedi Luang. Procession on November 23: gathering at 17:00 on Ratchadamnoen Road outside Tha Phae Gate, arrival at the temple around 18:00.

items.n: Yi Peng Festival: Lanna Lantern Workshop
items.d: Workshops on making traditional Lanna lanterns, a festive procession and a kids’ market at Jing Jai Market.

items.n: Krathong Making and Thai Dance Class
items.d: Krathong making and a traditional Thai dance lesson at The Connect Studio. Tickets and details in the CNX Local listings.
A festive pool party at Sabai Sabai Retreat on Yi Peng day, with a transfer: minibuses leave from 14:00.
Thousands of sky lanterns released, cultural shows and music at CM Event CNX. The ticket includes two lanterns, a krathong and an oil lamp.
A sky lantern festival at I Love Banthi.
A ceramics festival at Jing Jai Market: pieces by local makers and original designs. Free entry.
A fair with the feel of a cozy country market at Jing Jai Market.
A garden fair at Boonthavorn Private Garden.
A wintry festive atmosphere and Christmas decorations at Central Chiang Mai Airport.
An agriculture and innovation exhibition at Chiang Mai Hall, Central Chiang Mai Airport.
items.a: Chiang Mai Hall, Central Chiang Mai Airport

items.d: A Christmas wreath making workshop at La Luna Gallery.

items.n: Weekend Music at Soi Dog Blues Bar
items.d: Blues, jazz and live jam sessions at Soi Dog Blues Bar on the weekend.
A meetup for skateboarding and creative people at Chiang Mai Railway Station.
A festival of creativity, movement and self-expression at the out-of-town eco resort Mala Dhara Eco Resort.
A big 20+ festival at Royal Train Garden Resort in Hang Dong.
items.a: Royal Train Garden Resort, Hang Dong

items.d: A sunset Barre workout on the roof of MAI The Sky Bar at Meliá Chiang Mai by Babel, followed by a cocktail party. The ticket includes a Babel Styles outfit, the workout and 500 ฿ for drinks; from 16:00 a separate session for BABEL club members.
items.a: MAI The Sky Bar, Meliá Chiang Mai
items.p: Single Pass 1 880 ฿; Duo Pass 1 680 ฿ per person

items.d: A new countryside boutique resort in rural Mae Rim, soft opening on November 22: 3 separate lodges and a homestay, a saltwater mineral pool, a hot-water jacuzzi, free breakfast. Launch prices for the first guests; booking by phone.

The annual charity fair in a garden: 400+ stalls, food, live music, kids' entertainment, the Tombola raffle (60 baht) and auctions. The money goes to the Baan Unrak children's home and to air purifiers for residents. Songthaews run from Central Airport Plaza for 50 baht, and parking is limited. The music schedule is in a separate post.
items.p: lottery 60 baht; songthaew 50 baht one way

items.d: A new community mall on the new Chiang Mai–San Kamphaeng road, about 300 m from the San Klang intersection (landmark: Khao Cafe): small shops, cafes and services for local families, including restaurants, beauty and health, education and kids' activities. The opening is planned for February 2027.
items.a: San Kamphaeng, Chiang Mai–San Kamphaeng road

items.n: PETALS & POISE: a pilates day at Villa Aton Organic Farm
items.d: A joint event by Pax Pilates Club and PowerHaus Pilates at the countryside Villa Aton Organic Farm: morning Mat Pilates in the open air and a talk on wellness with Ann Thongprasom, brunch, afternoon tea with a workshop on making a mini lemon cake by Le Deli, a sunset dinner with a view of the mountains and a party with a DJ. Gifts from the club and partners and a prize draw; the dress code is white sportswear. Register through Pax Pilates Club and pay by bank transfer; places are limited.

Ahead of Loy Krathong, at Nic’s Restaurant & Playground you can make a colorful Lanna-style lantern yourself: all the materials are ready, and it suits adults and kids alike. You can combine it with lunch or dinner while the kids play on the playground.

items.n: PI BA PRA KONG RUE SI at KEEPING TONE LIVEHOUSE
items.d: A musician from Lamphun: acoustic guitar, reggae rhythms, humor and songs in the northern Thai dialect. After the concert there's an open jam, and you can bring your own instruments.

Three days of jazz, hip-hop, blues, traditional music, ethnic dances and the experimental scene from North Gate Jazz Co-Op. The lineup includes Lanard with Khorn Dance, Chiang Mai Big Band, Triple Edge FM, North Gate Brass, Articuno Lanna, a Burmese puppet dance, DJ Samche and others. All profits go to North Gate Rajchawong, a music and art school and community center for children from ethnic communities and vulnerable families.
A fully immersive cinema under a dome: a flight into the crater of a volcano, a trip back to the time of the dinosaurs and the Meadow Racers. Shows in Thai and English, for ages 5 and up.

items.n: Sale of a textile and folk art collection
items.d: A private collection put together over 35 years: about 100 unique items from all over the world, including small rugs and cushions, wall hangings, embroidery, wool and cotton fabrics, items for altars, Thai yantra cloths and other ethnic pieces.

items.n: Organic Nights with DJ SpaceDeer at Eudemonia Elements
items.d: Yoga and a Sound Journey, tai chi with master Ling Xin, a cacao ceremony and Ecstatic Dance with DJ SpaceDeer (founder of Arillas Soundgarden on Corfu), ending with a gathering around the bonfire. The price includes all the wellness areas: sauna, herbal steam room, hot tub, ice baths, magnesium bath and saltwater pools.
items.a: Eudemonia Elements, Nong Kwai, Hang Dong
items.h: 16:30 yoga, 17:30 tai chi, 19:00 cacao ceremony, 19:30 ecstatic dance

items.d: A little cafe in the mountains on the road up to Doi Suthep, near Wat Pha Lat: a panorama of Chiang Mai, mountains on the horizon and lots of greenery.
items.a: Suthep, the road up Doi Suthep, by Wat Pha Lat
items.p: espresso 65 baht, latte 75, matcha 130, carrot cake 90

items.n: A spot with a mountain view in Chiang Dao
items.d: Her photo: a mountain ridge in evening light, a wooden hut on a green field and daisies; a spot in the Chiang Dao area, with a map link.

A shop near Kham Thiang market with a big choice of children's costumes: Thai national outfits (sabai, chong kraben), Nang Noppamas costumes for Loy Krathong, costumes for jobs, astronauts and scientists; everyday kids' clothes too. You can try things on there, with parking in front.
items.a: by Lotus's Kham Thiang, Kham Thiang market

items.d: A big open-air electronic music party in the Deep Green garden near the Old City, with a Miki Vection sound system. Lineup: SGAMO (headliner), Koboro, DJ Casper, Butter and Rebel Rhythm; then the official afterparty at RED CNX until morning.
items.a: Deep Green @ Deejai Garden, Old City
items.p: Early Bird 200 baht, presale 400, at the door 500 (with a drink), with the afterparty at RED CNX 800

items.n: Zumba Dance Party for Loy Krathong
items.d: A free hour-long open-air Zumba party by Anytime Fitness Kad Farang Mae Rim, in front of the Rimping supermarket; come in a Thai outfit or comfortable festive clothes. No membership needed, but register in advance.
A yoga studio on Manee Nopparat Rd: daily yoga classes from October 1, free meditation on weekends, evening classes on the roof in good weather.
Loy Krathong, the full moon festival: krathongs on the Ping River, the riverside and venues around town. From the Chiang Mai events calendar for November 21–29, 2026.

items.n: Offering light in the Lanna tradition
items.d: Why phang prathip (ผางประทีป) oil lamps and lanterns are lit on Yi Peng: reverence for the Three Jewels, the legend of the Mother White Crow, light for the door, the well, the hearth and other parts of the house, and the belief in merit (anisong).
The opening of an annual exhibition of works on 3-inch Post-it notes at Great Shot Bar: more than 80 artists and over a thousand works at 300 baht each, portraits on the spot and the bar's cocktails.
Everything is good: the service, the courtyard, the food; a pleasant place to spend time. Dogs are welcome.
A place in Chiang Dao that hosts “secular” vipassana: the food is delicious, it costs serious money, you can ask questions and get detailed answers, and the guides are highly qualified.

Ahead of Loy Krathong, guided by Fon, participants make their own krathong from natural materials, flowers and candles; the price includes a 50-baht voucher for the shop, only 15 places. Full Stop in Nimman, opposite Warm Up Café, with parking.

items.s: Loy Krathong with a lantern release
items.d: November 24 and 25 at Horizon Village & Resort and Tweechol Botanical Garden: a walk around the garden, workshops (krathong, Luk Chup, Lanna Tung lanterns), food and drinks, and a mass release of sky lanterns at 20:00. A ticket includes 2 lanterns and a krathong; no transfer, tickets are non-refundable.
items.a: Horizon Village & Resort / Tweechol Botanical Garden, Doi Saket
items.p: with workshops: 3 599 baht (from 11), 1 800 baht (4–10); without them: 2 999 and 1 500 baht; under 4 free

items.n: CMU freshmen welcome: the climb up Doi Suthep
items.d: The traditional climb up Doi Suthep by Chiang Mai University freshmen. From the Chiang Mai events calendar for November 21–29, 2026.
The Payap University graduation ceremony at the Mae Khao campus. From the Chiang Mai events calendar for November 21–29, 2026.
A run around Montfort school. From the Chiang Mai events calendar for November 21–29, 2026.
A half marathon at Railway Park (สวนรถไฟ). From the Chiang Mai events calendar for November 21–29, 2026.
A traditional procession with clay lamps along Ratchadamnoen Road to Wat Chedi Luang. From the Chiang Mai events calendar for November 21–29, 2026.
items.a: Old City, Ratchadamnoen, Wat Chedi Luang

items.d: The big krathong parade from the Tha Phae Gate area toward the city hall. From the Chiang Mai events calendar for November 21–29, 2026.
A big music festival on November 28–29 at Royal Train Garden Resort. From the Chiang Mai events calendar for November 21–29, 2026.
items.a: Royal Train Garden Resort, Hang Dong

items.d: A future branch of the Japanese bookstore chain in the Lannatique project, on the site of the former Lanna Garden: about 1 500–2 000 m² on four floors, books and magazines, art and design, stationery, places to relax. Opening expected in 2028.
A new place in the Old City a few steps from the moat: mini golf with unusual courses and obstacles, pétanque, a cafe with music. A day ticket gives unlimited play, and you can leave and come back.

A new riverside cafe-restaurant on the Ping, on the grounds of Ping Pura Riverside Resort & Spa, in a glass pavilion among the greenery: breakfasts, brunch, lunch and dinner, and in the evening drinks and live music by the river. Opening in November 2026.
A beautiful hotel on the bank of the Ping with elegant colonial architecture and the feel of a getaway out of town; the RIO Grande cafe is opening on its grounds.

items.n: Krathong workshop at Chiang Mai City Craft Space
items.d: Making a krathong for Loy Krathong on November 19, 20, 24 and 25, all materials included; sign up through the form.
Making a krathong from natural materials; better to book a place with the organizers in advance.

items.n: A party under the stars at BAYA Chiang Mai
items.d: A party for the BAYA community to celebrate the opening of a new area: music, socializing under the open sky, the sauna and ice baths. No separate ticket, but you need the 400-baht day pass; the kitchen is open until 18:00.

items.n: Chaokoh: a temporary stand in front of MAYA
items.d: A temporary stand in front of MAYA: you can take photos for free and buy Chaokoh vegan coconut ice cream in a cone or a cup.
items.p: 30 baht in a cone, 40 baht in a cup

items.d: A roundup of cafes, farms and nature spots north of Chiang Mai, in the Mae Jo and San Sai area: from a cafe-farm and a dog park to Nong Sam Kha park and Huai Jo Reservoir; you can combine them into a full-day route.
A cafe and farm by the water, surrounded by greenery; you can also stay there as a farmstay.
A coffee shop with pastries in the Mae Jo area, a nice coffee stop.
A big farm with spacious green grounds.
A cafe with a big dog park; you can come with your pets.
An atmospheric cafe among the trees, with wooden tables and a relaxed, camping-style vibe.
One more interesting spot in the Mae Jo area, from a roundup of cafes and interesting spaces.
A cozy place to relax near Mae Jo, from a roundup of cafes and interesting spaces.
A coffee shop with coffee and desserts in the Mae Jo area.
A park with a lake and greenery, a place to relax in nature.
A reservoir among green hills: walks, bike rides and relaxing by the water.

An annual exhibition and festival of traditional crafts, contemporary art and sustainable living: textiles, ceramics, natural dyeing, more than 30 workshops, art installations in nature, live music; the Bamboo Family Market runs all four days.
items.a: Sanggadee Space, Ton Pao, San Kamphaeng
items.p: free entry; workshops may be paid separately

items.d: An astronomy park 20–25 minutes from the center: free telescope viewing on Saturdays (Jupiter, the Moon), a fulldome show in the planetarium; a screening in English on Friday at 11:00.
items.p: telescopes free; planetarium: adults — 50 baht, children / students — 30 baht
items.h: Telescopes: every Saturday 18:00 – 22:00; planetarium Tue–Sun 11:00, 14:00, 17:00 (Saturdays only)

items.n: Changphuak Gate Driving School Chiang Mai
items.d: A driving school where instructor Tok explains calmly, in good English and in small portions, and takes you onto a busy road on the very first day; students without English get a translator in the car, and the tests are in Russian.
items.p: 10 driving lessons: 4 400 baht (without the tests and exam)

items.d: A spot for stargazing far from the city's light pollution, from the Amazing Dark Sky in Thailand list (TAT Chiang Mai and NARIT).

A tram-style electric bus on route No. 5 around the Old City from Wat Phra Singh: 13.8 km, 14 stops (Warorot, Tha Phae, Wat Chedi Luang and more), about 40 minutes a loop. After a test run, it starts on November 18, 2026.
items.p: no more than 30 baht for the whole route

items.d: An aesthetic medicine clinic recommended in expat communities, including for Botox.
items.a: T Square, 3rd floor, 86 Sridonchai Road, Chang Khlan

items.d: A clinic recommended in expat communities: Botox, fillers, mesotherapy, laser and other aesthetic procedures.

items.n: Mueang Sat Luang (ชุมชนเมืองสาตรหลวง)
items.d: One of the biggest centers in the North for making khom Lanna lanterns; the craft grew after the lanterns made for the 1995 Southeast Asian Games. Best to go to Wat Mueang Sat Luang and walk along Mueang Sat street.

items.n: ยายนอมโคมล้านนา
items.d: A shop of traditional northern khom Lanna lanterns in the Mueang Sat Luang community (Nong Hoi), one of the biggest centers of this craft.

items.n: โคมล้านนาแม่อุ้ย
items.d: A khom Lanna lantern shop (Mae Oui) in the Mueang Sat Luang community, Nong Hoi; it sells lanterns all year round, not just before Yi Peng.

items.n: นวินโคมล้านนา
items.d: A shop of traditional northern khom Lanna lanterns in the Mueang Sat Luang community (Nong Hoi), one of the biggest centers of this craft.

A small cafe south of the Old City: sourdough pizza and focaccia, their own vegan cheeses, homemade pesto, their own kombucha (people especially praise the passion fruit one) and even their own cola; plant-based, vegetarian and regular dishes.

items.n: Kids' krathong-making workshop at Arbor Club
items.d: Before Loy Krathong, kids make their own krathongs and learn about the tradition; free, only 20 places, advance registration needed (QR code on the poster or by DM).

items.s: club with a pool and a gym
items.d: A wellness club in Hang Dong with a pool and a gym, which hosts free events for kids and adults.

items.n: Sound Bath Experience at Arbor Club
items.d: A morning sound bath with crystal singing bowls by the EARTH SOUL HEALING team, then snacks, a tour of the club and a light brunch; free, 40 places, registration via the link in the @arborclub.cnx profile.

items.n: Big jazz night at The Mellowship
items.d: Chiang Mai Big Band is back: brass, swing, bebop and improvisation, then modern jazz from Dandylion and The Mellowship Quartet; free entry. The club is open Tuesday to Sunday from 17:00 to midnight.
items.h: 20:00 Chiang Mai Big Band, 21:15 Dandylion, 22:15 The Mellowship Quartet

items.n: Stargazing spots in Chiang Mai province
items.d: A list from the Amazing Dark Sky in Thailand project by TAT Chiang Mai and NARIT: places far from the city's light pollution in Chiang Dao and other parts of the province, including hotels, campsites, an astronomy park, nature areas and communities that look after keeping the sky dark.
A spot for stargazing far from the city's light pollution, from the Amazing Dark Sky in Thailand list (TAT Chiang Mai and NARIT).

items.n: Ton Khao Hom Ban Om Doi
items.d: A spot for stargazing far from the city's light pollution, from the Amazing Dark Sky in Thailand list (TAT Chiang Mai and NARIT).

The railway park, where a local instructor leads free aerobics to music for everyone every evening from 18 to 20; on Sundays around 18:00 a saxophone from the Half.cnx coffee shop can be heard across the park.
A very beautiful restaurant with a river view and bamboo architecture; refined dishes, not greasy and beautifully presented. Better book ahead: it is often fully booked, especially now.

items.s: coffee shop by the park, live music
items.d: A small stylish cafe overlooking Railway Park; about every Sunday at 18:00 a live saxophone plays on the lawn in front of the cafe.

items.n: Thot Kathin, the festival of offering robes to monks
items.d: In 2026 the Kathin season runs from October 27 to November 24: after Vassa, temples offer monks new robes and donations, often with processions, music, dances and fairs.

items.n: Kathin at Wat Mae Tung Ting
items.d: Kathin ceremony, where monks are offered new robes and donations, at Wat Mae Tung Ting in Samoeng.
Kathin ceremony, where monks are offered new robes and donations, at Wat Doi Sappanyu in Mae Wang.
Kathin ceremony, where monks are offered new robes and donations, at Wat Chai Mongkol in Chiang Dao.

items.n: Movie night at Jugnu Studio: Ananda Bhairavi
items.d: A screening of the South Indian musical film Ananda Bhairavi, about a master of Kuchipudi dance who teaches a girl in defiance of caste bans; in Kannada with English subtitles.

Thailand's first Geminids meteor shower watching marathon: 30 competitors see who can watch the sky the longest, with a prize fund of over 100,000 baht; a festival with MUANSART MARKET, workshops and astronomy with NARIT.
items.p: free for spectators; competitors need a ticket via Ticketmelon

items.d: A very authentic coffee shop with a sweetest owner who helps you choose coffee individually; a high rating, very invigorating coffee.
Wholesale perfume: long-lasting scents without overpaying for marketing; a set of reed diffusers for 85 baht. Closed on Sundays.
A handyman the author has written about before: when expats in a group were looking for someone to come and wash a ceiling chandelier, he offered to do it.
A cafe with a viewpoint near Mon Jam.

items.n: Annual park passes for kids with student cards
items.d: The director of Pathfinders makes student cards for the kids, which let you buy annual passes to the park; Royal Park Rajapruek has annual passes too, about 800.
A French restaurant with tons of rave reviews, a great place for dinner.
A market of vintage, music and old cameras: vinyl records, cassettes, musical instruments, a separate Camera Market with film and vintage cameras, vintage goods and live music.
items.a: LAN DIN Project, 89/7 Moo 5, Ram Poeng Road, Suthep

items.d: A semi-rustic cafe where you can watch the planes, with cacti and a fish pond; budget-friendly: Thai food, sandwiches, breakfasts, pizza, desserts, Myanmar coffee with coconut. The cashier speaks English.

An unusual place on the grounds of an old barn in the style of a Japanese village: a cafe, floor coworking, yoga and wellness, boutiques of Japanese and handmade clothing, pastry shops, Japanese and Thai restaurants; dogs are allowed.
A viewpoint with panoramic views of the mountains and valleys.
A festival of live music and vinyl culture at the new Kad Dhara Dhevi venue; the lineup includes Flure, Srirajah Rockers, Yellow Fang, Khun Narin and others. Tickets via Ticketmelon.

The first international festival, December 10–13: film music (10.12, 137 Pillars House), a chamber evening (11.12, Shangri-La), a makers’ fair and a gala concert (12.12, InterContinental The Mae Ping), a free concert on 13.12 (by Wat Chedi Luang, according to ConnectThai).
items.a: 137 Pillars House, Shangri-La, InterContinental The Mae Ping, Wat Chedi Luang
items.p: 3 000 baht standard, 3 500 Premium, 1 000 student; December 12 gala 3 000 (cocktails) or 4 000 baht (dinner); December 13 free

items.d: A fair of local makers, craftspeople and designers as part of MuseArt Chiang Mai Festival: handmade goods, design, regional products. Free entry.
items.a: InterContinental Chiang Mai The Mae Ping

items.d: The English version of the channel for foreign friends; there is a link to read the channel without Telegram.

items.n: Tam Phang Patit Song Fah Haksa Muang
items.d: The 15th festival of Lanna traditions, November 20–23: clay lamps, Lanna lanterns, sword dances. On November 23, a procession from Tha Phae Gate and lamps lit at the four gates, with a temple ceremony at 18:00.
items.h: November 23: gathering 17:00 on Ratchadamnoen Road, procession 17:30, temple ceremony 18:00

items.d: The main city festival, November 23–25: lantern contests, Little Yi Peng, the choice of the festival’s prince and princess and performances in Ton Lam Yai park; lanterns and festive temple decorations at Wat Lok Moli all November.
items.a: Ton Lam Yai Market Public Park, Wat Lok Moli

items.d: A parade of large decorative krathongs on November 25: 26 floats compete for the royal trophy, with costumes, music and light displays.
items.a: from Tha Phae Gate to the Municipality building

items.n: Sky lanterns at Yi Peng: where and when they are allowed
items.d: Launching sky lanterns (Khom Loi) is restricted because of flights: it is banned in Mueang Chiang Mai and Hang Dong; at approved sites in 2026 it is allowed on November 24 and 25 from 19:00 to 01:00.
A cozy wooden house among the greenery: coffee, tea and fresh pastries, a good stop on the way to the mountains.
t: on the way to the mountains

items.d: A coffee shop among rice fields with wooden pavilions, a terrace and its own coffee roasting.
Slow coffee under an old wooden house.
A coffee shop and space for the running community; there is a shop with running clothes and accessories.
Breakfasts, fresh bread and pastries.
A cafe and bar on the top floor with a view of the city and the mountains, especially nice closer to the evening.
A small tea house with Japanese matcha among the trees.
A simple local place with traditional northern Thai food.
Northern Thai food, authentic flavors and dishes that are easy to share.
An intimate cocktail bar with Japanese touches in the interior.
A wine bar on Tha Phae Road for a slow evening with wine and snacks.
A small boutique hotel with minimalist design and a calm atmosphere.
A cycling gear shop and a meeting place for the local cycling community.
Specialist clothing and gear for cyclists.

items.n: Wat Pha Lad and Monk’s Trail
items.d: An atmospheric forest temple with streams, waterfalls and old buildings; you can walk there along a forest trail.
A national park with forests, waterfalls, temples and mountain villages.
A mountain area with panoramic views, gardens, cafes and places to relax.

items.n: Arsenic in the rivers of Northern Thailand
items.d: Arsenic pollution of the Kok, Sai and Ruak rivers: what it means for Chiang Mai (the city takes its water mainly from the Ping River), where to see PCD monitoring data, how to cook rice and choose food.
An antiques and rug shop: you can try a rug at home first, painted furniture, lots of decor; there is a cafe with a beautiful design for photos.
A national park included in the Green Destinations Top 100 Stories 2026 list; in the cool season, a sea of mist, mountain air and a starry sky.
items.p: foreigners: adults 300 ฿, children 150 ฿; Thai citizens 60/30 ฿; vehicle fee not included

items.n: Christmas Fair 2026 at Lanna International School
items.d: A Christmas fair at the school: crafts, food, entertainment, performances by students and by The Moat Rats, a band with one of the school’s teachers. Open to the general public from 15:00.
items.h: Friday, December 11, 13:30–19:00; open to the general public from 15:00

items.d: A special Thanksgiving menu at Favola, the Italian restaurant of Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel. Prepayment is required, early-booking seats are limited, kids under 6 eat free, no outside drinks.
items.a: Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel, Favola Chiang Mai
items.p: 1 650 ฿ early booking, 1 884 ฿ regular price, per person; including a 10% service charge and 7% tax

items.n: Christmas dinner at Gaj Kitchen and Bar
items.d: A holiday Christmas buffet at Gaj Kitchen and Bar in Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel. Prepayment is required, early-booking seats are limited, kids under 6 eat free, no outside drinks.
items.a: Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel, Gaj Kitchen and Bar
items.p: adults 2 800 ฿ (early booking), 3 200 ฿ (regular price); kids 7–12 1 600 ฿; including a 10% service charge and 7% tax

items.d: A special Italian Christmas menu at Favola restaurant in Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel. Prepayment is required, early-booking seats are limited, kids under 6 eat free, no outside drinks.
items.a: Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel, Favola Chiang Mai
items.p: 1 750 ฿ early booking, 1 990 ฿ regular price, per person; including a 10% service charge and 7% tax

items.d: A holiday Christmas buffet brunch at Favola restaurant in Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel. Prepayment is required, early-booking seats are limited, kids under 6 eat free, no outside drinks.
items.a: Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel, Favola Chiang Mai
items.p: adults 3 500 ฿ (early booking), 3 888 ฿ (regular price); kids 7–12 1 944 ฿; including a 10% service charge and 7% tax

items.n: New Year's Eve dinner at Gaj Kitchen and Bar
items.d: A New Year's Eve holiday buffet at Gaj Kitchen and Bar in Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel; includes the Countdown Party at The Plaii Eatery Cafe & Bar. Prepayment is required, early-booking seats are limited, kids under 6 eat free, no outside drinks.
items.a: Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel, Gaj Kitchen and Bar
items.p: adults 2 999 ฿ (early booking), 3 500 ฿ (regular price); kids 7–12 1 750 ฿; including a 10% service charge and 7% tax

items.n: New Year's Eve dinner at Favola
items.d: A special Italian New Year's Eve menu at Favola restaurant in Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel; includes the Countdown Party at The Plaii Eatery Cafe & Bar. Prepayment is required, early-booking seats are limited, kids under 6 eat free, no outside drinks.
items.a: Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel, Favola Chiang Mai
items.p: 2 950 ฿ early booking, 3 200 ฿ regular price, per person; including a 10% service charge and 7% tax

items.n: MIRA Thai Cooking and Craft Studio
items.d: Workshops for kids and adults: Thai and Japanese cooking, painting on canvas, bamboo weaving, fan painting and Thai umbrella painting. Suits families, groups of friends and people coming on their own.

items.n: Music in the Garden: Winter Season
items.d: Open-air music evenings at Kad Dhara Dhevi: live music, a market of local makers' handmade goods, a stroll among Lanna-style architecture.

Spanish tapas with Japanese ingredients and techniques: Pimientos de Padrón, charcoal mushrooms, seafood paella, filet mignon. A dark, intimate atmosphere for dinner with wine; at the time of the post, a soft opening.

A 24-seat micro cinema showing arthouse, documentary and classic films in the original language with subtitles, 4K and Dolby 7.1 sound; a Documentary Club partner. After a film, viewers often stay to discuss it.
items.p: regular ticket 140 baht; combos with popcorn and drinks available
items.h: daily, according to the screening schedule

items.d: A cafe at the Mecani cinema with coffee and homemade pastries; the names of some drinks are inspired by romantic films.

items.n: Pha Nok Kok — Doi Pha Klong — Si Sangwan Waterfall hiking route
items.d: A 16.5 km one-way mountain trek through Doi Suthep–Pui National Park: from Ban Pha Nok Kok via Doi Pha Klong (max. 1510 m) and Si Sangwan Waterfall to the forest temple Wat Pa Thammachat, with a descent of about 1080 m. Good fitness and transport at the start and finish are needed.
Si Sangwan Waterfall on the mountain trekking route from Pha Nok Kok to Wat Pa Thammachat in Doi Suthep–Pui National Park.
A forest temple where the mountain trekking route from Ban Pha Nok Kok via Si Sangwan Waterfall ends (elevation about 430 m).

A northern agricultural fair: more than 100 participants from Chiang Mai, Lamphun, Lampang and Mae Hong Son — farm produce, local food, clothing, handmade items, herbs and cosmetics; an exhibition of agricultural innovations, concerts from 19:00, prize draws.
items.a: Chiang Mai Hall, Central Chiangmai Airport

items.n: Saturday night: Prawn Supreme and Baan Tuek Super Boogie
items.d: A Saturday concert at The Mellowship: Prawn Supreme (funk jazz) and Baan Tuek Super Boogie (acid jazz, funk, disco).
items.h: 20:30–21:30 Prawn Supreme; 22:00–23:00 Baan Tuek Super Boogie

items.d: A place at the link that sells big tomatoes; it also has hummus pesto. The post does not give its name.
A small guesthouse complex with fairytale hobbit-style cottages among tropical greenery: garden paths, natural materials, cozy interiors.
A cafe with a fairytale interior in the style of the Brothers Grimm and Harry Potter; you can work here.
An intimate cultural evening: a Loy Krathong ceremony, a sky lantern release, traditional music, workshops and dinner. The ticket includes lanterns, a krathong and a return transfer.

items.n: Chiang Mai Loy Krathong — Miracle Land
items.d: An evening with floating krathongs, sky lanterns, dinner and a cultural program; the price and contents of the packages are best checked when booking.
A festival with a Buddhist ceremony, meditation, traditional performances and a lantern release; ticket and transfer options vary, so check the price for the date and package.
items.a: San Sai, Mae Jo, Lanna Dhutanka

items.d: The poster announces more than 10,000 lanterns, a Thai buffet, cultural performances and a transfer; ticket prices are not confirmed, so check the conditions with the organizers.
A release of two lanterns, a buffet dinner, performances and cultural activities; a round-trip transfer is included.
items.p: 699 ฿ for Thai citizens; 2 999–5 800 ฿ for foreigners

items.d: Releasing sky lanterns on your own in the city and in prohibited zones is not allowed; there are special permitted venues for it, for example the commercial Yi Peng festivals on November 24–25.

An organization rescues cats and kittens and finds them families; you can adopt a pet or become a temporary foster carer — a litter box, toys and a bed are provided if needed. Contact through the website or Facebook.

A guest shift by Taiwanese bartender Jaffee Hsu (bar Commons) together with the Taipei bar UNCOMMON: cocktails with the Japanese Toki, Roku and Haku and a signature mix with Singha Soda; the opening comes with burgers from Smash Daddy’s.

items.n: Yi Peng & Loy Krathong 2026 — Ton Lam Yai
items.d: The main venue of the city’s Yi Peng has moved to the park by the Ton Lam Yai flower market on the Ping River: lantern contests, the opening on November 23, the Grand Krathong Parade on November 25 from Tha Phae Gate; an installation at Tha Phae Gate on November 23–25.
items.a: Ton Lam Yai Market Public Park, Ping River
items.h: 23 November: 16:00 Khom Hang Yai lantern contest, 18:00 opening, 20:00 children’s contest; 24 November: 08:00–11:00 Sapao Lanna contest, 19:00 Miss & Mister Yi Peng; 25 November: Grand Krathong Parade

items.d: A cafe in Mae Rim with roses, pines and gazebos by a stream for reading, a beautiful design and well-trained staff.
Homemade Kazakh and Central Asian dishes made to order, with pre-orders accepted: chebureki, manty, pelmeni, pirozhki, plov, Olivier salad, borscht.
items.p: pelmeni 159–199 THB; beshbarmak 249 THB; pigodi 2 pcs 139 THB; manti 8 pcs 249 THB; baursaki 5 pcs 30 THB; pirozhki 20 THB

items.d: A saxophonist’s performance on Sunday at 18:00 in the railway park.
A NARIT astronomy evening for the Geminid meteor shower (up to 150 meteors per hour): more than 50 telescopes, workshops, astrophotography, live music, massage, a local food market. Free entry.
A Christmas village by the Tha Phae Gate of the Old City, December 1–25.
A festive Christmas market at One Nimman, December 4–25.
A large Christmas area with festive decorations at Central Festival, November 28 – December 25.
Christmas lights and decorations at the MAYA shopping center, December 1–25.
A night market with food, drinks and music; a festive atmosphere all December.
An evening market with souvenirs, gifts and street food; festively decorated in December.
A large evening market in the Old City, held every Sunday.
Christmas brunches and festive events along the Ping River, December 24–25.
A village of traditional painted umbrellas about 25 minutes from the city.
A market of handicrafts and local goods about 30 minutes from the city.
A farmers market with farm produce and local goods; the roundup lists it on weekends in December.
A Christmas market in Mae Rim on December 12, about 30 minutes from the city.
A Christmas fair in Lamphun on December 19, about 45 minutes from Chiang Mai.
A mountain market in Chiang Dao on December 19–20, about 1.5 hours from the city.
A Christmas market on December 12–13: food, local brands, workshops, music and entertainment.
A market of local makers at La Luna Gallery on December 12–13: gifts and handmade items.
A festival of design, art, crafts and creative projects on December 5–13 at various venues around the city.

items.n: Christmas Market 2026 at Grace International School
items.d: The 10th annual Christmas fair: shopping, food, workshops and handmade goods, a bouncy castle town, prizes, movies and games for kids; childcare 100 baht per child. Seller registration is open.
A weekly psychosomatic practice of free intuitive movement and relaxation at JT FOREST – Artistic Sanctuary; no experience needed. Sign up by messaging the organizers on Facebook.

items.n: Converting an International Driving Permit to a Thai licence (car)
items.d: Personal experience: a medical certificate for 150 baht in 5 minutes, copies about 10 baht in cash; after submitting, you get a link to 5 videos and a test, and the QR code must be printed. At the appointment there is a colour test, payment of 105 baht, a photo and issue of the licence. It was converted even without a patronymic in the passport.

The Sai River on the border with Myanmar is polluted by mine runoff upstream: in November 2026 arsenic exceeded the norm 25 times, and water supply to 14 villages was cut. Arsenic was also found in the Kok River; locals are giving up river fish.
A farm with sheep in the mountains, from a roundup of places for a trip to Mon Jam and around.
A waterfall in the mountain forest, from a roundup of places for a trip to Mon Jam and around.
A coffee shop in the Mon Jam area with beautiful views, a coffee stop on the way to the mountains.
A cozy coffee shop in the Mon Jam area.
A scenic waterfall with several cascades, from a roundup of places for a trip to Mon Jam and around.
An orange farm, from a roundup of places for a trip to Mon Jam and around.
A camping-style cafe, from a roundup of places for a trip to Mon Jam and around.
Hot springs, from a roundup of places for a trip to Mon Jam and around.
An amusement park in the jungle, from a roundup of places for a trip to Mon Jam and around.

With a Thai driving licence, an annual pass with unlimited visits is sold at the window on the right for 800 baht, with a 20% discount for guests. It is sold to children with a Thai birth certificate or a student card. Beautiful grounds for a walk and the sunset.
items.p: annual pass 800 baht (with a Thai driving licence), 20% discount for guests

items.d: A new Rimping supermarket in The Local shopping project near the Louis intersection; opening on November 26.
A campsite on Doi Pui: in mid-November it was 13 degrees in the morning; you can go for misty cool mornings and a view of the city at night.
A coffee shop with drinks and pastries and two pickleball courts in a renovated old family house with its architecture preserved; design by Normal Study. Address: 124 Moo 2, Tha Wang Tan.
items.a: Tha Wang Tan, near Nong Hoi

items.d: A new cozy cafe with breakfasts, brunches, coffee and fresh pastries, with attention to presentation; many photo zones. Address: 101 Photharam Road.

Experience getting a residence certificate (needed for a Thai driving licence) at Chiang Mai Immigration: passport copies, E-Visa, TM30, rental contract, 4×6 photo. Copies and photos in the neighboring building, cash only; for 500 baht the certificate was issued the next day.
items.p: about 200 baht for photos and printouts; 500 baht for expedited processing

items.d: A sauna with an ice bath; the post announced the opening on November 12 from 12 to 19.

Jicama season has started in Chiang Mai: it looks like a potato outside, with crunchy, lightly sweet flesh inside; it has inulin, vitamin C, fiber, 38 kcal per 100 g. Eaten raw in slices with lime, salt and chili.

An open-air cinema on the roof of Central Chiangmai after a year's break: screenings on December 11–13 and 18–19 (Love Actually, La La Land, Notting Hill and others). Doors open 40–60 minutes before the show.

items.n: ลานนา สาขา เชียงใหม่ 89 พลาซ่า
items.d: A small local eatery with traditional Thai hot breakfasts: Jok rice porridge with pork or chicken, Kai Krata eggs, Vietnamese bread with fillings.
items.p: Jok from 30 baht; Kai Krata 40 baht; Vietnamese bread 20 baht

items.d: The first Michelin-starred restaurant in Chiang Mai and Northern Thailand (Guide Thailand 2027). Modern European cuisine from local Thai ingredients, chef Matteo Santalusia.
items.a: InterContinental Chiang Mai The Mae Ping

items.d: In the mall on the ground floor by the entrance on the road side, a large choice of cotton kids' clothes and a little footwear.
A Mexican food truck in Mae Hia: burritos with any filling of your choice; a review notes the very tasty salsa.
An intimate gourmet format in Hang Dong, more a separate dinner by advance booking than a restaurant for a casual visit.

items.n: Ban Don Luang (บ้านดอนหลวง)
items.d: One of the best-known textile villages of the North: about 50 shops and workshops with cotton fabric by the meter, Lanna-style clothing, scarves, bags and home textiles; prices lower than tourist ones. Best to go in the first half of the day.

items.n: Ban Nong Ngueak (บ้านหนองเงือก)
items.d: A village of handmade cotton fabrics with natural dyeing and Yong patterns; in the workshops you can see the weaving process, and there is a double loom. It is best to check visits to the workshops in advance.

items.n: TSL Chiang Mai — Thai Language in Motion
items.d: A conversational Thai course through traditional dance and culture with Teacher Pin: 4 Saturdays in a row, a group of 5–10 people, textbook included; dates are confirmed once five participants have enrolled.

items.n: This Is Fine: art in the six biomes of the Earth
items.d: An open-air exhibition on November 19–21 about the climate: six biome zones, free workshops (clay figures, weaving from bags about PM2.5), PechaKucha and live music by Broccoli Blossom at the opening. Workshops require registration.
Run 5 km anywhere, come to FRINGE.th with proof (Strava and similar) and get a free Americano or Italian Soda and a membership with discounts until the end of 2026.

items.n: Oeimi Café - คาเฟ่สระบุรี
items.d: A cafe in Saraburi near Bangkok with the CHRISTMAS WONDERLAND 2026 park, which has snow and a New Year atmosphere.

items.n: An Evening of Burgundy under the Stars
items.d: 15 winemakers from Burgundy, rare wines, champagne, oysters and a dinner by Nick & Nont from Friend’s Table; an art and antiques exhibition, a charity wine auction. Smart casual dress code, limited places.
Homemade mini donuts made with fresh milk, cooked fresh and packed in gift sets; preorders accepted, including large batches.
Ordering coconut water directly from the seller through Facebook messenger (written in Thai through a translator); it comes out cheaper than through Grab.

items.n: ปลายฝนต้นหนาว — Late Rain, Early Winter
items.d: Nine evenings on November 9–17: music, street food, a fair of OTOP goods and crafts, photo zones, fun for the whole family and wooden car races.

items.n: Monthly housing rental group with local owners
items.d: A Facebook group where you can look for housing directly from local owners who rent by the month; especially useful during the lantern festival, when short-term rentals get more expensive.

items.n: Candle evening at Wat Chedi Luang (Tam Phang Pa Teet)
items.d: A lamp-lighting ceremony as part of Loy Krathong: a procession around 17:30, arrival at the temple around 18:00, an offering of lamps and candle dances around the ancient stupa.

items.n: The 70th National Exhibition of Art & The 41st Exhibition of Contemporary Art by Young Artists
items.d: A joint National art exhibition and exhibition of young contemporary artists, November 9 – December 23; official opening on November 13 at 17:30.
items.a: Chiang Mai University Art and Culture Center

items.n: Hang Dong Winter Festival & OTOP Fair 2026
items.d: A winter fair on November 10–19 with OTOP goods, food, exhibitions, free concerts by Thai artists and the Lucky Fish Game.
items.a: Hang Dong, near Hang Dong Rat Rat Uppatham School

items.d: Open days at Chiang Mai University on November 12–13: an introduction to the faculties and programs. Registration is required by November 11, one faculty per participant.
Five days of coffee and relaxation on November 12–16: local roasters, coffee and matcha, outdoor gear shops, evening film screenings.
A TEDx on the future of education and the impact of AI: talks, workshops, games; in Thai and English. The ticket includes coffee breaks, lunch and materials.
items.a: Faculty of Economics, Chiang Mai University
items.p: student 250 ฿, teachers 390 ฿, standard 500 ฿, Angel 3000 ฿

items.d: The annual Royal Project fair on December 1–10: fresh vegetables, fruit, berries, coffee and tea from the farms, dishes made from Royal Project products, crafts of mountain communities; this year the emphasis is on cooperation with Bhutan.
items.a: Royal Project Agricultural Research and Development Center, Mae Hia

items.n: Tatvani by Pa Sak Tong Estate
items.d: A private estate on 12 hectares (6 villas, up to 18 guests) with its own sanctuary for rescued elephants, a 30-meter heated pool, a spa, a butler and a private chef; part of the Mandarin Oriental Exceptional Homes collection. 7 km to the White Temple, 3–3.5 hours from Chiang Mai.
A Sunday with jazz at FRINGE.th: jazz vinyl from MERLE COFFEE, a Vinyl DJ Set by DJ.BIRD and a live jazz quintet; free entry, welcome drink.
A new music bar in the listening bar format: music, cocktails and wine in a pleasant setting.
A new wellness space: an herbal steam room of natural clay with mosaic, a wood-fired sauna, an ice bath, organic architecture. The opening is promised for October 24, 2026.
A new pizza place on Tha Phae Road in the center, with a great view and a wide choice.

The 12th design week on December 5–13 on the theme Local Thunders, Global Transformation: exhibitions of scents, fabrics and sustainable textiles, POP Market (16:00–22:00) and LABB.Fest on December 5–6.
items.a: Old City, Chang Moi, San Pa Khoi

items.d: A seaside resort where the author is going with the kids for the holidays: a 70 m² room with a jacuzzi and a rooftop grill, pool slides, wood-fired pizza, national parks and bikes nearby. You can leave even during the smog; you get there by car.

items.n: Vinyasa Flow Yoga & Pranayama at Baya Chiang Mai
items.d: Weekly yoga with pranayama, stretching and balance with Ken (@kenbluefish) at Bamboo Sala; the price includes the Baya Day Pass (sauna, steam room, ice baths). First class on November 18.

items.n: Mat Pilates at Baya Chiang Mai
items.d: Weekly mat Pilates with Amp (@ampp_pana): core, posture, flexibility; the price includes the Baya Day Pass. First class on November 20.

items.n: Virus and colds: tips from expat groups
items.d: When a virus is going around town, expat groups recommend Fah Talai Jone (an herbal remedy: 1 tablet a day for prevention, 2 tablets 3 times a day with symptoms), a propolis spray, a nasal rinse with saline solution from 7-11, and turmeric.

items.n: Draft of new rules for getting a Thai driving licence for foreigners
items.d: The DLT proposes to abolish the exchange of foreign licences without exams, to require a visa for another 2 years for 2-year licences and to hold exams only at the DLT. Open for discussion until December 4, 2026; the current rules remain in force for now.
A cafe in a rose garden in Mae Rim with European dishes, desserts and coffee; live music (violin) on Saturdays from November to February.

items.n: Musical Saturdays at Fleur Café & Eatery
items.d: Live music (violin) every Saturday from November to February in the cafe's rose garden.

items.n: Traffic closures in the Old City before Yi Peng 2026
items.d: Because of the installation of Lanna lanterns, the stretch from Wat Mahawan to the square at Tha Phae Gate is closed at night: November 8–14 and 16–18 from 22:00 to 04:00, November 20 and 22 from 18:00 to 00:00.

A new tennis center (opening November 11, 2026) with a herbal steam bath and an ice bath; in November a court hour costs 111 ฿ and a 5-visit pass 1 111 ฿. It is behind the Mu Kratha Tao Than restaurant (the link leads to the restaurant).
A local cleaning company: Big Cleaning general cleaning with deep cleaning of kitchens and bathrooms and window washing; they clean houses, condos, offices and hotels.

items.n: ร้านเครื่องเขียน ไซเรียง (อุดมผล) Zirieng (Udompol) Stationery store
items.d: A two-storey stationery store where you can find everything for drawing at budget prices.
A record shop with a large selection of vinyl, rating 4,2 (137 reviews).
A shop of vinyl records and cassettes where you can listen to recordings on good acoustics.
New and second-hand records of various musical genres.
A small music bar with a vinyl collection, jazz, funk, soul and DJ performances.
An intimate bar where the music is played from vinyl records.
A creative space in Chang Moi that hosts vinyl nights and music events.
A bar-bistro with a music collection and a relaxed atmosphere.
A cozy coffee shop with jazz records; at the time of the post it was marked on Google Maps as temporarily closed.
A coffee shop with great music and female baristas, a recommendation from a subscriber.

items.n: The Fox's Den - Vinyl Records Experience Store
items.d: A shop of vinyl records, turntables and accessories, with servicing of vinyl systems; there is a coffee area.

items.d: A buffet of Thai dishes (kanom jeen); an air-conditioned hall for an extra fee.

A new coffee shop not far from Nimman with a Jetstream trailer: air conditioning inside, armchairs outside; in the same yard as Sukhontha Shabu, parking available.
A new coffee shop in a classic style with a lot of wood, a pleasant place to watch the sunset; operating in Soft Opening mode.
items.a: On The Rock Namphrae, Nam Phrae

items.n: Wat Tha Mai (วัดท่าใหม่)
items.d: The temple is more than 500 years old; a large palace of Phaya Nak (Nagas) has been created where the pond was. People come here to ask for luck, success, love and health.

items.n: Christmas tree with a Lanna soul
items.d: A Christmas installation as part of A Celebration of Wonders 2027, created with the CMU Faculty of Architecture: Lanna weaving, bamboo, Tung flags, VASSANA flowers and Disney aesthetics. Until January 3, 2027.

items.n: Coffee shop with the tastiest coffee (a subscriber's recommendation)
items.d: According to a subscriber, the tastiest coffee she has tried in Chiang Mai: good quality and a price without hype. The post does not give the name.

items.n: Sound Post String Orchestra — Concert No. 6
items.d: An evening of classical music: Handel, Mozart, Vivaldi and Christmas melodies; the special guest is the Cherubim choir. Free entry, donations welcome.
items.a: Main Conference Hall, The Building 75 Years, Church of Christ in Thailand

items.d: Handel's oratorio Messiah performed by the Chiangmai Philharmonic Orchestra and five choirs in the Henry R. Luce Chapel; free entry, few seats, so it is best to arrive when the doors open.
items.a: Payap University — Mae Khao Campus, Henry R. Luce Chapel

items.n: Truck Food Good Taste & Workshop + Dance Gang Challenge

Weekly Friday meetups of Beyblade fans: training and competitions; free to join with a purchase of 200 ฿ or more at Lotus’s Go Fresh.
items.p: free with a Lotus’s Go Fresh receipt from 200 ฿

items.n: Little Miss Noppamas (หนูน้อยนพมาศ) — Moonlight Contest & Market
items.d: A children's beauty and talent contest for Loy Krathong with a prize fund of more than 20 000 ฿ and the Moonlight Market night market with food trucks. Registration until November 12, 30 places.
items.p: participation 199 ฿ (first 20 free with a Lotus’s Go Fresh receipt from 600 ฿)

items.n: Yi Peng lantern corner at The Backyard Mahidol
items.d: A festive photo zone with traditional northern lanterns on November 10–24; the whole family can come.

items.p: free with a Lotus’s Go Fresh receipt from 200 ฿

items.n: Lampang Hospital — โรงพยาบาลลำปาง

An evening of nostalgic hits of the Bakery Music label from the 90s and 2000s performed live by Pony Band and Love God Band; table reservations are open.
Makro sells the sweetest sweet potato: it looks pricier, but is cheaper than one baked in foil and sold one at a time in Mae Kampong and other touristy places.
From the list "25 places in Chiang Mai 2026": come for the buns in the morning, before the pistachio donut sells out.

A small non-profit international school (since 2022) following Common Core standards, from Kindergarten to Grade 9: small classes, projects, an individual approach. About 180 thousand baht a year; the director Rachel is very easy to reach.
A canyon, especially beautiful at sunset; in some places the paths are narrow with no railings, so be careful. You can stop here on the way to Pai.
A viewpoint with sunrises and a sea of fog near Santichon village; you can have tea.
A bamboo bridge over rice fields, especially beautiful in the green season; bring a sun hat and water. Can be combined with Pam Bok Waterfall.
A Yunnan Chinese village with characteristic architecture and tea houses; can be combined with Yun Lai Viewpoint.

items.n: Wat Phra That Mae Yen — White Buddha

One of the old temples of Pai.
A popular waterfall near Pai, especially full in the rainy season.
A waterfall in a narrow rocky gorge; can be combined with the Kho Ku So bamboo bridge.
Natural hot springs with pools of different temperatures.
Mineral springs among greenery and forest near Pai.
A historic metal bridge over the Pai River linked to World War II; a convenient stop on the way from Chiang Mai.
A viewpoint in the Mae Hi area near Pai.
A huge cave system about an hour's drive from Pai: stalactites, stalagmites and an underground river that you float down on a bamboo raft with a guide. Set aside half a day.
A cafe-bar on high ground with panoramic views, a great place for sunset.
An evening market with food, souvenirs, music and street performers; there is a great tea house.
Evening shows, fire shows and dancing in Pai.
A raw vegan restaurant and yoga studio, the author's favorite place; in front of the cafe is a huge lawn where fairs are held.
Vegan smoothie bowls, fruit and homemade granola; rating 4,8 and more than 700 reviews.
A plant-based restaurant in Pai.
Healthy food with vegan and gluten-free options.
A cozy garden cafe with breakfasts and vegetarian dishes.
Coffee, breakfasts and pastries in Pai.
A bakery with bread, pastries, coffee, hummus and shakshuka.
A dinner restaurant at the Reverie Siam hotel, very beautiful according to the author.
A resort with hot springs, pools and cottages by the river; at breakfast on the terrace you can see mahouts bringing elephants to bathe in the river.
A small hotel in green surroundings.
A beautiful boutique hotel with pools and a colonial atmosphere.
Cozy cottages among greenery in the center of Pai.

items.n: Pang Pao Beach / Sky Beach Cafe

A cafe in the Mae Taeng area where you can rest and have a coffee on the way to Pai.
A picturesque waterfall in the forest on the road from Chiang Mai to Pai.

A viewpoint in the Huai Nam Dang National Park area; a convenient stop on the serpentine road to Pai.

A new cafe that opens as early as 7 a.m.; available on GrabFood.
