A Thai women’s clothing brand in a casual / Korean-inspired style: tops, dresses, skirts, knitwear, accessories; rated about 4.8 on Shopee. The store is on the 1st floor of Central Chiangmai.

items.n: Arsenic and lead pollution of the Sai (Mae Sai) River
items.d: In August, arsenic 28 times and lead 5 times above the standard were found in the Sai River. In Mae Sai and Chiang Rai, do not drink or cook with river water and do not eat fish from the affected stretches; exceedances were also found in the Kok, Ruak and the Mekong.

An ice rink: skates are free, there is a support aid for beginners; you can buy socks, and the 2nd floor is a comfortable place for parents to sit. Children can be professionally taught figure skating.
items.p: 250 baht for 2 hours; support aid for beginners 150 baht

items.d: A Japanese vintage warehouse with a refreshed space: furniture and interior items, ceramics, toys and dolls, watches, bags, Japanese items several decades old.
A Saturday morning market at CMU next to the Royal Project shop: vegetables and fruit, farm products, bread, ready-made food; 4.5 on Google from 143 reviews.
Harborland is getting ready to open in Central Airport, with the opening promised in early October.

items.n: RTC city bus: route No. 24 and fares
items.d: From 10 October 2026 RTC launches loop route No. 24 in both directions: the airport, Nimman, Chang Phueak bus station, Warorot, Tha Phae, Wua Lai. Free on 10–19 October, then 50 baht per ride, with an interval of about 20 minutes.
items.p: 50 baht per trip regardless of distance; free 10–19 October

items.n: Loy Krathong and Yi Peng: a cooking evening
items.d: A three-part program: a Thai cooking class, making a Kom Loi lantern and a traditional khantoke dinner with music and dancing. Free transfer within the city, limited places.

items.n: Little Boo! Halloween at The Backyard Mahidol
items.d: Kids’ activities and workshops all October, and on 31 October the main celebration: Kids Fancy Contest, art and make-up workshops, Witch’s Mocktail and Halloween Market.

items.n: J Journey at The Backyard Mahidol
items.d: Special plant-based and J dishes and a free Wellness Check: weight, blood pressure, blood sugar level. 10–18 October.
Every Friday at The Backyard Mahidol, activities for Beyblade fans.

items.n: Truck Food Good Taste × Dance Gang Challenge
items.d: Every Wednesday at The Backyard Mahidol, food trucks, food and dance activities.
A Japanese mineral onsen, sauna and steam room with no time limit; there are beautiful Japanese robes for photos.
A cafe next to the ice arena where it is convenient to work while the children skate.
Pasta and pizza, with occasional promotions; the author recommends the mashed potatoes.

items.n: Fuji K.: ready-made dinners for 5 days
items.d: Ready-made dinners for the week with calories and protein listed (22–39 g per portion): chili con carne, kung pao with shrimp, Hainanese chicken rice and more. Delivery of 2 meals on Monday and 3 on Wednesday, and portions can be adjusted.

items.n: Archaeoastronomy exhibition at Sirindhorn Astronomy Park
items.d: A new exhibition on the astronomy of ancient civilizations: how the Sun, the Moon and the stars influenced the placement of temples (Phanom Rung, Phimai, Doi Suthep, Stonehenge); there is an interactive zone with models. Free entry.

items.n: Sima Garden สีมา การ์เดน
items.d: A cafe, park, crafts and creativity in a garden the owner built by hand; kids will love it.

A playful improvisation practice with movement, storytelling and voice, no preparation needed. Led by Jori Martinez, a certified InterPlay leader since 2007; sign up by message stating the number of participants.

Plumbing and electrical work: installation of pumps and tanks, installation and repair of water supply systems, leak finding, electrical installation. They work in Chiang Mai and the surrounding area and speak Thai, English and Chinese.

A cozy hotel with a homey atmosphere: lots of greenery, an area by the water with fish, a cafe, a garden, a restaurant/bar and free parking; spacious bright rooms. It is about 15 minutes on foot to Nimman and the Old City.
items.p: depends on the room category and dates

items.n: Chiang Mai P.A.O. Public Park — สวน อบจ. เชียงใหม่
items.d: A big green city park, good for a relaxed run.

items.n: CMU Main Stadium — สนามกีฬากลาง มช.
items.d: The Chiang Mai University stadium with a running track, for workouts on a flat surface.

items.n: Ang Kaew Reservoir — อ่างแก้ว มช.
items.s: water body for walks and running
items.d: One of the most popular options for walking and running: water, greenery and a view of Doi Suthep.

items.n: Tad Chomphu Reservoir — อ่างตาดชมพู
items.d: A small body of water next to Ang Kaew with a path of about 725 m around it, for a short run or a few laps.

items.n: Railway Park / สวนรถไฟ (สวนสุขภาพคำเที่ยง)
items.d: A green city park for relaxed running and walking.

items.n: Mae Hia Farm — ไร่แม่เหียะ
items.d: A spacious green area of Chiang Mai University with open views and a feeling of countryside space.

items.n: Huay Tueng Thao — ห้วยตึงเฒ่า
items.d: Running around a reservoir among the mountains, for those who want to combine sport and nature.

items.n: San Sai Luang Public Park — สวนสันทรายหลวง
items.d: A large public park in San Sai for morning jogging and walks, always shaded by trees.

items.n: Nong Sam Kha — หนองสามขา
items.d: A park by a large pond in the Mae Jo area, a calmer option for a run.
Local craft dark beer that, according to the author, gives no hangover; live music on Fridays and a pleasant atmosphere.
A children’s cafe with a playground, from the author’s selection.
A jazz club with live music; a late-night jam session on Thursdays (Pato Quartet, Pis-Pis-Pis, then a jam). Parking at Ibis Styles Chiang Mai.

items.n: The View เชียงดาว
items.d: A hotel with a restaurant and rooftop bar in Chiang Dao: an almost 360° view of Doi Luang Chiang Dao and the rice fields, Thai and international cuisine. There are rooms with mountain views, a pool and a gym; visitors are advised to come at sunset.
items.p: about 200–400 ฿ per person at a restaurant

items.n: Lungmin Coffee / ลุงมิน คอฟฟี่
items.d: A cozy coffee shop by Chang Phueak Gate that grew out of a coffee cart at Nong Ho market; there are non-coffee drinks. On the second floor are Japanese vintage, second-hand and items from local brands.

items.n: Return of RTC Chiang Mai City Bus
items.d: RTC Chiang Mai City Bus resumes service from 31 August 2026, first on the former routes via the airport, Nimman, the market and Chang Phueak bus station, Kad Luang (Warorot), Tha Phae Gate and Chiang Mai Gate. Routes to Arcade and the railway station are not yet agreed.

A shop with a very nice owner, closed on Monday: sundresses, scarves, sarongs, robes, jewelry, glasses, much of it from Bali, beach gear, decor and electrolyte tea. Next door are a shop of candles, hats and ceramics and a store of clothing made of linen, cotton and silk.
A plumber’s contact on a Facebook page.
The clothing store is open again: handmade items, natural cotton and natural dyeing; the range is gradually being restocked.
Elegant breakfasts and big portions; they are building a new large children’s playground and a sports area.
Reopened in Mae Rim: full meals and French pastry from a chef with professional training in French cooking and pastry; there is ravioli with tom yum.

Local grocery delivery from farmers and small producers: organic vegetables and fruit, grains, tempeh, tofu, sourdough, farm milk, eggs, cheeses, kombucha; eco-friendly packaging, with a 20 THB discount for returning a milk bottle. Special prices of the week appear at times.
items.p: free delivery from 450 THB within 15 km of Mueang and Saraphi, from 800 THB within 30 km; Vegetarian Box for 4 weeks 3,520 THB

items.d: A new place in Amataros: freshly baked Czech-style chimney cake, a crispy sourdough pastry tube with soft-serve ice cream and toppings. 25% discount until the official opening.

items.n: Subscription for 5 Chiangmai Serenade String Orchestra concerts, 2026–2027 season
items.d: A subscription for five string orchestra concerts at Shangri-La: 24 Oct The Concerto Concert, 20 Nov The Little Mozart, 19 Dec Mozart’s Vienna, 30 Jan The Masterpieces, 13 Feb The Farewell. Children under 7 are not admitted, no refunds.
items.p: Exclusive 8 250 baht; Premium 6 250 baht; Standard 4 250 baht; children’s (7–12 years) 3 000 baht

items.d: The St. Petersburg National Ballet Theatre will perform “The Nutcracker” (about 40 performers) at Christmas, a show of about 2 hours. Children from 3 years are admitted; families are advised to take the daytime show on 25 December at 12:00.
items.a: SiamPic Hall, 7th floor of Siam Square One (BTS Siam, exit 4)

items.d: A boy sells seedlings that he grows himself: cucumbers, watermelons, pumpkins, water spinach. Buying and pickup are arranged through private messages.
items.p: cucumber 20 baht, watermelon 15 baht, pumpkin 15 baht, water spinach 10 baht

items.d: A zipline park in Doi Saket about an hour’s drive from the city; the main feature is the longest line, 1 200 m, in a big route with platforms and suspension bridges.
A zipline park in Doi Saket: an extended program of 23 ziplines and 36 platforms with suspension bridges, the longest line 919 m.
A zipline park in Doi Saket with a zipline roller coaster, a curving track on rails about 1.1 km long, called the longest roller zipline in the world.
items.p: large programs in Doi Saket roughly 2 000–2 500 baht

items.n: International Vipassana Center Wat Phradhatu Sri Chom Tong
items.d: A strict Satipatthana Vipassana retreat at a temple at the foot of Doi Inthanon: 7–14 days for beginners, a basic course of 21 days, wake-up at 4:00, 8 precepts, separate rooms. Translation into Russian is possible; register in advance through Northern Vipassana.
An authentic, calm teahouse with an inner garden; there's matcha.
A new recovery space: sauna, steam room, ice bath and pool, BBQ and drinks at extra cost; run by Felix, a Swede.
items.p: Day Pass 350 baht; children 0–5 free, 6–12 — 150 baht, 13+ — 350 baht

items.d: In Mae Taeng, home to more than 400 domestic elephants, the first elephant hospital at CMU has opened: treatment, intensive care for at least 6 elephants at once, training of vets and research.
A cafe and restaurant on a large site with a tropical garden and water; you can come just to eat. There are rooms with 1–3 bedrooms, Pool Villas and family houses for up to 10 people.

items.n: Foreign condo buyers in Chiang Mai, 1st half of 2026
items.d: According to REIC, in January–June 2026 foreigners registered about 379 apartments in Chiang Mai (+19%); China 182, Myanmar 35, USA 30, Russians in the top 10 for the first time with 9 apartments.
A separate room in a villa near the historic center: king-size bed, a reading nook by the window with books, a garden, a desk, a bathroom, an interior of wood and handmade ceramics.
An organic farm 75 km from the city, founded by the former monk Pi Nan: gardening, cooking together, meditation lessons and Buddhist activities, a family temple. A separate room and 3 organic meals.
items.p: 300 baht per person per night (meals included, taking part in farm work)

items.d: Italian brunch: 2 hours of unlimited Italian dishes and drinks, on the 1st and 3rd Sundays of the month.
A small place with traditional Burmese breakfasts, snacks and a wide choice of tea; two locations, by Wat Ket and by Wat Umong. A review praises the curry chicken pies.
Simple two-story houses with two bedrooms in a good location, available for less than a full year.
items.p: 18,000 per month for a 2- or 6-month rental; 16,000 for 12 months

items.d: Artisan gelato in the Old City, one of the places with tasty ice cream.
An ice cream cafe with coffee, one of the places with tasty ice cream.
One of the places where you can find tasty ice cream.

Two water barrels at 3–4 °C, a 40 °C barrel with Epsom salt, infrared and Finnish saunas, a hammam; unlimited chamomile tea, a thanaka scrub, towels and slippers provided; there's a cafe with khao soi.
A cozy teahouse in the city center: quiet, vinyl, greenery and Chinese tea.
An outlet with a big choice of underwear and bras for women with medium and large sizes.
A shop in town with a big choice of underwear (mostly synthetic), plus tops, vests, socks, pajamas, kids' pajamas, sportswear and swimsuits.
There are three Decathlon stores in the city, and all have swimsuits, including sports and functional models; there is more choice at the one near Tha Phae and the one next to Central.
Where to buy swimsuits: the mall has several stores at once: Central Department Store (swimsuits and bikinis), H&M (swimsuits and beachwear), Supersports (sports swimsuits).
A store on Huay Kaew Rd with a big selection of bikinis and one-piece swimsuits.
A department store; swimsuits can be found in the women's clothing departments.
A lingerie and swimwear store on Chang Moi Kao Rd, open late.
Second-hand: clothes, swimsuits, hats.
A lingerie and swimwear store.
A lingerie and swimwear store.
An interesting swimwear brand, sold online on Lazada.
An interesting swimwear brand, sold online on Lazada.
An interesting swimwear brand, sold online on Lazada.
A chocolate place with its own production and farm, growing matcha “to Mozart”; they recommend the thick hot audiva chocolate. Available without sugar and syrup, with plant-based milk.
Deep steam cleaning of sofas, mattresses, carpets, curtains and car upholstery with home visits; curtains are taken down and hung back, and the cost of cleaning a carpet is estimated from a photo.
items.p: 10% discount when ordering 3 items or more

items.d: A new wellness center in Hang Dong on a restored site, still getting ready to open.

A certified masseuse with more than 10 years of experience: mobile massage for women and families at home, in a hotel or a place of rest, bringing everything with her. Speaks Thai and English, there is a Family Pack.
items.p: Thai Massage 400 ฿/hour; Aroma Oil 450 ฿/hour; Sport / Deep Tissue 500 ฿/hour

items.d: A house in the mountains with a coffee shop and a view of the Mekong and three countries at once, morning fog over the river, sheep live here. The road is good, the mountain is not high.
Acquaintances booked a hotel using contacts from Facebook, it turned out to be spam, and they had to pay again on arrival. Check the phone number against the Google Maps listing and call back.
A website for renting cars.
Budget car rental.
Sale of cold and hot smoked fish, dried fish, red and black caviar, Kamchatka crab, mushrooms, berries, honey, jam, cottage cheese and Adyghe cheese; some items to order, fish can be salted.
items.p: for example: cold-smoked sockeye 2300 ฿/kg, chum salmon fillet 1720 ฿/kg, red caviar 500 g 4500 ฿, cottage cheese 1200 ฿/kg

items.d: Group sound baths with Tibetan and crystal bowls and gongs almost every day; mats, pillows and blankets are provided. Rating about 4.4, the downside is noise from Canal Road. Advance booking required.
items.p: 150 ฿; Mindfulness Gong Bath on Saturdays 300 ฿

items.d: A great restaurant in Nap Prae, Hang Dong, next to Hideaway.

A school that, according to the author, currently has the largest Russian-speaking children’s community among the city’s schools. About 180 thousand baht a year, can be paid monthly; contact — Rachel.
items.p: about 180 thousand a year, can be paid monthly

items.n: Yi Peng 2026 at the Skugga vineyard
items.d: A Yi Peng evening among the vineyards: premium buffet, unlimited wine and beer, a show, live music, fireworks and its own lantern release; the main festival can be seen from a distance. Places are limited.
items.p: General Admission 3 500 THB + VAT; VIP 12 500 THB + VAT

items.d: The place the owners of the The Cocoon sauna are moving to; opening soon. The restaurant Wild Thyme by Butterhead is next door.
The farm of the German Marcel and his wife Naa: a beautiful place, fresh vegetables and fruit, flowers, orchids.

items.n: Suan Saek Saek Organic Farmstay Egg Sell by Who Farmstay Chiangmai
items.d: An organic farm with accommodation, where on request dishes from organic products are cooked together with guests.
Royal Park Rajapruek: you can walk around, there is a sports zone; family annual passes are sold with 10 bicycle rentals.
A Saturday camp for children aged 5–8: creativity, stories, games, movement and outdoor activities, lunch included. Places are limited, booking directly.
The first Victoria’s Secret store in Northern Thailand opened on September 24 on the 1st floor of Central Chiangmai: lingerie, clothes and beauty products.

The parcel is sent by Thai post or courier to the CDEK office in Bangkok, then by air to a CDEK point or to the door in Russia in 7–16 days. Not allowed: medicines, alcohol, aerosols, cigarettes, jewelry and others.
items.p: 690 ฿ first kg, 450 ฿ each following kg (by the greater of actual and volumetric weight)

items.n: Food Truck on Mondays at The Backyard Mahidol
items.d: From October 5, food trucks gather every Monday: street food, mala, grill, plus live music and Random Dance.
Reopening of PLAYWORKS, a space for local design and illustration: on September 25–27 a hand-drawn portrait for 100 ฿, on September 28 Stamp Day with composition-making from stamps.

items.s: open space with shops and cafes
items.d: A small open space opposite MAYA with a cafe, shops, local brands and design projects; interesting for its unusual architecture.
A movement studio: yoga and Pilates, circuit/core/mobility, Franklin Method, dance and ballet for children and adults. Class packages instead of a membership, the first trial class is free.
A cafe and restaurant with a lawn, a stream, pigs, rabbits and ducks; lots of pretty desserts; entry 100 baht, which counts toward drinks; quiet, few people.
items.p: 100 baht per person, credited towards drinks

items.d: A local scent brand since 2011: soy wax candles, diffusers, oils, sprays, sachets, there is a Chiang Mai Series. You can make a wax sachet yourself at a workshop.
items.p: Wax Sachet workshop: 990 ฿ individually, 690 ฿/person for 3 or more

items.d: A seller of interesting interior items on Facebook; for example, an Indian cotton rug for 500 baht.
Praised for gluten-free pancakes with a minimum of oil and sugar, with homemade strawberry jam and black sesame.
A family jewelry store: rings and chains made to order, jewelry repair, stone selection at reasonable prices. The owner speaks English and answers on Instagram and LINE herself.
The second location of the same family of jewelers, next to Nopparat Gems 2.
A new children's bookstore in Mae Hia with second-hand books at low prices.

items.n: Free Open Day at Ganesha House Chiang Mai
items.d: A free day: blessing of the Ganesha statue, Yoga Flow, Hatha, Zen meditation, a free lunch and a kirtan on the roof at sunset. Up to 12 people for yoga, sign-up on sheets in the studio from 10:00, mats provided.
A private museum of Ganesha and Hindu art 35–40 km south of Chiang Mai, by the Chiang Mai–Hot road: more than 1000 images of Ganesha, a shrine, green grounds. Free entry.

items.n: Wat PaPhutthasri วัดป่าพุทธศรี
items.d: A temple recommended by the subscriber Evgeny, where you can get acquainted with Buddhism in Russian; his experience is described in a VKontakte post.

Natural hot springs in Pha Daeng National Park, about 40 km from Chiang Dao: stone pools in the forest, water at 50–60+ °C, with cooler areas for bathing; can be combined with the Sri Sangwan waterfall.
items.a: Mueang Na, Pha Daeng National Park

items.n: ฤดูภูเขา — LadooPookhao
items.d: Cozy cottages and glamping with a view of Doi Luang Chiang Dao: A-frame, glass cabins and options with their own relaxation area.
A secluded private villa in nature for a getaway for two: a pool, large windows and mountain views.
A store of children's and adult Crocs-style sandals with jibbitz at Central Airport (2nd floor, opposite American Tourister); the size can be exchanged within 7 days with a receipt and an uncut tag.
The main mountain and symbol of the district, 2225 m high; the climb is a full-fledged mountain route.
A mountain village at an altitude of about 1120 m with a stunning view of Doi Luang, many homestays with overnight stays.

items.n: บ้านหมอกอรุณ โฮมสเตย์
items.d: One of the good homestays in the mountain village of Ban Na Lao Mai with a view of Doi Luang.

items.n: Highland Agriculture Research Station of Pagia
items.d: The highland area of San Pa Kia with panoramic views and campsites; a night costs 100 baht, no hot water.
An atmospheric place to relax in nature.
A very secluded private house with a view of Doi Luang for a quiet overnight stay.
A small atmospheric stay with a view of the mountains.
A homestay in the mountains with beautiful natural surroundings.
A small coffee shop in Mueang Ngai.
A cozy cafe in Chiang Dao.
A small atmospheric stay in nature.
A cafe and creative space in Chiang Dao.
A stretch of road 3024 with huge trees on both sides, one of the most photogenic routes in the district.
A beautiful limestone waterfall in Mueang Na; convenient to combine into one trip with the Pong Ang hot springs.

items.n: Mae Mae Treehouse / Tree House Hideaway
items.d: Cottages in the forest in the village of Mae Mae for full immersion in nature.
A mountain village in a quiet green part of the district with a viewpoint, a beautiful place to watch the sunrise.
A small campsite in mountain nature.

items.n: Baan Aob Oun / บ้านโอบอุ่น
items.d: A small stay in the Mueang Ngai area.

items.n: Bamboo rafting and tubing in Muang Kong
items.d: Bamboo rafting and tubing in Muang Kong, for those who want to add some activity to a mountain trip.

items.n: DEW DROP — ดิวดรอป
items.d: A local supplier of drinking water with delivery across Chiang Mai, operating from San Sai. A very wide choice of containers: 20 and 18.9 L jugs, bottles from 250 ml to 1.2 L, 750 ml glass.

items.n: GLACIER — กลาเซียร์
items.d: A well-known water supplier from the Saraphi area with delivery across Chiang Mai. There are jugs of about 20 L, small bottles, crates and glass bottles, the main feature.

items.n: POLESTAR — โพลสตาร์
items.d: An old local water supplier from the Suthep area, known for regular home delivery of big jugs; the author notes the water tastes good.

items.n: BIG BELL — บิ๊กเบลล์
items.d: A local water producer in Chiang Mai, historically associated with delivery of big plastic jugs.
A Japanese restaurant in the omakase format: the chef decides which dishes to serve and in what order. Basic set 1990 baht, seasonal menu.
A natural cosmetics brand: balm for psoriasis and eczema, natural mosquito repellents, face masks, diaper creams for babies.

A large complex in San Sai: two gyms, a saltwater pool, a sauna, an ice bath, group classes (Pilates, yoga, HydroFIT), a Longevity Clinic, a cafe, mini golf, pickleball and children’s areas; 10–15 minutes from Central Festival.
items.p: Day Pass 350 ฿ (pool, sauna, ice bath, gym, lounge, billiards)

items.n: Soap Opera Bangkok Balm Deodorant Lemongrass
items.d: A natural balm deodorant made in Thailand, free of aluminum, baking soda and fragrance; variants with mint, lavender and orange are available. Sold on Lazada.

A farmers market on the grounds of Jing Jai on weekends: vegetables, fruit and products from local farmers. From 26 September 2026 it is temporarily at the entrance on Srimongkol Road; visitors are asked to bring their own bags.
A space for art, creativity, socializing and meeting people in a cozy-home format; it has moved to a new house at 20 Ku Tao 2 Rd., Chang Phueak. Announcements are on Instagram.

items.n: Buying a condo in Chiang Mai as an investment: discussion summary
items.d: A summary of the owners’ debate: the claimed 7–11% ROI against the calculation “10% gross ≈ 5% net” after fees, management 10–12% and vacancy; older condos are often a better deal, and the entry price and location matter; rental income is taxed, and a foreign freehold condo ≠ a house through a nominee.

The night Express No. 51 (about 22:30 → 11:40) passes the scenic stretch after Den Chai in daylight; the train is old and noisy, and 2nd-class berths are best booked a month ahead. You can get off at Den Chai and continue via Phrae and Nan.
items.p: Den Chai → Phrae songthaew about 60 baht; Phrae → Nan bus about 130 baht

items.d: A taxi for dogs and cats of any breed: a spacious air-conditioned cabin, free waiting; it takes pets to the vet, grooming and boarding in Chiang Mai and the surrounding area.
Regular free technical sparring sessions without hard hits in the Suthep area; the group’s page has many videos of the sessions.
A resort with a cafe in a natural setting.
A cooking class for children aged 5–8 at Bloom Space: the children cook themselves, listen to stories and have dinner together with what they made; classes every Monday.
items.p: 800 ฿ single visit, 2 800 ฿ for 4 classes (dinner and VAT included)

items.d: An art school for children near Pathfinder: large formats, different techniques and the principle “create your own, don’t copy”; a lesson lasts 4 hours, the first one is free.
items.p: 600 ฿ per class (4 hours), first one free

items.n: Aunt Kai’s Kitchen ครัวป้าไก่
items.d: An old Thai restaurant in the Suthep area with home-style food that is not adapted for tourists and big portions; the specialty is fish, seafood and Thai salads.
A family place with Chinese-Thai food that has been running for more than 27 years; the specialty is koy seemee and rad nah, and there is jellyfish in sesame oil.

items.n: ลานลงต๋อง — Lab Lung Dhong
items.d: A place with Northern Thai cuisine and traditional Lanna dishes; the specialty is buffalo larb and lu.
An old street pad thai near Nawarat Bridge, cooked by grandmothers on a real charcoal stove from a recipe many decades old; the portions are small, so it is better to take several and come early.
A family bakery and shop of about 50 years by Warorot Market; the specialty is coconut rolls.
An old halal restaurant in the Muslim quarter of Ban Ho: the local version of khao soi with chicken or beef, khao mok gai, satay and goat biryani.

items.n: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวแดงโอชา Daeng Ocha
items.d: An old, simple noodle shop without tourist polish; the specialty is a rich beef broth with noodles that has been eaten here for several generations.
A famous stall with moo ping, charcoal-grilled pork on skewers, which many call one of the best in Chiang Mai; by 17:30 it is often sold out.
items.h: come early, often sold out by 17:30

items.d: An eatery with Hainanese chicken rice, founded in 1957 (the owner is 85 years old): tender chicken, fragrant rice and sauce, also pork satay.

A new cafe on Wua Lai Road by the Old Chiangmai Cultural Center in a building with Lanna architecture: premium matcha (the cold whisk matcha latte is praised), coffee, desserts and ice cream; parking and car charging.
items.p: up to 100 ฿ on the Wongnai menu

items.d: A new family cafe by the railway park in a deliberately “ruined” brick building: a large green area, a playground with a sandbox, trampolines and swings, brunches, Thai and Western cuisine, parking. Connected to Living A Dream Cafe.

An operator of active tours: kayaking, night kayaking, caves + kayaking, hiking and mountain biking; on promotion 2 activity tickets for ฿1,500, the voucher is valid until September 2027, no more than two vouchers.

A ceramics festival at Jing Jai Market with works by more than 50 Thai and foreign artists: main program 19–22 November, exhibition 19–30 November, pop-up store from 2 November 2026 to 31 January 2027; coffee activities and meetings with the makers.

items.n: จดหมายจากเชียงดาว — The Letter from Chiang Dao
items.d: A small complex of four cabins with a green garden, mountain views and wooden interiors, from a tent with a glass bathtub to a wooden house.
A small stylish place in nature that combines a mountain atmosphere and modern design.
A separate house for one group on a hill with a 360° panoramic view, including Doi Luang; a large terrace for stargazing and a bathtub; it is hard to reach by car.
An online flea market covering all of Thailand, including Chiang Mai, created by Artem (the author of the interactive guide).

items.n: The Causeway Irish Pub and Restaurant
items.d: An Irish pub-restaurant that, in the opinion of an expat who has lived in the city for 11 years, has the best burger in Chiang Mai; the excellent service is also noted.
A medical center where the recommended dermatologist Dr. Siri works and where you can take a blood allergy test (food + inhalant allergens).
A shop of light clothing in a natural palette, with linen, dresses, tops, pants and skirts in a relaxed resort style; two locations in Nimman (Soi 5 and Soi 13).
A massage and sleep salon where yoga teacher Nitti leads the Float in Sound practice.
A pediatrician at Bangkok Hospital Chiang Mai specializing in pediatric pulmonology, including allergic conditions of the respiratory system.
A pediatrician at Chiang Mai Ram Hospital specializing in Pediatric Allergy & Immunology, the most specialized option for a child with an allergy.
A Bangkok Hospital Chiang Mai specialist in internal medicine, allergy and clinical immunology; publications on urticaria, asthma, atopic dermatitis and allergen-specific immunotherapy.
A hospital where adults can have an allergy examination: panels of food and environmental allergens and an extended test for 107 allergens.
items.p: 20 food allergens — 2 900 ฿; 20 environmental allergens — 2 900 ฿; 107 allergens — 4 500 ฿

items.d: An excellent dermatologist at the Sriphat medical center, recommended for skin problems.
A dermatologist at Ram dermo clinic, recommended for skin problems; she also has her own evening clinic on Canal Road.
A cozy farm stay among greenery in Pong Yaeng (88/9 Moo 3).
A beautiful Lanna Colonial style hotel in the Old City (56 Samlarn Road) with pools and the atmosphere of a real home.
Minimalist houses (3/3 Hatsadi Sewi); some options come with a private pool.
A small stylish place to stay in Nimman near cafes and restaurants.
Beautiful cabins in Chiang Dao with stunning mountain views.

items.n: The Mellow Pillow @ Chiang Mai Gate
items.d: A stylish small hotel near Chiang Mai Gate and the Saturday Walking Street (5/2 Suriyawong Alley).
A modern cozy house in Chiang Dao made of natural materials with a minimalist interior and mountain views; 5.0 on Google Maps.
An intimate place in nature in Chiang Dao with beautiful mountain views.
A quiet wellness hotel at the foot of Doi Suthep near Wat Umong (189 Suthep Alley).
An intimate modern hotel with a pool, a garden and beautiful design (111/2 Kotchasarn Road).
An atmospheric European-style hotel with stone, wood and a pool in the Old City (24/1 Soi Inthawarorot 3).
An elegant colonial-style hotel with a beautiful pool (34 Huay Kaew Road).
Free Zumba for everyone at Vivid Dance Studio Chiang Mai from the Filipino Community in Chiang Mai; no date is given in the text.

Spaces in nature for retreats, workshops and corporate events: the Main Ballroom of 250 m² for up to 240 people, the Flora House hall of 100 m² for 20–45 people for yoga and Reiki, and the open lawn Krisda Doi Garden.
items.p: Pool Day Pass — 500 baht (includes 300 baht F&B credit)

items.d: Drawing courses for schoolchildren ม.1–ม.5: drawing, portfolio and preparation for art exams; from 1 October to 30 November 2026 a 300 baht discount for new students and for a referred friend. Sign-up through Instagram.

A new space in Mae Rim from the creators of Siam Insect Zoo: a gallery of butterflies and insects from around the world, live insects, DIY workshops and an interactive installation; there is a cafe, and no booking is needed.

A small local service: the owner cleans apartments, condos and houses herself with her own supplies, has a background check, accepts homes with pets, and offers regular cleaning for landlords; closed on Thursdays.
items.p: Studio/1BR from 350 baht; 2BR from 550 baht; 3BR from 700 baht; 4BR+ from 800 baht

items.d: An interactive guide put together by @artartemev from the chat’s recommendations: 500+ locations with reviews, a map with a filter by distance and “open now”, an events calendar, day routes and a handbook on daily life and visas.

A small wellness retreat in Hang Dong: outdoor massage with a mountain view, an outdoor onsen, a sauna, a steam room, villas with private pools; the place is remote, and mosquitoes and forest sounds come with it.

items.n: Gift — dog sitter and dog walker
items.d: A beginner dog sitter is taking her first clients: a walk with pick-up after the dog, water after the walk, monitoring of the dog’s wellbeing and photos/video.

items.n: Nadia Drive & Guide in Chiang Mai
items.d: A guide popular among expats with a personal driver: individual trips around Chiang Mai on a flexible route at your own pace.
A monthly evening in the 137-year-old teak Borneo House: live jazz, a free choice of beer, wine and cocktails, food from open cooking stations; dress code Colonial Elegance / 1920s.
A Thai girl makes fresh ginger shots to order with orange, carrot, lemon, turmeric and black pepper, without preservatives; delivery around Chiang Mai is possible.

A clinic that does intravenous iron infusions (Iron drip); according to a patient’s review from a few months ago, 2 500 ฿ per infusion plus a 600 ฿ doctor’s fee, so it is better to check the current price.
items.p: 2 500 ฿ per infusion + 600 ฿ fee for the first visit

items.d: A bar in the Old City (98 Chaiyapoom Road) with rock, blues and covers; on Thursdays there is Thursday Night Live with several sets, and the food is good.
The café of The Earth Hotel, open to non-guests too: all-day breakfast and brunch with attractive presentation and large portions; the Summer Salad, homemade sourdough and brioche get praise.
A shop on Tha Phae Road with local design, handmade items and vintage: ceramics, tableware, jewellery, postcards, clothing; a jazz bar is behind the shop.
A new restaurant of real Mexican cuisine in the Suthep area not far from My Vietnam; on opening there was a 50% discount on the whole menu for the first week.
A rose garden and nursery that sells rose bushes: 3 bushes for 200 baht.
A small boutique hotel in a Scandinavian-Japanese style with spacious rooms and suites, some with a living room and mini-kitchen; the café The Moon Eatery is part of the hotel.
A minimalist shop in Nimman with handmade items: ceramics, wood, accessories, jewellery, tableware and home goods.
A brand shop with original characters (for example, the duck man) that are turned into clothing and souvenirs; it holds creative workshops.
A local design shop with T-shirts, bags, posters, gifts and scented candles, with a café attached; it was temporarily closed in the week of the post.
Thai massage, aroma oil, herbal balm, deep tissue, hot stone and foot massage; the One Nimman branch is open late.
A nail salon focused on nail art: Korean aesthetics, detailed drawing and raised 3D elements; cats live in the salon.
A small juice bar in the Klay Commu space: natural juices and smoothies with no added sugar, acai bowls, and a photo booth nearby.
A space that hosts yoga, Pilates and barre classes; the juice bar Goofy Juice is located there too.
A local design shop: ceramics, home goods, works by Thai designers, prints, postcards; there is a small coffee corner.
Korean barbecue that the author calls the best in the city.
A very beautiful mountain temple; bring sun hats, pay the pickup trucks for the ride up, and you can grab a snack in the parking lot. There are hot springs on the way and the Rai Homfa garden nearby.

items.n: Hot springs on the way to Wat Chaloem Phra Kiat
items.d: Hot springs more or less on the way to the temple Wat Chaloem Phra Kiat; the post does not give the name.
A beautiful garden near the temple Wat Chaloem Phra Kiat.
A classic campsite by a stream with a view of Doi Luang Chiang Dao: toilets and showers, hot springs nearby, you can bring your own tent and dogs.
Glamping with ready-made tents and a view of Doi Luang Chiang Dao — no need to bring gear, suitable for families and groups.
A waterfall with a camping area: you can bring your own tent or rent one on site, and the waterfall is a walk from the campsite; good for a trip with older children.
The “wildest” campsite, by a waterfall in the forest: your own or a rented tent, no electricity and almost no signal; the waterfall was closed after the 2025 flood, so check its status in advance.
A beautiful villa with few reviews that can be found on Airbnb.
A 5-bedroom villa that the author’s friends rented for several families; it was comfortable for both adults and children.
The No. 1 online cleaning app in Thailand: hourly cleaning of houses, condos, rooms and offices in Bangkok, Chon Buri and Chiang Mai; customer reviews, damage insurance.
A bar with live Thai Jazz Fusion music from Wednesday to Sunday: two sets per evening (AC 2B, Roots Isaan, Bamboo Trio, Som-Tum Jazz Messengers and others), cocktails.
A new Telegram chat for casual conversation; sometimes members hold meetups on different topics.

items.n: Chiang Mai Kayaking Center — Wat Fah Ham
items.d: A simple local rental of single and double kayaks for a self-guided paddle on the Ping; the pier is at the temple Wat Fah Ham and monks help visitors into the boat. Sometimes no one is at the pier, so it is better to check in advance.

items.n: Leisure River Kayaking — Mae Ngat → Mae Taeng Forest Reserve
items.d: An organized outing from Chiang Mai: about 4 hours of kayaking on the Ping through the Mae Ngat valley to the Mae Taeng Forest Reserve; transfer, equipment, briefing, escort and lunch are included, suitable for beginners. The operator is Chiang Mai Mountain Biking & Kayaks.
items.p: depends on the date and booking platform

items.d: A day tour: about 17 km (4 hours) on the Ping through the Chiang Dao jungle, Class 1+; transfer, guide, equipment, lunch and water are included, suitable for motivated beginners. The operator is Chiang Mai Mountain Biking & Kayaks.
An evening route of 6 km on the Ping toward the centre of Chiang Mai: hotel pickup at 18:00, briefing and launch, single and double kayaks. The operator is Chiang Mai Mountain Biking & Kayaks.
A blues/rock bar that recently moved to the 3rd floor of Chiang Mai Night Bazaar and reopened in its new location.
A jazz club by the North Gate of the Old City (91/1–2 Sri Poom Road): different musicians every evening, improvisations and jam sessions; the “hit of all hits”.
A small bar on Nimman Soi 5 with blues, funk, soul and jazz from local musicians; the program changes by day.
An intimate bar in the Old City (34/3 Ratvithi Road) with jazz, funk, jams and improvisations by local musicians.
A small bar by Tha Phae Gate (2/7 Chang Moi Kao Road) with acoustic music, folk and blues.
A small bar with a garden in the Chang Phueak area (8/22 Moo 2) where calm live music is played regularly.

items.n: The Sax Music House — One Nimman
items.d: A music bar in One Nimman (B101–102) with live bands in the evenings and a full menu, so you can come for dinner.
items.h: approximately from 16:30 to midnight, longer on Friday and Saturday

items.d: A large Thai music venue (73 Khlong Chonprathan Road) with bands, popular Thai music and evening shows.

items.n: Cleaning service from the post t.me/ChiamgMaimy/4540
items.d: A subscriber’s review: a Thai granny-manager brought two cleaners who scrubbed a house with 3 bedrooms from 9 to 16; liked more than BeNeat.
A small free local library and a space for families with small children, created by local parents; Story Time and Rhythm Time take place here.
A children’s bookshop in Hang Dong with used English-language books from the US and UK; on the website you can search books by age (0–2, 3–5, 6–8, 9–12, 12+).
Regular meetups for families with toddlers at various locations in Chiang Mai; there is a free library for members, and books are brought to meetups 2 times a week.
A national library not far from the Old City (20/1 Bunrueang Rit Rd) with a separate children’s section of illustrated books in Thai, English and other languages.
A provincial public library where you can find children’s books.

items.n: Muang Chiang Mai District Public Library
items.d: A district public library where you can find children’s books.
A café in Hang Dong with a separate children’s area with toys and books, as well as an open outdoor area.
A festival in Chiang Dao on November 26–29 as part of the Northern Thailand festival season.
One of the biggest festivals in Thailand, December 3–7: music, art, workshops, wellness, culture and sustainability.
Music, nature and a community gathering in Panya Forest on January 25–27.

A series of music, art and community festivals from November to February along the route Chiang Dao → Chiang Mai → Chiang Dao → Pai, with a trip to Wonderfruit; the peak is from late January to late February, and dates may change.
A route of Chiang Mai (4 days) → Chiang Dao (3) → Chiang Rai (3) → Lamphun (2) → Mae Kampong (2), with a list of temples, caves, waterfalls, markets, tea plantations and cafés for each stop.
A technician who professionally cleans washing machines without damaging the appliance; the price and visit can be arranged by phone or on LINE.

A dinner club with ready-made restaurant-level dinners based on classic French technique, cooked just before delivery and brought warm; the menu is on LINE, and members get a Member Shop with bread, delicacies and desserts.
items.h: delivery on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays

items.d: A Mexican restaurant with a lunch set: a burrito, an enchilada or 2 tacos (vegetarian and vegan fillings available), a drink and free chips with guacamole and salsa; air conditioning and board games.
An art space for kids and adults: painting on canvas and bags, modeling, Paint Pour, Paint & Sip, family classes, birthday parties; no booking needed, all materials included, with a cafe on site.

A secret rooftop bar at 193 Chang Moi Rd: coffee, matcha and hojicha by day, drinks, Japanese izakaya food and sometimes live music in the evening; for the sunset it is better to come early to the upper deck.
Italian and European food, wine, a Wine Buffet and cocktails, live jazz in the evenings; visitors praise the food, atmosphere, service and music.

items.n: ร้านราเมงพี่หมี (Ramen Pee-Mhee)
items.d: A ramen shop; the Kaki Shio, a ramen in a salty broth with a pork trotter, is especially praised.
Individual and group dog walks, day care, pet sitting and pet transport; they send walk reports and work in most areas.

items.n: Huen Por Sala Daeng (เฮือนป้อสล่าแดง)
items.d: A space with traditional Lanna wooden houses that preserves the knowledge of sala craftsmen (building, woodwork, crafts); once a month it holds a program about a Northern Thai tradition with a Lanna Market, buffalo rides and performances.

items.n: Baanrainaifun Organic Garden บ้านไร่ในฝัน หางดง
items.d: A cafe by a rice field with very tasty khao soi with lion's mane mushroom and a greens juice that can be mixed with honey and passion fruit juice on request.

items.n: Kahavadi Chiang Rai, Curio Collection by Hilton
items.d: A new Hilton hotel on the bank of the Mae Kok River, 15 minutes from the airport: 167 rooms in the style of Lanna merchants’ houses, the restaurants Larderley and Tasabiang, The Ledger bar, eforea Spa, a pool and a fitness centre open 24/7.
items.a: bank of the Mae Kok River
items.p: from roughly 2 600–2 700 baht per night on some dates

items.d: A Friday sale of Royal Project products: for example, quinoa milk and chocolate tomatoes.

Ayurveda and acupressure consultations from Sangeeta, who has trained therapists of spas and wellness centres in Thailand; she sees clients in a tree house at Baanrainaifun Organic Garden, speaks good English, and has a massage room.

A panoramic view of the Mae Kuang Udom Thara reservoir with its small islands; a route with a boat crossing and a 2–4 km climb along a forest trail, comfortable shoes and water are needed, and the trail is slippery after rain.
items.p: about 250 baht per person or about 1 500 baht per boat for up to 6 people

items.s: boat and escort at Doi Nori
items.d: Local organizers of the boat crossing and escort for the Doi Nori route; it is worth contacting them in advance and asking about the trail condition.

items.n: Chokmai Mint (เรือนำเที่ยว โชคมายมิ้นท์)
items.d: A local boat operator that takes people across the Mae Kuang reservoir to the Doi Nori route.
A café that regularly makes toasts and bowls with fresh figs; once it gave guests fig cuttings to plant.
A shop of natural stones and jewellery where you can order custom pieces.
A vegan and vegetarian café.
A new outlet of Korean synbiotic yogurt (probiotics and prebiotics) with fruit and toppings such as goji, aloe, konjac and mochi; some portions have 10–12 g of protein. Opening in September 2026.
A café-bistro with decent tasty food and coffee, where a large children’s playground has been built among greenery: slides, climbing frames, swings.

A small hotel with cabins in Mon Jam: air conditioning, hot water, a private bathroom; breakfast and dinner (a Moo Kratha set) are included, children under 7 are free, and there are teepees and houses with a pool.
items.p: rainy season promotion: White Box House 1 390 baht/night, Teepee Tent 1 190 baht/night, Cher Doi House 2 990 baht/night, Phu Doi House 3 990 baht/night; extra bed 400 baht

items.n: Alena and Anton: suluguni at Kad Farang
items.d: Russian-speaking people from Moscow who trade at Kad Farang market; a new item has appeared in their range — suluguni.
A new yoga and sportswear brand made from eco-friendly materials; sold through an online shop with delivery from Bangkok.
A café in an old wooden house with a beautiful green garden: coffee, desserts and a pleasant atmosphere; people come more for the place as a whole.

items.n: Chiang Mai: heading for wellness and longevity
items.d: On September 3–4, 2026, the Chiang Mai Longevity Summit took place at Shangri-La Chiang Mai: the Chiang Mai Wellness Playbook 2026 and four pilot wellness routes were presented, including San Kamphaeng hot springs and the villages of Samoeng and Bo Kaew.
A small coffee shop in the green garden of a family home in the Old City: the beans are roasted right in the garden, and the owner also bakes homemade bread.
A coffee shop in the Old City where you can get to know Northern Thai coffee: the beans are grown by farmers from the Akha community.
A small specialty coffee shop in the Old City — a calm place without unnecessary pretension.
A coffee shop in the Old City for those interested in good coffee and roasting culture.
An intimate coffee shop with a slow bar and local beans just outside the Old City; it was especially praised in the discussion, and one commenter called it the best coffee shop in Chiang Mai.

Fully vegan Thai street food at Phaploen Night Market by the Night Bazaar: cooked in front of you and served on banana leaves; the green curry noodles, corn fritters, pumpkin curry and vegan sausage are praised.
A new burger place near Doi Suthep with a homely “like visiting a friend” atmosphere; its hours are irregular and are worth checking on the map.
A new place: warm buns with French butter, signature jam and Monsoon tea.

A coffee shop and culture club in Don Kaeo: specialty coffee, sourdough, pastries and its own film club with arthouse cinema (Scorsese, Kiarostami, Haneke); a minimalist space, with a Bed & Breakfast.

items.n: Nuts and tea leaves for Burmese salad (Lazada)
items.d: Lazada links where you can buy nuts and fermented tea leaves for Burmese tea leaf salad.
A hotel where you can stay or just come for dinner at a restaurant with a splendid view; there is a deer and a piece of salt in the toilet.
Home, studio and shop of the potter Somluk Pantiboon (who studied Karatsu ware in Japan), 12 km north of Chiang Rai: wood firing, local clay and ash, open workshops, a garden and a small cafe.

A family’s experience: the Horizon Club is better value than breakfasts for a family (lounge with food, afternoon tea, Happy Hour, room upgrade), and kids get a passport with tasks and gifts; booking through Shangri-La Circle is cheaper than Agoda. There is a pool day pass and a coffee shop with croissants.
A temple in the Old City and a center of the khua thong craftsmen’s community (Lanna brasswork: patterns, jewelry, temple umbrellas). The temple has a small museum, Phuak Taem Khuatong.
A small market with the atmosphere of the Sanpakoi area: tasty food, cute things, simple local Chiang Mai. Held in front of the library building and along Charoen Muang.
items.h: every first Sunday of the month, 08:00–13:00

items.d: A farm with sheep: paid entry with a drink, a sheep-herding show at 10 am, you can buy feed and feed them; it gets crowded.
items.p: entry 100 baht, can be exchanged for a drink

items.n: Pang Hwa Flower Garden & Orange Orchard
items.d: A garden in the mountains: a field of purple flowers, photo spots, wooden houses, a tangerine orchard and a cafe with gazebos; more tangerine farms nearby. They left the car at the concrete road and walked.

items.n: Neighboring farm (next to Pang Hwa Flower Garden)
items.d: A farm next to Pang Hwa Flower Garden that the author recommends seeing there too, in the mountains near Mae Rim.

A fairytale castle among flowers with wooden walkways and a cafe, next to an alpaca farm not far from Mon Jam; the ticket can be used as a discount on drinks. Best in the morning or closer to evening, peak bloom is in the cool season.
A cafe and farm among the mountains: they grow coffee, there are sheep and views of green slopes; especially atmospheric in the rainy season.
DEER Forest Cafe is a cafe in a garden and nature; the main draw is the greenery around and the deer.
A cozy cafe with a wooden cabin atmosphere and nature around, at The Wood Cabin Chiang Rai.
A cafe on Doi Chang with an open view of the mountains and several relaxation areas; especially magical when mist comes down in the morning.
An art cafe in Chiang Rai itself: Mid-Century interior, a gallery and creative activities.
A small cottage-style cafe among greenery where you can sit by the water, and cats live there; especially recommended in the rainy season.
A small wooden cabin in the mountains where the main star is the surrounding landscape; Cabin & Cafe operates there.

items.n: A spot where “divine” grapes were delivered
items.d: The author reports that very tasty grapes were brought here; the place is not named in the post, only a map link.
The Mae Ngat dam and reservoir, an hour and a half from Chiang Mai: you can take boat rides with beautiful views.

items.n: Salakphat at Huen Por Sala Daeng
items.d: A monthly program: the theme is Salakphat, the traditional Lanna offering of food to monks, with a procession; buffalo rides, traditional houses, performances, Lanna Market 09:00–13:00.
items.a: Huen Por Sala Daeng, San Pa Tong
items.p: entry 50 ฿, of which 20 ฿ can be spent on a drink

items.d: Modern northern Thai cuisine: local dishes, lots of herbs and spices, beautiful presentation; be sure to notice the bone with marrow.
A place with Thai breakfasts: rice, eggs, pork and other local dishes; a good way to try a proper Chiang Mai breakfast.
A craft bakery whose draw is huge round doughnuts with fillings and creams: pistachio, chocolate, vanilla, berries.
Vietnamese cuisine; worth trying nem nướng, grilled sausages with rice noodles, herbs, vegetables and sauces.
Matcha straight from Japan, including from Hoshino (Fukuoka), in different varieties with different flavor profiles; a very atmospheric place in Baan Kang Wat.
items.a: Suthep, Baan Kang Wat, Soi Wat Umong

items.n: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวหมูภูเขาไฟอุดมผล (Udomphon Volcano Pork Noodles)
items.d: A local noodle shop with famous “volcano” pork noodles: rich broth, pork, meatballs and lots of add-ons; next to the Udomphon bookshop.
Frozen yogurt with no added sugar, with fruit, chocolate, granola and other toppings.
A stylish minimalist cafe: coffee, matcha and desserts; the draw is ice cream and unusual drinks with ice cream, and a beautiful interior.
A fantasy festival: knight duels and fencing, characters and quests, a fair, a parade, photo zones and an evening program; you can come in costume.
items.p: Early Bird 250 ฿; VIP Bronze 600 ฿; VIP Silver 900 ฿; VIP Gold 1 200 ฿

items.d: In the author’s opinion, the best cosmetics consultant in Central Festival is the young man at the Charlotte Tilbury counter: he chose everything attentively and added gifts.
Jon Jandai’s Pun Pun Center for Self-Reliance (TEDx “Life is easy”): seed saving, natural building, courses and programs for adults and children; you can come for a visit or a tour.

items.n: Grand Sunday Brunch at InterContinental Chiang Mai
items.d: Brunch every first Sunday of the month: Canadian lobster, Fine de Claire oysters, Wagyu carvery, live cooking and a kids’ dessert station; Come 4, Pay 3 offer.
items.a: InterContinental Chiang Mai, The Gad Lanna, 1st floor
items.p: adults 2 400 THB net; children 6–12 years 1 200 THB net; under 6 free
items.h: every first Sunday of the month, 12:00–15:00

items.d: A music camping festival in the mountains with Thai indie folk: Phumin, Manutsawee, Khwanjai; tickets with accommodation are available.

items.n: Free library of Russian-language books in Chiang Mai
items.d: A free library with books in Russian, opened in September 2026 (according to the author, at Murka); it has a Telegram channel.
A coffee shop in a collector’s home: antique furniture, tableware, vintage, much of it for sale; upstairs there are three antique rooms to stay in. About a 5-minute walk to Tha Phae Gate.

items.n: Away Chiang Mai Thapae Resort - A Vegan Retreat อะเวย์เชียงใหม่ท่าแพรีสอร์ท
items.d: A vegan hotel that serves a large vegan tea set for two.

A small forest cafe that feels like a country house: wooden furniture, vintage, greenery; drip coffee, homemade desserts, people praise the pastries and cheesecakes. On the way to the Doi Saket hot springs, with parking and occasional creative events.

A mountain circuit of ~600 km: Chiang Mai → Pai → Mae Hong Son → Mae Sariang → Chiang Mai (highways 107/1095, return via 108). Thousands of curves (1 864 on one section), by motorbike or car, allow 4–5 days.
A huge cave system with stalactites, an underground river and wooden rafts on the Pai → Soppong stretch; in the rainy season access to some parts depends on the water level.
A Chinese village near the Myanmar border: a lake, tea plantations, Chinese food and a cool climate; a nice extra detour on the Mae Hong Son Loop.
A mountain at about 1 400 m near Mae Sariang that you can visit on the Mae Hong Son Loop route.

An eco-hotel in the forest on the Mae Hong Son Loop: villas (Jolie and Pitt stayed in one) with a private fire pit, a nature trail nearby, morning yoga with an instructor; they grow the greens for the kitchen themselves.

items.n: Hmong New Year in Ban Pang Ung
items.d: In early January the Hmong New Year is celebrated on the grounds of the Ban Pang Ung school: traditional costumes, a fair, food, music and an old game of tossing a ball.
A homestay next to the Ban Pang Ung school, a great place to get to know local customs and nature.

items.n: Visa-free period for Russians cut to 30 days from September 15, 2026
items.d: From 15.09.2026 Thailand cancels the 60-day visa exemption: for Russians it is 30 days under the bilateral agreement plus a possible 30-day extension (up to 60 in total instead of 90). Those who entered before September 15 keep their period.

items.n: Wise in Thailand in 2026 and the DTV
items.d: Wise is moving customers with a Thai address to its Thai entity: the DTV is accepted for verification, and THB transfers, top-ups from a Thai account, PromptPay/Thai QR and a new card are coming. You can’t withdraw cash at Thai ATMs with this card.

A renovated trampoline park from 28 August 2026 with a SUPERHERO theme: ~2000 m², 15 attractions, including a Floating Boat with water by the ball pit, Ninja Fortress, a ~8 m slide, a LEGO zone and a sandbox.

items.n: Kad Kang Tong Hong Rue (กาดก๋างโต้ง โฮงเรือ)
items.d: A small community market: Thai food and sweets, drinks, groceries, souvenirs and goods from local makers; the atmosphere of an ordinary neighborhood market, suitable for a family trip.

items.n: New houses for rent next to the sports center (Kad Farang, Hang Dong)
items.d: Two new houses in the Kad Farang area, practically nose to nose with the sports center; a point on the map.

items.n: Another house for rent near Kad Farang
items.d: Another house for rent near the author in the Kad Farang area; an approximate point on the map.

items.n: Rise in COVID-19 cases in Thailand (August 2026)
items.d: Since the start of 2026, 95 357 cases and 14 deaths, with growth over the last month, variant NB.1.8.1. Recommendations: stay home when sick, wear a mask in crowded places, wash hands, vaccination for risk groups; see a doctor for shortness of breath and chest pain.

items.n: Changes to DTV application rules from August 31, 2026
items.d: From 31.08.2026 you can apply for a DTV only in the country of citizenship or permanent residence, so visa runs to neighboring countries no longer work; a police clearance certificate is required. The DTV itself is unchanged: 5 years, multiple entry, up to 180 days, from 500 000 baht.
A new cafe in the Modern Forest Luxury style among greenery: drinks, pastries, desserts, pizza, pasta and Thai dishes.

A clinic where, according to a friend of the author, Botox was done with excellent service (consultation of doctors, a separate room, a mask, anesthetic cream) for the same price as a home cosmetologist.
items.p: botox (Korean brand), forehead and around the eyes — 5000 baht

items.d: Royal Project shops sell very tasty grapes, like homegrown ones according to the author; buy them while they are on sale.
One-off 3-hour creative classes for kids aged 4–12 (painting, drawing, clay, DIY, printing), groups of up to 12 children, materials included; no long-term course sign-up.
items.p: 600 ฿ per class; 3 000 ฿ for 6 (3 months); 6 000 ฿ for 12 (6 months)

items.d: Rose makes homemade fermented foods, baked goods, desserts, natto, kombucha and tasty hummus; she sells on Saturdays at the Saturday Organic Market near CMU and on Tuesdays on the other side of CMU, and the kombucha is available in health-food shops.
items.h: Saturday — Saturday Organic Market; Tuesday — a stall on the other side of CMU

items.d: A cafe next door to the Saturday Organic Market near CMU; the author suggests dropping in after the market.

Interactive Chiang Mai University maps: risk zones and flood depth if the Ping rises (with 2024 data). The risk zone covers lowlands along the river: Nong Hoi, Nong Pa Khrang, Pa Daet, Wat Ket, Fa Ham, parts of Chang Phueak and San Phranet.

A pass of the local Eiiga platform: you show it at partners (cafes, restaurants, shops, craft places, entertainment) and get discounts and gifts. With the promo code TAT100 it costs 99 baht instead of 199.
items.p: 199 baht; 99 baht with promo code TAT100

items.d: A place with a sauna almost diagonally across from Ferment Space; relaunching as a retreat space with yoga, dance, art and food. News on Instagram.
One of the new notable clubs: stylish interior, a DJ booth in the center, tables and sofas around; they usually play hip-hop, EDM and popular club music.
A new green space by AWC (opening 26 August 2026): food, coffee and tea, local brands and crafts, art, live bands and DJs, a cabaret show; marked on the map as LANNATIQUE KALARE.
A space in Lanna Garden about the meeting of Lanna and Chinese heritage, with a focus on architecture and a Chinese courtyard.
A gastronomic project in Lanna Garden with northern and ethnic flavours.
A cabaret show with drag artists in Lanna Garden.
The first full Tesla Center in the north: sales and service; already on Tesla’s official list, opening planned for the third quarter of 2026.
items.a: Tha Sala, 498 Highway Chiang Mai–Lampang Frontage Road

items.n: Burmese food seller at the market near Kad Farang
items.d: A guy at the market near Kad Farang sells Burmese “addictive” salad, chickpea tofu and nuts for the salad; the spot is from the avocado stall, turn into the left aisle.

items.n: Alena and Anton’s products (cottage cheese, kefir, sochniki)
items.d: Cottage cheese, cottage cheese pastries, cheesecakes, sochniki, kefir and more; the products can now be found at the fair (judging by the neighbouring post, at Kad Farang).
An intimate creative evening: poetry by Mali and Josefina, a sound performance by Mo, then an open mic of 5–7 minutes for anyone who wants to take part. Free entry.
items.a: Kindred Studio @ Lansieow Freeative Art Space

items.d: A shop that sells, for example, a carved door from a Gujarat temple.
A restaurant from a list of refined places for dinner; nearby is its more budget-friendly family version, Bstreet food.
A restaurant in the Mae Rim area that can be combined with a trip out of town.
The pizza with gorgonzola and pear is recommended.
A burger chain with smash patties of imported beef or pork, three branches; for US Independence Day it released the My Boy burger, Blue Cheese Smash with blue cheese and bacon.

An active Buddhist temple and historic site, not a park: yoga and acro yoga, climbing on statues, pagodas, waterfalls and rocks, swimwear and revealing clothes, and noise are prohibited; for violations the temple may be closed to tourists.

A large park: the Ho Kham Luang pavilion, an orchid house, greenhouses, Bug World, gardens of 22 countries, the Sky Walk, a playground; a free electric train runs through the park. Seasonal blooms by month.
items.p: Foreigners: adults 200 baht, children 150; Thais 100/70; concession 70; under 100 cm free; annual 899 baht, group (3 people) 2 000 baht

items.d: Khao soi, a large area for walks, art and ceramics, from the “unusual places” for visitors.
A cocktail bar focused on signature drinks and an evening atmosphere.
A cocktail bar for those interested in the Chiang Mai cocktail scene.
A cafe-restaurant with tropical greenery, water and a jungle atmosphere; recommended to show to visitors not only for the food but also for the atmosphere.

items.n: Ezy Airlines flights Chiang Mai — Mae Hong Son / Pai / Nan suspended
items.d: Ezy Airlines planned 12-seat Cessna flights to Mae Hong Son (35–40 minutes, 2 500–3 500 baht), Pai and Nan, but suspended its northern programme because of an airport landing fee of about 40 000 baht; the Mae Hong Son authorities are seeking a review.
A free clothes swap with no price tags: bring clean items in good condition and take other people’s. Leftovers go to the Free Bird charity centre to help refugees; swaps have been held since 2013.

items.n: Doi Suthep / Wat Phra That Doi Suthep
items.d: One of the main symbols of Chiang Mai; locals advise visiting both early in the morning and late in the evening, as the atmosphere is completely different.
Chiang Mai’s Old City is one of the places locals advise showing to first-time visitors.
A national park and the highest mountain in Thailand, from the list of recommendations for visitors.
A famous mountain village in the Doi Saket mountains, from the list of recommendations for visitors.
Mountains with beautiful views, from the list of recommendations for visitors.
A zipline for those who want to add some adventure, from the list of recommendations for visitors.
A night market from the list of places locals advise showing to visitors.
A night bazaar from the list of places locals advise showing to visitors.
A Sunday walking street market from a list of places for newcomers.
A place that is praised especially for its smoothie bowls.
Doughnuts for those who want something sweet and unusual.
An elephant park that is recommended, among other things, for its good treatment of the elephants.
A small place with an open kitchen and modern local cuisine from different regions of Thailand; baked bone marrow with nam prik kha and beef tongue are popular.
Thai cuisine with a focus on fish, seafood and sustainable fishing.

items.n: Chow Chow Thai Contemporary Food and Kitchen
items.d: Modern Thai cuisine with Asian fusion notes.
A cosy cafe for a daytime visit.
A restaurant with a Japanese focus.
An option for an evening out and drinks.
A small place with Vietnamese cuisine, in particular banh mi.
A homely cafe for a quiet daytime visit.
A gastronomic place with a signature approach and local products in Nimman.
A cosy place for a healthy breakfast: big smoothie bowls (Green Green Bowl, Berry Berry Bowl), protein smoothies, juices, plant milk, coffee from Karen Tribe and board games.
A small science club in September on the theme Autumn Forest: simple experiments, observations and creative tasks; suitable for homeschoolers.

items.n: Phocoderma velutina caterpillars: do not touch
items.d: Caterpillars of the Phocoderma velutina moth are found in the forests around Chiang Mai (including the Chiang Dao area) and cause severe skin itching on touch because of their venomous hairs.
One-off and regular house cleaning, pressure washing, lawn mowing and tree trimming, planting, minor repairs, painting and furniture work in Chiang Mai and Lamphun.

items.n: Arsenic in Chiang Rai rivers (Kok, Sai, Ruak, Mekong)
items.d: A bottom sediment check in July 2026: arsenic up to 80 mg/kg in the Mekong, 55 in the Ruak, 45 in the Kok, 25 in the Sai against a norm of 10. A danger to the food chain (fish); the Kok River also runs through Mae Ai in Chiang Mai province.

items.n: Huai Tueng Thao Waterfall น้ำตกห้วยตึงเฒ่า
items.d: Huai Tueng Thao Lake with a trek to the waterfall (about two hours there and back, muddy in the rainy season, so sturdy footwear is needed). The author did not like the food on the rafts on the lake.
items.p: entry 50 baht cash, free for children under 6–7

items.d: A decent Indian restaurant about 5 minutes from Huai Tueng Thao Lake; they cook fast, and the owner has a little dog.

The NARIT astropark: inexpensive workshops for children (crafts for about 100 baht versus 700 at school) and a cafe with a great view for parents. The schedule of paid workshops is published on a separate Facebook page, not on the website.
A barber at Kad Farang; it says “men only”, but he cut the female author’s hair too. His LINE is in the photo; it is best to check the schedule in LINE.
items.h: approximately from 11 to 19/20, says no days off

items.d: A website with events in Chiang Mai, developed by Rustam, who also designs posters and websites for concerts.
A spacious two-story cafe: you can sit with a group or work, almost a coworking space; there are cats.
A cosy cafe for breakfast and brunch with a green yard (from the list of 70 coffee places).
A pretty cafe with a dog called Robert; you can bring your own dog; there's Greek salad.
A cafe in the Australian coffee style with Market Lane Coffee beans from Melbourne.
A cafe and art space in the Old City from the list of 70 coffee places.
Specialty coffee, music and vinyl.
A hotel worth stopping by for the cafe and especially for the palace-style decor.
One of the best-known bakeries in Chiang Mai: sourdough bread, pies, croissants and a cozy garden. A good option for breakfast.

Homemade baking by a cook with a Le Cordon Bleu diploma in the World Club Land moo baan (Nong Kwai, Hang Dong): unexpected combinations, homemade jams, dogs allowed; almost everything is sold out by lunchtime — better to come in the morning.
A cafe mentioned twice in the list of 70 coffee places: in the “cafes among gardens” section and in “for beautiful photos”.
A cafe from the “cafes with beautiful views” section of the list of 70 coffee places.
A cafe from the “for beautiful photos” section of the list of 70 coffee places.
A cute stylish takeaway matcha shop with a couple of chairs; the menu includes premium matcha.

A tea house in a teak house from 1915 in the Lanna Colonial style on Tha Phae Road, restored by the family behind the Raming Tea brand: a quiet garden, celadon ceramics, the atmosphere of old Chiang Mai.
A cosy coffee shop by day and an atmospheric cocktail bar in the evening by the North Gate, a convenient starting point for a walk around the Old City.
A cafe from the “cafes with a view of the Ping River” section of the list of 70 coffee places.
A place for matcha lovers from the list of 70 coffee places.
A family German restaurant with an 18-hole mini golf course in Hang Dong: you can have lunch, play and keep the kids busy; usually closed on Tuesdays.
A lakeside cafe from the “cafes with beautiful views” section of a roundup of 70 coffee shops.
A garden cafe with a large open area where dogs are welcome.
Afternoon tea in collaboration with Skugga Estate: single-origin cocoa from Mae On in desserts, pastries and savoury snacks, with a focus on local products.
Dog boarding, daycare and training; there is a natural swimming pool, a running field and a fenced agility area.

items.n: Cost of living in Chiang Mai in 2026
items.d: Price benchmarks for 2026: a Thai dish 50–80 ฿, specialty coffee 60–120 ฿, songthaew 30–50 ฿, massage 200–400 ฿/hour, 1-bedroom outside the centre ~9 500 ฿/month, home internet 600–900 ฿, mobile 300–600 ฿, gym 1 000–2 000 ฿/month.
Help for expats: documents and applications, Thai driving licence, finding housing, bank account, buying a car, insurance, translations, visas and TM30. English and Thai.

items.n: Tips for drivers in the rainy season
items.d: Tips for the rainy season: slow down and keep your distance, turn on the headlights, watch for mopeds, avoid sudden braking, beware of puddles and potholes, and in heavy downpours stop and wait it out.
A sports complex with a big outdoor pool (~38 m), a kids’ pool (~20 m, depth ~50 cm), a small slide, a fitness gym and courts; one ticket includes the pool and fitness.
items.p: single visit: adult 110 THB, child under 13 70 THB; 10 visits (for 1 month): 899 / 599 THB
items.h: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri 13:00–19:30; Sat, Sun 09:00–19:30; closed Wednesdays

items.d: A cafe near World Club Sport Complex in Hang Dong; the author advises stopping by to sit after the pool.

items.n: Galyani Vadhana: a mountain district of Chiang Mai Province
items.d: A remote mountain district (since 2009, formerly part of Mae Chaem) at an altitude of 900–1200 m: pine forests, fog, rice fields, Karen and Lisu villages. It is ~150–160 km to Wat Chan, about 4 hours; stay at least overnight.

items.n: ป่าสนวัดจันทร์ — Wat Chan Pine Forest / FIO Watchan
items.d: A huge pine forest with a lake, wooden cabins and paths; one of the best-known places in the district, with low light pollution, so it is good for stargazing.

items.n: เลอเปลอ — Le Pler
items.d: A small atmospheric café in an old wooden house: greenery, flowers, homemade pastries and local coffee.

items.n: สดชื่นแจ่มใส คอฟฟี่88
items.d: A small slow bar in the mountains: coffee, simple food and a view of nature; a good stop on the way.

items.n: ฟาร์มอินน์ปอวา — Farm Inn Porwa
items.d: A small farm stay in nature: a calm rural setting, walks, a campfire.

items.n: ดอยไม่มีชื่อ — Doi Mai Mee Chue / No Name Mountain
items.d: “The mountain without a name”: open mountain spaces and panoramic views; especially beautiful in the rainy season, when clouds and fog sit between the mountains.

items.n: บ้านแม่ตะละเหนือ — Ban Mae Tala Nuea
items.d: A mountain village among forest and rice fields: trekking, views of terraces, local life.

items.n: เกอลีโกล — Ker Lee Grow
items.d: A cozy homestay in Ban Mae Daet Noi: a wooden house, a large terrace, mountains all around, a slow pace of rest.
A quiet place to rest among the mountains: greenery, mountains, fog.
A homestay in Ban Mae Daet Noi with beautiful views and morning fog in the valleys; about 111 km from Chiang Mai, 3–4 hours.

items.n: Chiang Mai Padel Pilates Recovery AMA
items.d: A new sports space: padel, padbol, Pilates, a recovery zone and a place to socialize. Opened on 23 August 2026, with free activities for the first 10 days; courts and classes are booked through Playtomic.

items.p: brunch 1 200++ ฿/person; brunch + free flow wine 1 995++ ฿/person

items.d: The only villa with a pool in an area where elephants live: you can see the elephants right at your door. Ask about the price directly.

A studio with painting and creative classes, in the selection of 50 places to escape the smog.
One of the places where workshops on sewing, clothes repair, embroidery, natural fabric dyeing and weaving are held throughout the year.

A wellness club: Himalayan salt, magnesium float, volcanic, warm 40°C and cold 10°C pools, a steam room and sauna, a café. A spa and ancient Lanna practices from folk healers (Yam Khang, Tok Sen and others). Soul Soak on Fridays.
items.p: Thermal Wellness Pass — 600 baht (unlimited for the whole day)

items.d: An independent bookshop since 2011 with tea and homemade desserts; it hosts lectures, film screenings, book clubs and discussions. There are nice inexpensive souvenirs and a ginger cat.
Salads, bowls and other light dishes. Recommended by Mae Hia residents for ordering through GrabFood.
The best-known scented candle studio: they make candles shaped like pastries, matcha lattes, teddy bears, fruit and cheese; at the workshop you choose the scent and colors and take the candle home.

A sauna with an ice plunge from the selection of wellness places; according to the post, it closes on 1 October 2026.
Yoga and a spa from the selection of Chiang Mai wellness places.
A spa and wellness center from the selection of Chiang Mai wellness places.
A new bar the roundup’s author singles out: a nice place to meet friends, have a drink and spend the evening.
A coworking space from the selection of Chiang Mai places.
