Ceramics from the handmade & crafts section of the selection of Chiang Mai places.
A ceramics studio from the workshops section of the selection of Chiang Mai places.

An account of the Thai ritual of “calling the khwan back” after a fright, an illness or before important events, and of the Chetawan academy. In Chiang Mai the tradition is preserved by Rajabhat; master Athit Bunmawong from San Kamphaeng is named as a specialist.

An organic coffee farm of the Lahu mountain people: processing of coffee, tea and cocoa, walks, a Lahu village, a vegetarian lunch, roasting arabica yourself. You can go from Chiang Mai for a day; book in advance.
items.p: half day — 800 ฿/person; full day — 1 200 ฿/person; overnight +400 ฿ with breakfast

items.n: Vejpong Natural Honey (น้ำผึ้งเวชพงศ์)
items.d: A Thai natural honey brand since 1969, with no additives; sold in large chains, available at Makro (255 ml × 2 and 760 ml) and online.
A popular bar on Nimman Soi 7, easy to combine with other bars in the area.
One of the best-known options for a big noisy group on Rattanakosin Road: music, dancing, a maximally party atmosphere.
A dressier bar in Nimman: beautiful interior, music, DJ.
A big nightlife venue on Sirithorn Road (Chang Phueak): music, lights, live performances, late opening hours.
A tasty place with great brunches, drinks and desserts — everything is at a good level.
A spacious two-story café with a large choice of desserts, including Thai tea flavor; pets are allowed.

items.n: Once in a Blue Moon Coffee & Hostel
items.d: A cozy café with a hostel on Moon Muang Soi 9 — convenient if you are walking around the Old City.
A small cozy café on Nimman Soi 17 where you can combine coffee and pastries.
An intimate café with a beautiful modern space in Chang Phueak.
A matcha bar in Chang Moi — for those who want matcha rather than coffee.
A café in Suthep where you can have a proper breakfast; opens early — convenient for a morning outing.

items.n: KRAM คราม Cafe & Eatery
items.d: A café-restaurant on Suthep Road with breakfasts, Thai food and coffee.

items.n: บุญรวย กาแฟและไข่กระทะ Boonruay
items.d: A traditional Thai breakfast and the famous ไข่กระทะ — eggs in a pan; Chang Moi Road.
A calm café on Charoen Rat Road (Wat Ket), on the eastern side of the city — a way to get out of the tourist center.
A café with breakfasts, toasts and drinks on Huay Kaew Road — can be combined with a trip toward Doi Suthep.
A café north of Chiang Mai in Mae Taeng — convenient to combine with a trip in that direction.
A café among northern nature in Mae Na, Chiang Dao — a destination for a separate trip.
A small café in the north of the city, in San Sai / Mae Jo.
A coffee roastery in the southern part of Chiang Mai, in Hang Dong.
A small café in a calm suburban location in San Sai.

items.n: MAHAMITr.DSK มาหามิตร (ดอยสะเก็ด)
items.d: A café in Doi Saket for a separate trip east of Chiang Mai.
An art space with a garden, creative activities and a café in Mae Rim; a good option for a family trip.
An intimate café on the eastern side of Chiang Mai, in San Kamphaeng.

items.n: บ้านยื่นหมูยื่นแมว Yeunmoo Yeunmaew Home
items.d: A café with a homey atmosphere in Mae On — worth going to as part of a small trip out of town.
A café in Mae Taeng for a northern route: lots of wood and a natural setting.
Cooks homemade food to order: bread, syrniki, mashed potatoes, nuggets, pickled cucumbers, sauerkraut, pies and cakes.
A café where the food is cooked very tasty and fast; the pad thai is especially praised. Located across the road from the “basik”.

items.n: Waterfalls in the rainy season: flash floods
items.d: On 15 August 2026 a flood came within seconds at Mae Sa Waterfall in Mae Rim, knocking people off their feet. In the rainy season the water level can rise sharply because of rain upstream: if you hear a staff member’s whistle, get out of the water immediately.
Gluten-free vegan bread at nice prices; build your own sandwich with pesto, sun-dried tomatoes, roasted vegetables and other fillings. Near the trail.
A place from the list of places for coffee and food with a dog (check the conditions in advance).
A café from the list of places where you can come with a dog (check the conditions in advance).

A wellness space in Pa Tan by the Ping River (601 Pa Tan Soi): ice bath, cold and hot baths, steam room, pool; Rainy Day Wellness promotion daily 18:00–22:00 — Thai massage 60 min 400 baht; check whether the promotion is available.
items.p: promotion: Thai Oil Massage 60 min — 700 baht (instead of 850); Thai Massage 60 min — 400 baht (instead of 550); Full Wellness 2 hours — 300 baht (instead of 450)

items.d: A trampoline arena and laser tag: a summer camp for ages 6–14 on Tue/Thu/Sat (1,000 baht a day with lunch), dodgeball on weekends at 11:30, discounts for solving a Rubik's cube, "five come, four pay", trampolines + laser tag combo 450 baht.
items.p: camp 1 000 baht/day; trampolines + Laser Tag combo 450 baht
items.h: camp: Tue, Thu, Sat; Dodgeball: Sat and Sun at 11:30

items.d: A large green area in Hang Dong where dogs are welcome: water bowls and treats, and Sunday Dog Social owner meetups on Sundays.

A French project in a Lanna manor with gardens in Mae Rim (512/6 Moo 1, Rim Tai) with chef Olivier Elzer (30+ years in Michelin restaurants); Le Bistro is open: tartare, onion soup, bourguignon; OpenTable 5/5.
A European cuisine restaurant near Le Manoir Botanica in Mae Rim: the author calls it wonderful, everything is delicious, and the prices are lower than at the neighboring restaurants.
An organizer of wellness events with Barre Sculpt workouts; moving to a new large and beautiful space in the Jed Yod area.

The 10 baht coin of 2533 was issued in only 100 pieces and is valued at up to ~1 million baht; on 19 August 2026 the Treasury launches the Coin Market platform and offers it as the first lot. There are fakes made from 2537 coins.

items.n: Makhwaen (มะแขว่น) — a spice of Northern Thailand
items.d: A spice from the fruit of Zanthoxylum limonella: citrus aroma, heat and tingling, like Sichuan pepper; added to northern larb, nam prik, kaeng khae; a GI application was filed in April 2026. At the market look for มะแขว่น / มะแข่น.

items.n: What to bring back from Chiang Mai: GI products
items.d: A guide for gifts: products with a geographical indication: makhwaen, Thep Sadet coffee, Bo Sang umbrellas, Chiang Mai celadon, Teen Jok Mae Chaem silk, Sai Nam Phueng oranges and Emperor lychees from Fang.
Thailand’s first coastal national park (1966), ~60 km south of Hua Hin: limestone “three hundred peaks” mountains up to ~605 m, marshes, beaches, mangroves, birds and caves; good for cycling.
A famous cave with a royal pavilion inside, in Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park.
A wooden walkway across the marshes with mountain views in Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park.
Dogs can be brought inside the air-conditioned room.
A dog-friendly place where you can hide from the heat together with your dog.
A burger place where you can bring a dog; there is an air-conditioned area.
A large green area where you can spend time calmly with your dog.
A dog-friendly café where you can combine coffee with a walk.
A real dog café — a place created especially for dogs.
A dog-oriented place, including a pool.
A pet-friendly hotel and café with a pool for dogs, grooming and a separate menu for animals.
A space created especially for dogs.
A café-restaurant from the list of places where you can come with a dog (check the conditions in advance).
A café-hostel from the list of places where you can come with a dog (check the conditions in advance).

A place from the list of places for eating with a dog (check the conditions in advance).
A healthy food place from the list of dog-friendly venues; as The Bowl Spot it prepared lunch for the Barre + Cacao wellness morning.
They help with catching and rescuing snakes, including venomous and injured ones; if there is a snake in the house and the species is unknown, it is better to call them than to deal with it yourself.

items.n: Snake in the house: the golden tree snake
items.d: Chrysopelea ornata (Golden Tree Snake, “flying snake”) often lives near people where there are many trees and geckos, and can crawl into a house; it is mildly venomous and almost harmless to humans, but do not touch it with your hands.
A small free hot spring in Chiang Dao: a simple, local and fairly wild place with small tubs by a stream (not to be confused with Pong Ang).
Wat Pha Lat temple; the post has fresh photos and a map link.
A small homemade pasta café in an alley near Wat Duang Dee: carbonara, pesto, arrabbiata, with shrimp, salmon, mussels; good value for money; few seats and no parking of its own.
items.p: Salmon Pesto — 185 baht, Shrimp Arrabbiata — 165 baht

items.d: Driver-guide Autsadajit Likitchewan (Jia): sends a well-thought-out route in advance, drives carefully, gets along with children, makes stops and photographs the family; travels to Mae Kampong, San Kamphaeng and around Northern Thailand.
A space in nature (from 18 August 2026, Sweet August): yoga, somatics, contact improvisation, dry and wet sauna, a saltwater pool, an art room and coworking.
items.h: sauna, pool, art room, coworking: Mon–Thu 10:00–17:00

items.d: Stability, mobility and strength practice at JT Forest Artistic Sanctuary on Mondays and Wednesdays, from 18 August 2026.
Deep Flow Yoga classes with Joy at JT Forest Artistic Sanctuary on Tuesdays and Thursdays, from 18 August 2026.
Somatic practice with Nami at JT Forest Artistic Sanctuary on Tuesdays, from 18 August 2026.
A jam of contact improvisation and free movement at JT Forest Artistic Sanctuary on Thursdays, from August 2026.

items.n: เฮือนป้อสล่าแดง (Huen Por Sala Daeng)
items.d: An authentic village of 27 rai in Ban Klang (108, San Pa Tong): dozens of old Lanna houses and a temple, built with clever ventilation; the whole village is run by one family of 8 brothers; entrance to the center is free.
items.p: free entry to the cultural center

items.n: กำกิ้นมะเก่า เล่าเรื่องบนเฮือน นั่งเกวียนย้อนวันวาน
items.d: A monthly old Lanna day at Huen Por Sala Daeng: traditional houses and crafts, local food and drinks, cart rides, people in northern costumes.
items.a: Huen Por Sala Daeng, San Pa Tong
items.p: for foreigners adults 100 baht, children free

items.d: Ancient rock salt from the underground brine of Nan province: no microplastics, minimal processing, natural minerals; close in price to regular salt; the author recommends the large flakes as a finishing salt. Sold on Shopee.
Raw and homemade pasteurized milk with 3,68% fat content, delivered across Chiang Mai, noticeably cheaper than store milk; delivery is free for an order of 4 kg; ordering through Facebook.
items.p: raw — 30 baht/kg (from 2 kg — 25); pasteurized — 35 baht/kg (from 2 kg — 30)

items.d: Japanese teppanyaki on the 5th floor of Central Festival: meat, fish and seafood are cooked on the griddle in front of guests; the beef steak, tenderloin and garlic fried rice are praised.
A company recommended to expats in Chiang Mai’s English-speaking community: Thai tax residency, filing tax returns, foreign income, tax planning.

An introductory Zen meditation meeting: stretching, instructions for sitting meditation, two 15-minute sessions and a conversation; the leader has practiced since 1971 and was a monk for 7 years. Air-conditioned room, 1,5 hours.
A gardener: came with a partner, and in two hours they cut all the grass and bushes and cleared everything away with a leaf blower.

A clinic since 2006, dermatologist Dr. Jedjunya Siripakkaphant (formerly at Ram): several types of lasers for scars and pigment spots; laser for a scar 9500 baht per procedure, injections extra; free consultation.
items.p: laser scar treatment 9500 baht per procedure (steroid injections separate); consultation free

items.d: One of Thailand’s best-known contemporary art museums; during Galleries’ Nights on 8 August 2026 a separate daytime route went there.
A lab cheaper than Bria Lab: fast and clean, the nurse speaks excellent English, prices can be checked in advance on LINE; results the same day, B12 the next day.
A coffee shop in a Vintage Beach Club style with a vintage clothing store, accessories and a barbershop; behind Rajabhat University, Soi 1, Thanon Muen Dam Phra Khot; parking available.

A large music festival: 20+ stages and 40+ Thai artists (Jeff Satur, Three Man Down, Slot Machine, Big Ass, Potato, Polycat and others); tickets through AllTicket (Counter Service at 7-Eleven) and Ticketier.
items.a: Royal Train Garden Resort, Hang Dong

items.n: Elephant Jungle Sanctuary Chiang Mai (Grand Canyon Branch)
items.d: A one-hour Feed Me program at Elephant Jungle Café near Grand Canyon: feeding elephants (3 baskets), a workshop on making paper from dung, no riding and no shows; Feed & Shower available; free transfer, 5 km from the Old City.
items.h: sessions at 10:00 and 14:00; book at least 2 hours ahead

items.d: A bright, calm café in Chang Khlan (Pa Phao Road Soi 9): specialty coffee, breakfasts and brunches, homemade pastries; the French toast is especially praised; suitable for working; Google rating 4,9.
A wellness center in Hang Dong before the Mantana village: sauna, saltwater pool and ice bath; promotion until 31 August 2026 — 590 baht for two, booking in advance.

items.n: “Regular sweetness” in coffee shops is now 50% less sweet
items.d: Since 11 February 2026, on the Ministry of Public Health’s initiative, Normal Sweetness at Café Amazon, All Café, Black Canyon, Inthanin, Punthai, Chao Doi and others means about 50% less sugar; for sweeter drinks, order 75% or 100%.
A good breakfast place in Hang Dong: good coffee, cakes can be ordered, no trans fats are used; when it is busy, orders can take a long time.

items.n: Massage chairs at gas stations on long drives
items.d: Thai gas stations have massage chairs that work the calves and back; on a long car trip (for example, from the sea to Chiang Mai in one day) this quickly relieves tiredness.
A night safari; the author advises comparing ticket prices on Klook and Agoda before buying, as they differ noticeably.

A pizzeria at 33 Nimman Soi 5 (since June 2025): dough fermented 24 hours on live sourdough, the first in Chiang Mai with AVPN recognition; the Margherita, Spicy Calabrian, fried burrata, arancini and tiramisu are praised.
items.p: average bill 400–600 baht per person; pizzas from roughly 295 baht, tiramisu 250 baht

items.d: A hidden cocktail bar on the 2nd floor of the Kiti Panit teak mansion (around 1888) on Tha Phae Road: cocktails made from northern ingredients — mountain tea, corn, jasmine rice; a calm, intimate atmosphere, the signature CORN.
One of the best-known natural textile studios in Chiang Mai, combining traditional Lanna dyeing with contemporary textile art; a gallery and workshops.
Traditional northern Thai celadon ceramics: they show the whole production process from shaping to glazing and run painting and decorating workshops.
The best-known art café in town: you pick a canvas and a subject from dozens of options and paint as much as you like; no experience needed. Recommended for just trying out painting.
A café where you can combine coffee and painting; suitable for a calm creative evening.
A studio with a huge choice of workshops: acrylic, textured painting, alcohol ink, figurine painting, rug and mirror tufting in one day, epoxy resin, interior and seasonal decor.
An art workshop in the Old City with drawing and painting classes; recommended for those who want to learn seriously.
A modern studio with painting classes and original workshops.
A small studio and gallery of a local artist where you can take an individual drawing lesson.
One of the largest art studios in the city: regular classes in watercolor, acrylic, drawing and mixed techniques, themed art evenings and workshops for adults and children.
A full-fledged art school: one-off two-hour workshops and long courses in watercolor, oil, acrylic and academic drawing.
The only gallery and teaching studio in Chiang Mai devoted entirely to watercolor; workshops for artists of any level.
A large modern creative space with regular workshops in illustration, painting, mixed techniques and contemporary art.
An art school with courses for adults and children; recommended for those who want to learn drawing seriously.
A small art school with creative classes and workshops.
Primarily a children's art school, with family classes from time to time.
A small creative space in Nimman with various art workshops, including painting and decorative techniques.
An art center with classes in watercolor, oil, graphics and printmaking techniques.
A fragrance lab with professional perfumers: your own perfume from 150+ components, soy wax candles, diffusers, room sprays, herbal inhalers, balms, soap and a full perfumery course.
An atmospheric space with small workshops on making essential oils, blending tea mixes and flower arrangements.
A workshop on making scented bath bombs with a choice of color, scent, flower components and decoration; suitable for children and beginners.
A small creative studio that regularly holds workshops on creating your own perfume together with the founder of Artistic Lab.
A large handicraft festival (“Sew, embroider, knit”) at Jing Jai Market several times a year: materials and dozens of workshops — knitting, embroidery, tufting, jewelry, felt, bags, Murano glass.
A creative community in the Wua Lai area: regular classes in knitting, textile techniques, sewing, embroidery, clothing repair and crafts, and knitting meetups.
A modern crafting space with original DIY workshops: accessories, textile decor, seasonal projects.
Polymer clay workshops: bag charms, rings, earrings, magnets and other accessories that can be taken home right after the class.
Regular workshops on traditional crafts: paper art, textiles, decorative items; the program changes through the year.
The studio holds workshops on weaving wall hangings, plant hangers and bags in the macramé technique; dates are announced separately on social media.
They teach how to restore broken ceramics using the Japanese kintsugi technique with lacquer and gold powder; workshops are held regularly, in small groups.
One of the favorite ceramics studios of locals and expats: hand building, the potter's wheel, glazing, the Japanese nerikomi technique; one-off classes for beginners are available.
A studio of bright original ceramics: you can shape and paint figurative pieces — fox bowls, avocados, piglets; one-off classes for beginners are available.
An atmospheric studio near Chiang Mai University: individual classes in hand building, the potter's wheel and ceramic sculpture; you can combine drawing and clay.
A small art studio in Baan Kang Wat with original workshops on making teapots, cups and other ceramic pieces.
One of the oldest ceramics workshops in Chiang Mai in the celadon tradition; primarily a gallery and production site, with demonstrations and classes from time to time.
A small family pottery workshop in Hang Dong with cozy workshops for small groups.
A small local studio where you can try hand building and make your own mug, plate or vase.
The best-known chocolate workshop in the city, right at the production site: bean-to-bar, tasting of Thai chocolate, you make the bars yourself and take them home; suitable for beginners.
A chocolate farm not far from Chiang Mai with a Tree to Bar workshop: a walk through the cacao plantation, roasting, grinding, tempering, your own bar and a tasting.
Professional multi-day Tree to Bar courses — from harvesting and fermenting cacao to tempering and packaging your own chocolate; groups are formed as they fill, check the dates in advance.
A park devoted to making eco-friendly paper: an interactive tour of the whole process and a workshop where you can make paper, a postcard, a notebook, a bookmark or a picture.
An art space among gardens in Mae Rim: classes in handmade paper, notebooks, botanical printing, collage; there is an art café, an exhibition space and a shop of local makers' products.
One of the best bookbinding workshops: you can sew a notebook, planner or sketchbook and choose the paper, thread and cover yourself; short workshops and in-depth courses.
An art café, gallery and workshop by Tha Phae Gate: DIY workshops (collage, scrapbooking, zines, soap, perfume, cyanotype), exhibitions and weekly meetups; book places via direct messages.
A small original workshop of beautiful books, notebooks and paper goods in Baan Kang Wat: sells handmade items and holds workshops on a schedule.
A workshop of original notebooks, zines and handmade paper goods; holds bookbinding workshops through the year, dates are published as groups fill.
Off-site workshops by Amara Soap Making Class at Attika Studio on Sundays in August 2026 (2, 9, 16, 30): body and face soap, shampoos, scrubs, themes change.
A quiet space for work and reading: a workspace, a library in Thai and English, unlimited coffee, tea and water, fast Wi-Fi; holds YIM Conversations meetups about the culture and life of Chiang Mai.
A workshop in Hang Dong with 15+ years of experience working with leather: workshops for beginners — a wallet, a card holder, a key holder; all materials and tools included.

A brand from Chiang Rai with hand-painted ceramics and original characters (matcha bowls, mugs, bowls); in Chiang Mai — on weekends at Jing Jai Market, Objects of Desire Store (3rd floor); takes Made to Order requests on Instagram.

A craft center by the Silver Temple (Wat Sri Suphan): you stamp a ring, bracelet or key ring from aluminum or copper yourself; artisans with hearing impairments work here, and the project supports the Wua Lai neighborhood.
items.a: Wua Lai, near Wat Sri Suphan
items.p: aluminium ring/bracelet/keychain — 50 baht; copper ring — 70 baht; copper bracelet — 110 baht

items.d: A small studio in the Old City: workshops on making jewelry from real silver — rings, couple rings, pendants; materials included, small groups, suitable for beginners.
A one-day jewelry course of about 6 hours: sawing, shaping, soldering, sanding and polishing a silver ring or pendant to your own sketch.
items.p: 3 500 baht, silver paid separately by weight

items.d: Rental of whole private estates for retreats, weddings, celebrations and groups: Wat Ket (8 bedrooms, a pool), Tha Phae by the gate, Riverside on the Ping River, Pa Tan; private dinners, massages, a concierge.
items.p: no fixed price list, cost on individual request

items.d: A studio and creative community: turns the work of local artists into original prints, organizes exhibitions, holds printmaking and cyanotype workshops, takes part in Chiang Mai Design Week.
Halo House workshops on cyanotype on fabric (plant prints made with sunlight) at MUJI Chiang Mai every Saturday in August 2026.
A public space in the MUJI store (1st floor of Central Chiangmai Airport): a new monthly program of free and paid workshops, exhibitions, meetings with artists and markets of local brands.

items.n: Block Print by Days in and Days Out
items.d: A free workshop on hand printing on fabric with stamps at Open MUJI every Wednesday in August 2026; registration via Google Form, age 16+, arrive 10 minutes early, cancellation 24 hours ahead.
A market of contemporary crafts of Northern Thailand at Open MUJI from August 1 to 31, 2026: clothing with embroidery and natural dyeing, textiles, candles, screen printing.
A local brand of clothing and jewelry with hand embroidery and natural dyeing; a participant of the Artisan Living market at Open MUJI.
A local brand of handmade cotton textiles with natural dyes; a participant of the Artisan Living market at Open MUJI.
A local brand of handmade scented candles, perfume and interior items; a participant of the Artisan Living market at Open MUJI.
A local brand of textiles dyed with natural dyes and mineral pigments; a participant of the Artisan Living market at Open MUJI.
Clothing and home textiles created together with local artisans and ethnic communities; a participant of the Artisan Living market at Open MUJI.
A studio of original screen printing (Silk Screen); a participant of the Artisan Living market at Open MUJI.
Contemporary clothing using natural fabric dyeing; a participant of the Artisan Living market at Open MUJI.
A brand of original fabrics and hand-printed items; holds free Block Print workshops at Open MUJI and takes part in the Artisan Living market.

A soap-making school since 2016 (114/109 Moo Baan Pikul Thong, Mae Hia, 5–10 minutes from the airport): 14 programs from a kids' class to a professional course — Melt & Pour and Cold Process soap, shampoos, scrubs; materials included.
items.p: from 650 baht (Melt & Pour, 1 hour) to 6 000 baht (full professional day course)

items.d: A “sawmill” restaurant by Tha Phae Gate across from Bangkok Bank: Lanna dishes, grill, Moo Jum hot pot, cocktails; live music in the evenings, a green courtyard and terrace, a big choice of vegetarian dishes.
items.a: Old City, by Tha Phae Gate

items.d: A Thai restaurant by the Windows team on the grounds of the boutique hotel SELA Chiang Mai (519 Moo 7, Nam Phrae): khao soi, Hang Lay curry, wagyu dishes; open to everyone, it is better to book a table.
A European restaurant in the boutique hotel complex SELA Chiang Mai in Hang Dong; the same team opened the Thai restaurant SUTHI next door.
A restaurant on the ground floor of the restored Kiti Panit teak mansion from the late 19th century on Tha Phae Road; many people have dinner here first and then go up to the North Country bar.
A studio of scented paper flowers in Chang Moi (41/1 Taiwang Road): you can assemble a bouquet yourself, there are workshops under an hour, flower boxes and gift sets; rating 5.0 with ~645 reviews.

A family resort: rooms with a jacuzzi, grill and shower on the roof, slides in the pool, bicycles, mini golf, tennis, billiards, a cook who prepares food to order; a lake with lotuses nearby. Caution: there is sharp grit on the pool steps.
items.p: about 1700 baht for 70 m² with breakfasts

items.d: A lake with lotuses and boat rides.
A beach with coral cliffs: after the temple you need to park and walk along a trail for about 800 meters.
A coffee shop with food on the way toward the military beach.
A coffee shop from a list of places in Prachuap Khiri Khan.
Another coffee shop from a list of places in Prachuap Khiri Khan.
A coffee shop on a colorful little street on the way to Ao Manao, where the coffee is made by a charismatic elderly owner.
The owner bakes cheesecakes, biscotti and other desserts herself and will suggest which wine goes with which pastry; on the little street on the way to Ao Manao.
A boutique hotel with breakfasts and a café in an interesting old Thai house, the owner is the elegant June; you can drop in to rest. On the little street on the way to Ao Manao.
A park with monkeys from a list of places in Prachuap Khiri Khan.
A gathering point for farangs from the neighboring hotels: hammocks for kids, understandable European food, fresh fish, a very pleasant owner.
The best coffee and food worth its money (especially the rice in a pineapple), aesthetic design; sometimes it is crowded and you have to wait. A market, Lotus's and a car wash are nearby.
One of the author's favorite places — it is simply very beautiful.

items.n: Chicken and Bee : Good Food and Organic Farm
items.d: Tasty organic food, spacious, dogs are welcome.

items.n: Prachuap Khiri Khan: impressions, pros and cons
items.d: Few people, lots of nature, mountains and sea, half-empty embankments, pleasant housing prices. Cons: many dogs (sometimes aggressive), jellyfish — after a sting rinse with sea water or vinegar, not fresh water; Ao Manao is safer; strong winds.

items.n: English Corner at Much Room Cafe
items.d: A weekly English conversation club (already 4 years): friendly chat on a set topic with participants from different countries. Free for native English speakers, the organizers treat them to coffee.

items.n: Chiang Mai Zoo (สวนสัตว์เชียงใหม่)
items.d: On weekends and holidays at the zoo you can brush capybaras and scratch their bellies under staff supervision. Daily feeding of capybaras 10:00–12:00, deer 10:00–15:00, elephants 13:00–15:00; penguins and lemurs by appointment.
items.h: capybaras: Sat, Sun and public holidays; capybara feeding 10:00–12:00, deer 10:00–15:00, elephants 13:00–15:00

items.d: Muk, a student, cleans homes personally and takes 1–2 orders a day: living room, bedroom, bathroom, kitchen, balcony, windows from the inside, dust, vacuuming, floors; cleaning products included. Not included: windows from the outside, mold, heavy furniture, difficult stains.
items.p: 2 hours — 350 baht; 4 hours — 550 baht; 6 hours — 700 baht

items.d: Branch 1 of the NJ Durian chain of durian shops (6 branches in total) in Hang Dong; on the day of the post there was a promotion: ripe durian at 75 baht/kg.

items.n: ร้านทุเรียนเสี่ยนิวNJสาขา2สันทราย
items.d: Branch 2 of the NJ Durian chain of durian shops in San Sai; on the day of the post, a promotion at 75 baht/kg.

items.n: ร้านทุเรียนเสี่ยนิวNJสาขาสามแยกสันป่าตอง
items.d: Branch 3 of the NJ Durian chain of durian shops in San Pa Tong; on the day of the post, a promotion at 75 baht/kg.

items.n: ทุเรียนเสี่ยนิวNJ สาขา แม่ริม ( Durian Sian New NJ Mae Rim )
items.d: Branch 4 of the NJ Durian chain of durian shops in Mae Rim; on the day of the post, a promotion at 75 baht/kg.

items.n: Traditional Thai desserts: vegan and gluten-free
items.d: Khanom Tom, Lod Chong, Khanom Sai Sai and Bua Loi are made from rice and tapioca flour, coconut, palm sugar and pandan; the classic recipes are usually vegan, gluten-free and oil-free, but it is worth checking additions in cafes.
A venue hosting an Indian curry evening (naan, curry, onion bhajis, beer, bhangra, candlelit tables); there is space for kids to run and play.

The hospital’s cardiology center implanted a leadless pacemaker through the femoral vein (the second case in Northern Thailand). Such an operation is not covered by state insurance (NHSO, Social Security) and is paid for separately.
The Fish Cave Temple, 15 km from Mae Sai: a spring with sacred mahseer fish (you can feed them), the moss-covered Nine Spires Pagoda, nine caves and a colony of Assamese macaques.

A meetup of dogs and owners at Keo Park: consultations with dog trainer Owen (Dog Leader Academy, 16+ years of experience), a photo shoot by Lek (Hidden Street), a sunset walk with views of Doi Suthep and a prize draw. The date is not given in the post.

items.n: HIV in Chiang Mai and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP)
items.d: The province has almost 24 thousand people with HIV and about 700 new cases a year. HIV is not transmitted through everyday contact; after a risky exposure PEP must be started within 72 hours, and it is available at large hospitals and specialized clinics.

items.n: Entry refusal: what to prepare for immigration
items.d: A Russian citizen was refused entry at Chiang Mai airport under Section 12(2) for unconfirmed funds and an unclear purpose of travel. It is worth having proof of funds, a return ticket, an accommodation booking and a clear plan; the decision always rests with the officer.
A handyman recommended several times in a moms’ group: repairs, installation, household work during a move. Friendly, hardworking, looks for cheaper solutions.

items.n: Shop-café with a French atmosphere in Nimman (name not given)
items.d: A new small café-shop: homemade French-Mediterranean vegetarian food, superfood smoothies, organic coffee, vintage clothes and decor, yoga goods, and items made from hill tribe embroidery and kimonos.
A cozy guesthouse run by the owners of the French café-shop in Nimman, in the Mae Taeng area, for a quiet stay in nature.

items.n: Driving from Chiang Mai to Prachuap Khiri Khan
items.d: About 1000 km, doable in a day (faster than to Koh Chang, as there is no ferry). The Hua Hin direction offers space, bikes and national parks. To make it to Wat Chantharam on the way, leave at 7–8 in the morning.
A restaurant on the way with a lot of fresh greenery; next to it is a hangar with groceries where you can buy something for the road.
items.a: on the way from Chiang Mai to Prachuap Khiri Khan

items.d: A beautiful mirror temple with a huge territory and a very budget canteen. It has a peculiar schedule: closed at lunchtime, then open from 14:00 to 16:00; at exactly 16:00 the lights go off and the gates close.
A hotel with a coconut farm just past Bangkok, a convenient overnight stop on the way south; the room cost about 900 baht.

items.s: coffee shop on a coconut farm
items.d: A coffee shop near the Coco and Canal hotel, opens early; it sells very tasty young coconut puree, a jar costs 40 baht.

A floating market: a boat costs about 1000 baht for 40 minutes (in the morning, when there are few people, you can bargain), and coconut sugar evaporation is demonstrated. Lots of souvenirs and touts, little authenticity; the sanitation of the cafes by the canals is questionable.
A market right on the tracks, through which a train passes. Very crowded, with parking difficulties.

items.n: ข้าวทุ่งเบ็ญจาโฮมสเตย์
items.d: A homestay before Bangkok with rice fields, a mini water park and lots of birds, an option for an overnight stop on the way south.

items.n: Kamphaeng Phet Historical Park อุทยานประวัติศาสตร์กำแพงเพชร
items.d: A historical park that can be visited on the way south if you are not in a hurry and stop overnight before Bangkok.

items.n: Lapassarin Zab cafe (ละพัดสะริน แซ่บ คาเฟ่)
items.d: A cafe after the mirror temple: the food is tasty, ordering through an AI translator was no problem, and the portions are big.
items.a: near the Mirror Temple, Wat Chantharam

items.d: A bistro in Cha-am where breakfast was very tasty; the beach is three minutes on foot.
A coffee shop not far from HiDE BISTRO in Cha-am with excellent coffee and wonderful desserts.

Spacious two-room units with a kitchen, a pool shared by several units, breakfasts included (a 7-year-old child free), bicycles, a good restaurant. Empty beaches nearby, and a beach market on Saturday evenings.

items.n: What to see in Prachuap Khiri Khan province
items.d: An underrated province without crowds: Ao Manao beach, the Wat Khao Chong Krachok viewpoint, the Phraya Nakhon and Wat Ao Noi caves, wild elephants in Kui Buri, Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park, the waterfront and Walking Street, Pran Buri Forest Park.
One of the best beaches in the province: calm sea, a clean wide beach, pines instead of palms, few people. It is on an air base territory, entry is free.
The best-known viewpoint in the city: 396 steps, a temple on the summit and a panorama of three bays. Lots of cheeky monkeys, so do not hold food or bags in your hands.

items.n: Wat Klong Wan Phra Aram Luang
items.d: A beautiful royal temple by the sea, calm, with no tourist buses.
An unusual temple with a long staircase and a large limestone cave with a reclining Buddha; the atmosphere of the cave is especially praised.
The best place in Thailand to see wild elephants, as well as gaur, deer and birds; the best time is after 15:00.
The most famous cave in Thailand with a small royal pavilion lit by a ray of sun through an opening in the ceiling. Reached on foot or by boat with a short hike.
One of the best viewpoints in Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park: limestone mountains, mangrove forests and the sea; very beautiful at dawn.

items.n: Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park
items.d: The main natural attraction of the province: mountains, caves, marshes, mangroves, beaches and rare birds; it is better to set aside at least a day.
A pier from which boats leave for the caves, through the mangroves and on national park excursions.

items.n: Khao Ta Mong Lai Forest Park
items.d: A viewpoint almost unknown to tourists with beautiful views of the coast and sunsets.
A cozy waterfront with fishing boats, cafes, bike paths, evening markets and great sunsets.
A weekend street market: seafood, Thai food, souvenirs, live music; highly rated by locals.
A photogenic park: an easy mangrove trail of about 1 km on wooden walkways, a viewpoint with a crocodile, birds and crabs, views of the river and the coast; there are usually few people.

items.n: Yoga in the Park Chiang Mai
items.d: Free morning classes by a volunteer community on the lawn between the ponds by the playground in Buak Haad park: vinyasa, Lanna martial arts, kundalini, power yoga. A mat can be rented for 20 baht.
On the ground floor there is a jazz bar with live music.
Update: a subscriber went to the exhibition center and it was empty, with no signs or any sign of an exhibition; apparently the announcement was inaccurate or the event was postponed or canceled.

items.n: No paid fast track at passport control in Suvarnabhumi
items.d: Suvarnabhumi airport stated that there are no paid services for faster passport control; offers of priority passage for money are a scam.

items.n: Chiang Mai — Nan flights by Ezy Airlines
items.d: Ezy Airlines plans Chiang Mai — Nan flights from November 2026 on a 12-seat Cessna Grand Caravan (about 50 minutes). Right now the road takes 5–6 hours, and GreenBus buses run 3–4 times a day for 430–450 baht.
A free bus route around the Old City along the moat. Boarding at exit 1B next to Starbucks in Central Chiangmai Airport.
items.h: Fri, Sat, Sun and public holidays; departures at 11:00, 15:00, 18:00

items.d: The hospital has started endoscopic spine surgery for disc herniation and nerve root compression (an incision of about 1 cm, fast recovery); the operations are performed by neurosurgeon Dr. Nithipat Durongwattana, with the decision made after an examination and MRI.

A regular halal street food fair (20+ stalls with certified food) at Icon Park Hotel, 310 Manee Nopparat Road near the Old City. July–October 2026 on the last Friday of the month, November 2026 – February 2027 every Friday.
items.a: Icon Park Hotel Chiang Mai, Manee Nopparat Road
items.h: July–October: last Friday of the month; November–February: every Friday

items.d: A Thai brand of very soft and light flip-flops that tire the feet less. Stores: One Nimman (2nd floor), MAYA (4th floor), Nimman Soi 5, Nimman Craft Soi 9, Chiang Mai Premium Outlet; also an official store on Lazada.
items.a: Nimman, MAYA, Chiang Mai Premium Outlet (Hang Dong)
items.p: usually 330–550 baht, 200–300 baht at the outlet on sale

items.d: The Silver Temple: women may not enter only the main silver ubosot (a Lanna tradition); the rest of the grounds, the museum and the workshops are open to everyone. A ticket is 50 baht for everyone; a monk may offer to teach meditation for free.
A new café in a vintage glass greenhouse: a high glass ceiling, antique furniture, lots of plants and natural light. Good for coffee and working on a laptop.
items.a: Chang Phueak, Canal Road (Keep in Touch)

items.d: A bar hidden inside the Nimman Mai Design Hotel (1st floor); it holds DJ nights and themed parties.
An unusual temple with colorful statues of Chinese deities and guardians; locals pray for well-being and luck, and there are few tourists.
A morning of drawing by Wat Chedi Luang: you can come with your own notebook.
The fourth Chiang Mai film festival (theme Local in Motion) at TCDC: more than 50 short and documentary films, meetings with directors, discussions. Entry is free.

items.n: Deli shop with homemade ham (name not given)
items.d: A shop with its own homemade ham and dishes of the week (cordon bleu, chorizo burger, steak and ale pie, chicken madras). New customers get −10% in the shop, on Fridays −10% from 350 baht on pickup.

items.n: Ban Mae Lek route: cliffs and caves in Lamphun
items.d: An eco-route 1–1.5 hours from Chiang Mai: the Pha Daeng viewpoint (360°), the Tham Tho, Tham Makok and Tham Cham Ma Fa caves, a copy of the Golden Rock. You need a flashlight, shoes with good tread and gloves; going on your own is not recommended.
A center for traditional handmade Lamphun brocade silk, used for ceremonial clothing of the royal family; the Ban Mae Lek hike usually starts here.

items.n: Unpaid traffic fines and the tax sticker
items.d: From August 1, 2026 the police pass fine data to the DLT: with an unpaid fine you can pay the tax, but the Tax Sticker is not issued (only a temporary one for 30 days) until the fine is paid. Applies to cars and motorcycles, including those of foreigners.
A hotel near Nimman and MAYA sells a Day Pass for 290 baht: gym, pool and one drink of your choice, alcoholic ones included.
An indoor play center on the 4th floor of Central Chiangmai Airport by Major Cineplex: a multi-level maze, slides, trampolines, ball pits, areas for toddlers. Prices depend on age, day and time.
items.h: Mall: Mon–Fri 11:00–21:00, Sat–Sun and public holidays 10:00–21:00

items.d: A concept cocktail bar inspired by the philosophy of Michel Foucault, literature and postmodernism.
A secret bar behind a bookcase, with a menu inspired by the John Wick films.
A cocktail bar experimenting with umami flavor and salty notes.
A cocktail bar where the drinks are inspired by the Pantone palette.
A cocktail bar that regularly holds jazz nights.
A cocktail bar with an intimate atmosphere from a selection of 16 Chiang Mai bars.

items.n: Eiiga Pass: Chiang Mai discount card
items.d: A tourist e-card for 199 baht gives discounts and special offers at partner bars, cafes, restaurants and other places; it is issued on the website, then shown at the venues.

items.n: Yuen Nueng (ยืนหนึ่ง)
items.d: A restaurant where Thais have been queuing for about two years: fresh meat and seafood, signature sauces, fast service, a spacious open terrace. For 359 baht, a wide choice of ingredients.
An elephant park mentioned in the channel only with a map link.
A Thomas the Tank Engine train takes children around the mall on the 4th floor of Central Chiangmai Airport; departures every 20 minutes.
items.h: Fri 13:00–20:00; Sat, Sun and public holidays 12:00–20:00; break 14:20–15:10

items.d: A garden and lawn maintenance company for private homes and commercial grounds: mowing, spraying against weeds and pests, topdressing, aeration, dethatching, installing tree supports.
One more jack-of-all-trades: judging by the post's hashtags, repairs and construction, plumbing, electrics, internet, metalwork.
Chicago thin-crust tavern-style pizza, cut into squares. Lunch offer: a 9-inch pizza and a drink for 239 baht, promo code LUNCH on the website gives −10%; available on Grab.

items.n: Free meditation at Layla Garden Yoga
items.d: Every Wednesday Layla Garden Yoga holds a free meditation from 19:00 to 20:15, booking through online booking.

The artist John's labyrinth house: tree roots through the walls, narrow passages, drawings everywhere. The gallery is now kept by his son Ken, who sells his father's works and postcards; open every day from 13:00.

items.n: Vegan khao soi for 40 baht (name not given)
items.d: Vegan khao soi for 40 baht, may run out by 12 noon; the post gives no name, only a map link.

items.n: Free yoga in Nong Buak Haad Park
items.d: Free classes on the grass by the playground between the ponds, Mon–Sat with different teachers (hatha, vinyasa, kundalini, power yoga, Lanna martial arts). A mat can be rented for 20 baht; there is a WhatsApp group.

items.n: Wood carving and painting workshops (name not given)
items.d: A place you can come to on your own (in addition to the Baan Tawai tour) and take any workshop: paint a wooden figurine with the kids or try wood carving.

A CrossFit and HYROX gym in Mae Hia near the airport: workouts for any level, weightlifting, a group for children aged 9–13, Open Gym. The coaches and the international community are praised; booking through an app.
items.p: unlimited 3 900 baht/month; 10 workouts — 3 500; single — 600; Open Gym 2 000/month or 400/day

items.n: Free sparring at Suthep Municipal Stadium
items.d: Open, light, friendly sparring for any level on Tuesdays and Thursdays. You need a mouthguard (required), shoes and hand wraps; 14–16 oz gloves can be lent. Questions go to Ben.
A museum in the Mae On area (40–50 minutes from the center) with exhibitions of contemporary Thai artists, gardens, beautiful architecture and a cafe. Entry to the main exhibitions is free.

items.n: HOM BOON 3: Art for Life Charity Auction 2026
items.d: 59 works by 51 artists: exhibition on August 10–16, final auction on August 16 at Chiangmai Honda Automobil. Part of the proceeds will go to the Maharaj Nakorn Chiang Mai and Suan Prung hospitals.

A shop of the old silk house founded by a former pilot, on the ground floor of Central diagonally across from Zara; during the sale season you can buy very cheaply. There is a “secret” shop on the grounds of Anantara and an outlet in Bangkok.
items.p: very cheap in the sale season

items.d: An art cafe that held workshops in January (the schedule was in the post's picture).

items.n: Checks on companies with Thai nominees
items.d: In Chiang Mai an operation is under way against companies and land registered to Thai nominee owners; since April 2026 company registration has been tightened, and the DBD uses the AI system IBAS. Foreigners living legally are not affected.

A small cafe on Huay Kaew Road with a green courtyard: toast, sandwiches, coffee, smoothies and fresh juice, light breakfasts. The atmosphere, fruit drinks and garden are praised; parking along the street.

items.n: Khao Soi Lung Prakit Kad Kom
items.d: The most frequent answer from Thais to the question about the best khao soi: a classic where both locals and long-time Chiang Mai residents go.
Despite the name (kanom jeen), Thais especially recommend the khao soi here.
A small family cafe in San Pa Tong that Thais themselves recommended several times, although it has few reviews on Google Maps.
One of the oldest and best-known khao soi places in the city.

items.d: Khao soi and nam ngiao, run by a local couple; spicy, rather touristy, almost 1 thousand reviews with a rating of 5.

A volunteer program in Thailand (through Worldpackers): helping schoolchildren with English, immersion in local community life; accommodation, meals and group activities included.

items.n: Daily AirAsia flights Chiang Mai — Hua Hin
items.d: From October 25, 2026 AirAsia flies Chiang Mai — Hua Hin daily (7 flights a week).
One of the best-known shops in Chiang Mai: natural cotton, linen, hand dyeing, clothes, bags and home textiles.
A small shop of organic-fabric clothing in a minimalist style.

A school from kindergarten to high school with the Play | Think | Create concept; a huge campus, its own park, many projects, more suited to bilingual children. A couple of years ago ~14–15 thousand baht a month; programs 80/20 or 90/10 English, and cheaper 50/50; discount for a second child.
items.p: about 14–15 thousand baht a month (at prices from a couple of years ago)

items.d: An eco-friendly clothing brand made of cotton, linen and natural fabrics with minimalist design; there are women’s and kids’ collections. Outlets at Jing Jai Market and in Nimman.

items.n: How to learn to ride a motorbike and get a Thai driving licence
items.d: A review of motorbike schools in Chiang Mai. Beginners are advised to start with basic skills at a motorbike school (Changphuak, KW or Teacher Joe), then take a course at Honda Safety Riding Park, then get the Thai licence.
The best-known safe driving centre: official Honda courses, preparation for the Thai licence, an enclosed training ground. Complete beginners may be asked to master the basics first.
items.p: Course (1 day, 6 h) — 500 baht; Pre-Riding (2 days, 12 h) — 2 000 baht; Pre-Clutch (2 days, 12 h) — 2 000 baht
