A simple cosmetology clinic with low prices; people note quality skincare and facial cleansing.
A shop of second-hand goods from Japan: hand tools, stainless steel kitchenware, toys, bags, shoes, camping and home goods. New deliveries arrive regularly.
American cuisine: burgers, steaks, pizza, pasta and big portions. Recommended by Mae Hia residents for ordering through GrabFood.
An Italian restaurant with sourdough pizza; a set menu for two of 5 items (salad, main course, pizza, dessert, 2 drinks) for 899 baht, delivery available.
items.p: discount on any pizza from 17:00 to 18:00

items.d: A European bakery with cozy pastries and croissants; in the Christmas season — desserts and hot chocolate, suitable for a family break.
Sandwiches, fresh bread, cold cuts, cheeses and wines. Recommended by Mae Hia residents for ordering through GrabFood.
Pizza and European dishes. Recommended by Mae Hia residents for ordering through GrabFood.
Natural smoothies with no syrups or artificial additives: dates instead of sugar, and you can add pea protein. Recommended by Mae Hia residents for ordering through GrabFood.
A small Japanese restaurant in an old wooden house, run by a Japanese chef. Open only in the evening, almost always full — booking a table in advance is advised.
A cafe for work and relaxing: comfortable workspaces, power outlets, coffee, drinks and desserts at affordable prices.
A place next to the Carrot cafe where people suggest popping over for a chocolate to go with your coffee.

items.n: Pom Hai Ya (ป้อมหายยา)
items.d: The only surviving section of Chiang Mai's outer earthen rampart (a crescent from Ku Hueang to Sri Phum), now the quiet Pom Hai Ya Park; Taksin's troops attacked across this line in 1771. Good for walking with small children, few people.
A recently opened studio for recording podcasts, filming interviews, portrait and commercial photo shoots, Reels and other video content.

items.n: Cafe with cats and Japanese second-hand
items.s: cafe with cats and a second-hand shop
items.d: A sweet cafe with lots of cats, tasty coffee and budget prices; next to it is a Japanese second-hand shop with linen and clothes for the smallest children.
An atmospheric neighborhood along the Ping River: old wooden houses, cafés, artisan bakeries, galleries and family restaurants. It is advised to set aside at least half a day for a walk.
One of the best-known places in the area: Pak Mor (rice dumplings) and Saku Sai Moo (sago dumplings). A simple place with a local atmosphere.
A small family stall with fried pork, popular with locals.
A Japanese restaurant with creative presentation; fresh sashimi, sushi, grilled dishes, a calm interior and good service are praised.
One of the most popular Italian restaurants in the city, with fresh homemade pasta.
A small contemporary gallery that regularly holds exhibitions of local artists.
Wood-fired pizza. Recommended by Mae Hia residents for ordering through GrabFood.
Mexican food: tacos, burritos and quesadillas. Recommended by Mae Hia residents for ordering through GrabFood.
Breakfasts, coffee and fresh pastries. Recommended by Mae Hia residents for ordering through GrabFood.
Texas barbecue. Recommended by Mae Hia residents for ordering through GrabFood.
Home-style Thai food. Recommended by Mae Hia residents for ordering through GrabFood.
One of the best-known Mexican restaurants in Chiang Mai. Recommended by Mae Hia residents for ordering through GrabFood.
Filipino cuisine. Recommended by Mae Hia residents for ordering through GrabFood.
Steaks, ribs and grilled meat. Recommended by Mae Hia residents for ordering through GrabFood.
Grilled dishes and barbecue. Recommended by Mae Hia residents for ordering through GrabFood.
Japanese cuisine: sushi, sashimi and other traditional dishes. Recommended by Mae Hia residents for ordering through GrabFood.
Doughnuts, coffee and desserts. Recommended by Mae Hia residents for ordering through GrabFood.
Coffee, breakfasts and light dishes. Recommended by Mae Hia residents for ordering through GrabFood.
A popular restaurant of Northern Thai and Isan cuisine. Recommended by Mae Hia residents for ordering through GrabFood.
A family cafe with breakfasts, coffee and a varied menu; recommended by Mae Hia residents, including for ordering through GrabFood.

A restaurant of Mediterranean, European and Thai cuisine with a large bamboo playground; children's birthdays are free (venue and decoration), you pay only for food and drinks, Tue–Fri 10% discount. Google 4,3 (340+ reviews).
items.p: average bill 200–400 baht; kids’ menu 75–155 baht; pizza 175–365 baht

items.n: JOYA - Everyday Wellness (Sauna, Cold Plunge/Ice Bath, Calisthenics)
items.d: A handmade Finnish sauna, an ice bath and calisthenics; no pool.

items.n: Bliss Ice Bath & Sauna Chiang Mai
items.d: A sauna and ice baths on the 3rd floor of the building.

items.n: Vibes Chiangmai - ice bath and sauna
items.d: A modern wellness space with a Finnish sauna, ice plunge, pool, cafe and lounge area; people come to recover after workouts and socialize.

A company with a history of ~50 years: curtains, roller blinds, blinds, electric curtain rails and automation. A specialist comes for free to measure and calculates the cost with no obligation; showroom in Saraphi, visits all over Chiang Mai.

A new family space in nature: zipline, rope park, water obstacle course, suspension bridges, climbing wall; on the farm you can collect chicken and quail eggs and cook Kai Krok on charcoal. Check prices directly.

A farm with programmes for children and families: feeding and bathing dwarf buffaloes, collecting eggs and cooking Kai Pam, rice planting and a mud slide, soap making, indigo. There is a Farm Stay and they host birthdays; better to message in advance.
items.p: tour and buffalo feeding 250 baht; buffalo bathing 399 baht; workshops from 150 baht; children’s program 899 baht

items.n: Donation point by Wan Wela Cafe
items.d: Next to Wan Wela Cafe you can leave unneeded clothes, shoes and other things.

items.n: Chiang Mai – Mae Hong Son flight (EZY Airlines)
items.d: EZY Airlines is preparing a Chiang Mai – Mae Hong Son flight instead of the many-hour winding road with 1 864 curves; the Ministry of Transport also spoke of resuming flights to Pai. Test flight on July 18, 2026.
A presentation of the Tonkla international school at Central Festival: interactive exhibitions, workshops, student performances, meeting teachers and the admissions team.
A new, beautiful yoga studio in a garden; on opening day it held a free meditation meetup.

items.n: Thayan Onsen and Spa Chiang Mai
items.d: A new onsen with private and shared mineral water baths; also aromatherapy, herbal compresses, scrubs, face and body care, combined packages.
Thais, like the Chinese, consider durian a “hot” fruit that causes bloating, pimples, a dry mouth and a feeling of heat, so they “ground” it with cooling foods: mangosteen, coconut milk, watermelon.

A walk through the Wua Lai silver quarter, a visit to Wat Sri Suphan temple and a workshop, then making your own 925 silver ring at Kaparti Crafting Hub. Groups of 3–6 people, booking required; temple dress code (shoulders and knees covered).
items.a: Kaparti Crafting Hub, 12/8 Wua Lai Soi 3, Hai Ya
items.p: 3 590 baht for one person; 3 445 baht per person for two or more

items.d: A legendary place with a history of almost 100 years: traditional Thai doughnuts tue ka ko cooked on a charcoal stove (crisp outside, soft inside) and fried tofu.
The oldest shop, which moved from Anusarn market: bird’s nest soup (hot and cold), desserts, herbal drinks, chrysanthemum tea and tao suan.
Rice porridge with tender pork ribs, crispy pork, fresh spring rolls and freshly squeezed orange juice.
Famous for charcoal-grilled pork satay; also tom yum with fish, spicy soups and wok dishes.
Dim sum made to Southern Thai recipes: hakao, siumai, bao, chicken feet, fish maw soup in red sauce.

items.n: Karaoke bar scams: how to avoid a huge bill
items.d: After a British tourist’s complaint about almost 150 000 baht charged at a karaoke venue: check the bill, do not let your card out of sight, keep receipts and notifications, check reviews on maps; in a dispute, call the Tourist Police 1155. Beware of tuk-tuks that take you to a particular venue.
A vegan restaurant with Wafū Edition pop-up dinners: a chef’s set combining Italian techniques, Japanese flavours and seasonal Chiang Mai produce. Booking through LINE.

items.n: Fun & Learn Chiang Mai — Weekend Camp
items.d: A monthly camp for children aged 6–14 in different places in the North: Doi Inthanon, rock climbing in Mae On, survival in Ob Khan, a cave in Samoeng, SUP in Chiang Dao, a rope park in Mae Rim. Meals, accommodation, insurance and equipment included.
items.h: once a month on weekends: 18–19 July, 28–29 August, 26–27 September, 31 October–1 November, 28–29 November, 12–13 December

items.d: A cozy izakaya by Tha Phae Gate with Osaka kushikatsu (breaded skewers), tasty grilled eggplant and homemade Japanese curry; there is a separate room for get-togethers. First 2 hours free at the partner parking.

items.n: Visa-free stay cut from 60 to 30 days
items.d: On July 14, 2026 the cabinet cancelled the 60-day visa exemption: 30 days for 59 countries, and for Russian citizens the visa exemption is cut to 30 days. It takes effect 15 days after publication in the Royal Gazette; to stay longer than a month, a TR tourist visa (60 days) through e-Visa or a DTV.

items.n: Thai nominee owners: possible tougher penalties
items.d: AMLO is preparing amendments to equate the use of Thai nominees with money laundering (freezing and confiscation of assets); for now it is only a bill. It does not affect those who rent housing, live on a visa and do not use nominee schemes.

Its own production of old teak and rattan furniture with a showroom: ready-made furniture and made to order, retail and wholesale, delivery all over Thailand, lifting and installation, warranty up to 3 months, discount for self-pickup. 40–45 minutes from Chiang Mai.

items.n: J.Jaan Chiang Mai (จ.จาน เชียงใหม่)
items.d: A huge warehouse shop with thousands of items: ceramic tableware, planters and pots, terracotta, decorative animals, naga statues, fountains, vases, incense and candles for altars. Easy to spend a couple of hours.
Handwoven cotton textiles directly from the makers: mats, pillowcases, Tote Bag bags and large rugs; a good option for home or a gift. Order by phone, LINE or Instagram.
items.p: mats 300–680 baht; pillowcases 390–450 baht; rugs 1 490–2 250 baht; Tote Bag 500 baht

items.d: A temple under construction since 2006, in Lanna, Shan and Burmese styles; a giant by the staircase in Converse sneakers, a well-known statue of Kruba Srivichai and a huge Maitreya Buddha. In June 2024 a fire damaged the ubosot, restoration is under way.

items.n: Rice terraces of Ban Pa Bong Piang
items.d: Picturesque rice terraces in Mae Chaem district, beautiful even on an overcast, rainy day; link to photos by Wachira Thomas.

items.n: Lazada finds for a room: mirror, basket, chair
items.d: A budget upgrade of a room corner in a minimalist Japanese style: a narrow mirror (hang or stand it), a tall basket and a comfortable chair (swivel or regular) from Lazada.
A recommendation for smoked paprika from Lazada: it instantly gives dishes a bright flavor.

items.n: Sugar-free fruit jam (made with grape and date juice)
items.d: Jam with interesting flavors (cherry, apricot, raspberry, black currant, grape), sweetened with grape and date juice concentrates, with pectin and lemon juice. Available on Lazada, at Tops and at Rimping.

A small craft incense workshop using documented raw materials (Thai agarwood, Omani Hojari frankincense, sandalwood, vetiver, saffron, Damask rose); the maker develops the recipes himself and sends orders personally.

An aromatherapy supplies shop opposite CMU: you can learn to make a scented candle for free by buying the materials (100+ scents, molds, containers, decor). Also diffusers, humidifiers and essential oils.
items.p: teaching is free, you pay only for materials

items.d: A floral studio with bouquet workshops (by prior booking), bouquets and arrangements for any budget. Two branches: near the airport (by the Bangchak gas station) and near Dara Academy/Prince Royal’s College and McCormick; Grab delivery, free within 2 km.
items.a: by the airport; by Prince Royal’s College

items.d: A spa with a thermal complex (Thermal Wellness, therapeutic pools) and Lanna massage techniques; a promotion gives 50% off a second spa package.
items.p: spa treatments from 600 baht; Thermal Wellness Day Pass 600 baht

items.d: The H&M site has a bigger choice than offline and regular promotions (about once a week): around 30% off from ~3500 baht and 15% from ~1500 baht. A selection of natural-fabric items for the heat; cotton items on sale can be cheaper than polyester ones.
items.p: regular promo: ~30% off ~3500 baht, ~15% off ~1500 baht

items.d: A place the author recommends just from the photo: “no need to write anything”; there is a booking link.
A traditional free meeting: warm-up and stretching, instructions, two 15-minute meditation sessions, a talk and questions. Led by a Zen practitioner since 1971 (student, then monk).

items.n: Ban Rak Thai in the rainy season
items.d: A rainy-season trip idea to the Chinese village of Ban Rak Thai (5–6 hours from Chiang Mai): mists, tea plantations, a boat ride on the lake, oolong with a view, Yunnan cuisine (pork knuckle with mantou); few tourists.
One of the best-known hotels in Ban Rak Thai village, with postcard views of the lake, tea terraces and mountains in morning clouds.
A cafe in Ban Rak Thai with a beautiful panorama that is recommended for a visit.
A “hundred-in-one” place: tasty food, a lot of space, dog-friendly; massage and yoga have opened on the grounds.
A new Detroit-style pizza place on Manee Nopparat Road, near the site of Smash Daddy’s first pop-up.
An enthusiastic review of the massage: every press is exact, and at the end they applied lip balm and refreshed the face with a spray.
Workshops for kids last an hour and a half and cost 100 baht (for example, a hydraulic arm); lovely views around, you can walk and play inside, easily spending 3 hours.

items.n: Julia: homemade food and cakes to order
items.d: Homemade dumplings, cream rolls and condensed-milk nut cookies, cakes, main dishes and soups from a menu; parents order Napoleon, honey cake and zefir for parties. Order a day ahead, pickup near Central Festival or Grab delivery.
items.p: pelmeni 580 baht/kg; tubes 300 baht/5 pcs; nuts 210–220 baht/12 pcs

items.d: A shop of exquisite roses: friendly staff advise on growing and caring for them at home, and everything for their care is available. Facebook auctions are held from time to time: you can buy online and pick up here.

items.n: Cafe next to the rose shop
items.d: A cafe next to the rose shop, apparently decorated with the same roses.

The ancient capital of King Mangrai, 15 minutes from Warorot: a horse-carriage ride among temple ruins with a guide’s commentary (start at the information center). It has developed as a tourist spot since the 2000s; excavations began in 1984.
items.p: about 300 baht per cart (up to 2 people)

items.d: An unusual area with red earth and patterns of natural erosion, resembling Mars; the “Ghost Market”. Best light early in the morning or before sunset.
An ordinary local barbershop, one of the cheapest in the city: men’s haircut 60 baht, a shave another 10 baht.

items.n: Aircraft noise map of Chiang Mai
items.d: The flightpathnoise.com service: enter an address and see how audible aircraft noise is there; useful when choosing housing.
A buffet in Doi Saket, founded by a Swiss, Roberto; venison is on the menu.
A weekend breakfast buffet with a discount for online booking: eggs to order, bacon, dim sum, northern Thai cuisine, cheeses, fruit; can be stretched to 12:00. Children under 5 free with an adult.
items.p: 350 baht instead of 530 baht (online booking); free for children under 5

items.d: Plai, a relative of ginger, is used in compresses, oils and balms; the preparation Prasaplai is on the national list of medicines (for painful periods, after childbirth). In 2026 capsules with plai extract were released as a supporting remedy for allergies and asthma.

items.n: Liver fluke and raw pla ra
items.d: Opisthorchis viverrini is contracted through raw fermented fish paste pla ra (often in som tam) and raw freshwater fish; the parasite raises the risk of bile duct cancer. Don’t eat raw river fish; if in doubt, get a stool test: it is easily treated.

A preventive and anti-aging medicine clinic of Siam Wellness Group on the grounds of RarinJinda Wellness Spa Resort: tests and hormones, vitamin selection, IV drips. Opening offer until July 31: free EIS Scan and −25% on IV Drip.
items.a: Wat Ket, RarinJinda Wellness Spa Resort
items.p: promotion until 31 July: EIS Scan free, IV Drip −25%

items.d: A place the author calls the “Thai Bali” and has already recommended before; the post gives no details, only a point on the map.
The second shop of a local home fragrance brand: candles made of 100% rice bran wax, diffusers, essential oils, roll-on perfumes, home and textile sprays. Good for finding an original gift.

items.n: เฮือนไม้ในสวน (Huen Mai Nai Suan)
items.d: A restaurant in a green garden with a free mini zoo (ducks, chickens, goats, sheep) and a children’s play area; you can have lunch or coffee. 20–30 minutes from the center.

A fresh pasta and wine restaurant with themed evenings: Tue — Open Vinyl Night (bring a record), Wed — Ladies’ Night, Thu — The Rella Record Club, Fri — Fish Fridays with seafood. Free parking behind the restaurant.
A large lake with a walking promenade not far from the city: you can run, cycle or ride a pedal boat, have a picnic or drink coffee with a view of the water. Popular with locals, few tourists.

Huge American soft cookies with many fillings (chocolate, peanut butter, mango with sticky rice, Dubai chocolate). The main location is near CMU; from July 9 a second one at Tha Phae with warm cookies and a scoop of ice cream (Scoopable Cookie).

An immersive horror quest with live actors: several stories (an abandoned school, an old medical faculty) from short ones to 60–90 minutes, for 2–12 people; afterwards you can sit in the cafe. Booking via Facebook, phone or website.

A market that has finally come alive: musicians in the center, a chocolate stall with thick sugar-free hot chocolate, Nano Bakery, vegan options, wolffia (40 baht for a large bag), straw hats from 390 baht. There is only one coffee stall, with a queue of up to 40 minutes.
A bakery at Bamboo Market with a huge choice of very fresh pastries, which people come here for specially.

A coffee shop a couple of minutes’ drive from Bamboo Market: excellent coffee, pleasant music, lemon water and an atmosphere where you want to linger; an alternative to the 40-minute coffee queue at the market.
A hair salon: beautiful curls, great haircuts, cold lightening, care and restoration for any hair type.

items.n: Where to treat knees and joints: orthopedists and clinics in Chiang Mai
items.d: A roundup of orthopedists and clinics based on expat recommendations: Bangkok Hospital doctors and private clinics, a podiatry center, rehabilitation. The author did not like the doctor at Ram (too by the protocol). With a badly swollen knee or if you can’t step on it, go straight to an orthopedist.

The most recommended orthopedist: sports injuries, arthroscopy, meniscus and ligaments, arthrosis, hyaluronic acid injections, reasonable prices. Also sees patients at Bangkok Hospital Chiang Mai; the author’s consultation was free and nothing unnecessary was prescribed.

An orthopedic trauma surgeon, joint surgery including knee and hip replacement; also sees patients at Bangkok Hospital Chiang Mai. Expats recommend his private clinic: it is easier to get an appointment there.
items.a: Hang Dong Road, near the airport

items.n: Doctor Keng Orthopedic Clinic (Dr. Keng, Taninnit Leerapan)
items.d: A clinic for treating joints, the spine and sports injuries with modern diagnostics and non-surgical methods.

items.n: Dr. Urarat Vasuntaraporn (Bangkok Hospital Chiang Mai)
items.d: An orthopedist at Bangkok Hospital Chiang Mai whom expats recommended positively.
An orthopedics and joint disease clinic: an alternative if you can’t get an appointment with the most recommended doctors.
An orthopedic clinic with good reviews.
An orthopedic surgeon’s clinic.
A clinic of orthopedics, traumatology and joint surgery.
An orthopedic clinic on Mahidol Road.
A podiatry center: they help with gait problems, select custom orthopedic insoles and assess foot biomechanics; sometimes knee pain comes from the foot.
A physiotherapy clinic that expats recommend for rehabilitation after injuries and surgery.
A medical and physiotherapy clinic recommended by expats for rehabilitation after injuries and surgery.
An Indian restaurant from a roundup of places with curry, naan, roti and biryani in Chiang Mai.
An Indian restaurant from a roundup of Indian food places in Chiang Mai.
An Indian restaurant from a roundup of Indian food places in Chiang Mai.
An Indian restaurant from a roundup of Indian food places in Chiang Mai.
An Indian restaurant from a roundup of Indian food places in Chiang Mai.
An Indian restaurant in Nimman, the favorite of the author of the Indian restaurant roundup, which she always enjoys going back to.
An Indian restaurant-bar with a grill from a roundup of Indian food places in Chiang Mai.
An authentic Indian cuisine restaurant from a roundup of Indian restaurants in Chiang Mai.

A coworking space with fast internet, ergonomic chairs, phone booths and meeting rooms, free tea, coffee and water, parking and the Tora Bake bakery in the building. With a monthly membership, 24/7 access.

items.n: Bun Bang Fai (rocket festival) at Huai Lan Reservoir
items.d: An annual homemade rocket festival at the Huai Lan reservoir in San Kamphaeng: team launches, live music, a fair, street food, dancing. Arrive by noon, bring a hat, water and sunscreen.

items.n: Somm Wine & Dine SOMM Restaurant CNX
items.d: A nice rooftop restaurant with tasty food and a good choice of dishes; in the low season you can find free seats.
A cafe with fresh pastries right in the One Workspace coworking building.
A recommendation of good cleaners in the Chang Khlan area (several Facebook profiles); you can ask whether they work in your location.

items.n: Lamphun: factories of global brands, wasabi and Yok Dok silk
items.d: In Lamphun, half an hour from Chiang Mai, there are factories of Murata, HOYA, Le Creuset, Bernina, Wacoal and others; Lanna Products has grown real wasabi for Japan for 30 years; the province is the home of royal Yok Dok Lamphun silk. Tourists come for Wat Phra That Hariphunchai and longan.

items.n: Yoga in the park in Chiang Mai (Nong Buak Haad Park)
items.d: Morning classes in Nong Buak Haad Park with different teachers: for the week of June 29–July 3 — Nervous System Flow, Lanna martial art, Martial Arts Dance, Mindful Mobility, kundalini kriya yoga. No classes on weekends in July; bring your own mat.
items.h: weekdays 08:00–09:15; no classes on Saturdays and Sundays in July

items.d: An art space in Hang Dong: mindfulness, meditation and watercolor painting practice in groups of up to 6 people; children can also be brought to classes. Booking through the organizers.

A legendary family noodle shop famous for mini portions at 3 baht: now pricier, but the format is the same — you take several small bowls of different kinds. Many locals; Google 4.1 from almost 1900 reviews.
A market reopened after renovation, with a food court and small shops; live music in the evenings.
A link to buckwheat on Lazada: the color is something between green and brown, and the price is average too.
A temple on a mountain, a wonderful place for greeting the sunrise and for views of the city.
One of two temple ice cream spots recommended in the post; according to the post, one opens at 8 and the other at 9 a.m.
The second temple ice cream spot from the same post; according to the post, one opens at 8 and the other at 9 a.m.

Tourist SIMs periodically go stale even if the package is paid and there is money on the balance, so they need to be renewed: for TrueMove (dtac) you dial the command for 180 days, which costs 12 baht (the command was in the photo).

The private estate of designer Bill Bensley, in the style of a Mexican hacienda in the middle of a tropical forest, with thousands of plants and antiques. It cannot be visited as a museum: it is rented only as a whole, 11 bedrooms, minimum 5 nights, on prior request.

From June 22, 2026 cannabis flowers are sold only with a medical prescription (form ภ.ท.33); smoking lounges in shops, online sales, vending machines and selling near temples, dormitories and parks are grounds for license revocation. Buying from individuals is a risk for the buyer.

items.n: Coconut ice cream at the Blue Temple
items.d: The Blue Temple in Chiang Rai sells beautiful coconut ice cream — it is recommended not to walk past it.

An online shop of handmade organic soap (cinnamon-ginger, coffee-almond milk, tamarind-lemon, jasmine-annatto and others); shipping across Thailand within 48 hours. Promo code SOAP20 gives 20% off and free delivery.

An exhibition of key works from the MAIIAM museum’s own collection (curator — co-founder Jean-Michel Beurdeley): almost 40 artists, among them Apichatpong Weerasethakul, Rirkrit Tiravanija, Daido Moriyama.
3D garden design, landscaping in minimalist, Japanese and English styles, automatic watering and sprinklers, waterfalls, fountains and water walls, tiled paths, lawn laying.

A walking route from the North Gate heading south: coffee shops, museums (Treasury Museum, City Arts & Cultural Centre, House of Photography), restaurants, the temples Wat Chedi Luang and Wat Phan Tao; at the end — Yok Fah Rad Na by Warorot Market. It can be done in a day.
One of the best coffee shops in the Old City: coffee made in different ways — V60, Kalita Wave, drip, cold brew or espresso from Northern Thailand beans.
A small museum of the history of Thai money in the Old City, a visit takes 30–40 minutes; there is a traveler’s passport — fill it with trips around the country and you can get a prize.

items.n: Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Centre
items.d: A museum of the history of Chiang Mai and the Lanna kingdom with modern multimedia exhibits; next door is the Lanna Folklife Centre.
A museum of the traditions and daily life of Northern Thailand next to the Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Centre; many people visit both.
A small blue mansion with exhibitions of historical photographs of Chiang Mai; entry is usually free, and it is often missed because the house is not in plain sight.
An unusual Farm to Glass cafe: signature drinks, desserts and craft soda made from seasonal fruit.
A small restaurant of traditional Central Thai cuisine — dishes cooked for locals.
One of the most popular places for breakfast and brunch in the Old City: great coffee and big portions.
The main temple of the Old City with a majestic 15th-century chedi, where the Emerald Buddha was once kept.
One of the few surviving teak temples in Chiang Mai; the inner courtyard has a beautiful golden chedi that many people miss.
The restaurant of the boutique hotel Tamarind Village: Thai and northern cuisine in a green courtyard with a pool; you can come without staying at the hotel.

Legendary rad na noodles, cooked for more than 30 years: thick sauce, homemade noodles, big portions. A little east of the Old City, by Warorot Market, 15–20 minutes on foot from the Three Kings Monument.
A new cozy space in front of the entrance to Wat Ton Kwen (Wat Inthrawat), blending with the Lanna architecture; a place to walk and take photos before visiting the wooden viharn. Entry is paid.
The Chiang Mai–Lamphun road (the yang na road, Saraphi, old Highway 106) with hundreds of century-old yang na trees — one of the symbols of Northern Thailand.

Big Clean — a deep clean of a house in one day: windows outside and inside, 3M machine floor cleaning, removal of mites from mattresses and sofas, ozonation, cleaning of air conditioner filters, the kitchen and the bathroom.
items.p: promotion: free dry cleaning of a sofa, mattress or carpet or a discount of up to 1000 baht

items.n: Bird watching community in Chiang Mai
items.d: Chiang Mai has a whole channel (a Facebook group) about bird watching — children may find it interesting too.
A bird watching route (a map link from the post about the birdwatcher community).

items.n: CAD Academy Art and Culture Center (Payap University)
items.d: A newly opened center of Payap University and the Chiang Mai CAD Foundation for studying and preserving Lanna art and culture and supporting modern creative projects.

A Lahu mountain village with a view of Doi Luang Chiang Dao: a waterfall on the way, a trek to the Pha Sam Liam viewpoint, tea plantations, homestays. 1.5–2 hours from Chiang Dao via Mae Mae Tree House; the road is muddy in the rains, and homestays offer a transfer.

items.n: A Thai Herbal: Traditional Recipes for Health and Harmony
items.d: A rare book in English (C. Pierce Salguero, 2005, 188 pp.) about 150+ Thai medicinal herbs, recipes and the link with Thai massage; sold through a book page on Facebook, which has other books too.
The “Rainbow Cave” with stalactites, stalagmites and multicolored walls (Unseen Thailand) reopens on July 1, 2026 after renovation: a paved parking area and road, new safe walkways.
A family park: a pool with water slides, a mini zoo (ostriches, deer), a walking park, a green maze and topiary trees. The family offer is only with advance booking and payment through Facebook.
items.p: 259 baht for 1 adult + 1 child (instead of 368); extra adult 120 baht, child 60 baht

items.d: A dental clinic that the channel’s author calls the “best recommendation”.
Great Thai massage in the Jed Yod area.
A WhatsApp group with listings for long-term housing rentals in Chiang Mai (an alternative to Facebook groups).
A fishing lake: the owner Graham shows and tells you everything, and also cooks very tasty food; people come here to celebrate birthdays too.
Overnight oats oatmeal delivered through GrabFood (a spot in Fa Ham).

A cafe where you can order a whole banoffee cake (about 700 baht) for a birthday; good coffee, a dense tiramisu, a lemon dessert with poppy seeds. Many orders come through Grab, but the dining room is almost empty.
A cafe that the channel’s author advises those who haven’t been yet to visit.
A tasty chocolate cake — an option for a children’s birthday (about 900 g for about 1400 baht); the hot chocolate is also praised, especially the shot of Belgian.

At the zoo you can see the baby hippo Som Poy (born 14.04.2026), and a new reptile pavilion has opened. Talks are under way with China about a new pair of pandas (the last panda died in 2023), expected in 1–2 years.

A massage school at Oasis Spa: student trainees look for clients on Fridays and Saturdays — excellent quality, the price is about 10 times lower than a spa (where it starts from 1500 baht). Offers come on LINE. The Oasis cafe is next door; you can also learn massage.
items.p: roughly 10 times cheaper than Oasis Spa (where it usually starts from 1500 baht)
items.h: practice with clients on Fridays and Saturdays

items.n: Organic Hass avocados from a local farmer
items.d: A farmer from Chiang Mai grows organic Hass avocados: delivery via Grab or Bolt, or a meeting at Central Airport Plaza or Tha Phae Gate. Contact through WhatsApp.
A salon in Hang Dong where hair is washed and dried divinely while you lie in a massage chair that even massages your calves.

items.n: Road repairs along the Old City moat (phase 4)
items.d: The municipality is relaying asphalt on the outer side of the moat from Si Phum Gate via Hua Lin Corner to Ku Hueang Corner, and also on Bun Rueang Rit Road and Manee Nopparat Road; temporary traffic restrictions are possible.
One of the most beautiful housing estates in the city (in the channel author’s opinion), with a link to the developer’s project page.

Free round-the-clock help for Hang Dong residents in natural disasters and emergencies (wind, downpours, storms): cutting up and clearing fallen trees, pulling out cars stuck in mud, starting an engine with a dead battery.

The first three-level interchange in Chiang Mai, at the junction of Highways No. 121 (Middle Ring Road) and No. 1317, is 92% complete, with traffic planned to open in September 2026; it should relieve jams toward Saraphi and San Kamphaeng.
One of the most popular places in Nimman for live music lovers: bands and jazz performers every evening, Thai and European cuisine, cocktails.
A cozy sports bar with pool tables, good food and live music: acoustic sets on Fridays, a live band on Saturdays. The courtyard has several restaurants.

items.n: Quarterly Hot Wheels tournament on the Mario Rainbow Road Super Track
items.d: Hot Wheels car racing at Wild Heart Chiang Mai in the Open, New, Special and Quarter Cup categories; every participant gets a 100-baht coupon for a car and a 50-baht coupon for food. For children and adults.
Repair of houses and condos, plumbing, electrical work, fridge repair, cleaning and installation of air conditioners, garden and pool maintenance. English-speaking team, warranty, free consultation.
A small family Lanna restaurant in Suthep, known mostly to locals: nam ngiao, kaeng hang lay, sai ua, nam prik noom. Rating 4.9/5, most dishes up to 200 baht.

A rose garden next to Phuwin Cafe on Mon Jam: dozens of rose varieties against mountains and mist, coffee with a view. At the end of June the first part was in bloom, and another section blooms in about two weeks. Most beautiful in the morning.

items.n: Waitrose Duchy Organic Stoneground Wholemeal Plain Flour
items.d: Organic stoneground wholemeal flour, without additives, with a nutty taste and 12.9 g of fiber per 100 g. Sold at Tops, on Shopee and Lazada.

A clinic with branches at Central Chiangmai Airport and Central Festival; a promotion for online booking: a package of 9 underarm treatments (3 Gentle Hair Laser hair removals, 3 masks, 3 treatments) for 888 baht.

An inconspicuous, cozy Japanese restaurant on Nimman Soi 11: fresh handmade soba (hot and cold), hambagu, ramen, tonkatsu, mapo tofu; the owners make the tableware themselves. A bar in the evening, delivery available. Noodle show on Sat and Sun.

Rice-paper rolls assembled to taste, with calories and macros calculated; concept Low Carb • High Protein, low-calorie sauces without sugar. Order via GrabFood and LINE MAN, free delivery when ordering through the shop page.

items.n: Open-air movie night at KEO Park: Stand By Me
items.d: A monthly movie night at KEO Park: “Stand By Me” (1986) in English; a special food and drinks menu, a limited number of cinema-style seats.

The famous cabin from a Thai TV series among rice terraces in Ban Khun Pae village (Chom Thong), 2–2.5 hours from the city; open for booking for the first time. Prices and dates from the owners on Messenger. The green-field season starts at the end of June.

items.n: ฮั้วหอยทอด เชียงใหม่ (Huahoitod Chiangmai)
items.d: A place with unusually low prices for oysters, from 60 baht.

items.n: CMU Museum of Veterinary Anatomy and Pathology
items.d: A free, little-known museum at the CMU veterinary faculty: skeletons of an elephant, a giraffe, a horse, skulls and anatomical exhibits. Classes run on weekdays, and some halls may be closed. Parking on the grounds.
items.a: Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, Chiang Mai University
items.h: Mon–Fri 08:00–16:30; closed Sat, Sun and public holidays

items.n: Airport fee on international departures: 1120 baht
items.d: From June 20, 2026 the fee on international departures from Suvarnabhumi, Don Mueang, Phuket, Chiang Mai, Chiang Rai and Hat Yai is 1120 baht instead of 730, already included in the ticket. For domestic flights it is 130 baht, unchanged.

A cafe a few steps from the Tha Chomphu White Railway Bridge: open terraces on the 2nd and 3rd floors with a view of the bridge, mountains and fields, especially when a train passes. Best in the morning or toward evening.

A snow-white arched railway bridge more than 100 years old on the Northern Railway between Bangkok and Chiang Mai, one of the most beautiful in Thailand; in the rainy season it is bright green all around.
A recommended place in Chiang Dao (the post gives only the name and a map link, the type of place is not stated).

items.n: TATA Chiang Dao Cafe and Farm
items.d: A cafe and farm in Chiang Dao (the post gives only the name and a map link).

items.n: Chiang Mai city rail Red Line
items.d: The Chiang Mai public transport Red Line project, on the route Nakhon Ping Hospital → Mae Hia Intersection, received environmental impact assessment (EIA) approval in June 2026.

items.n: Wat Phra That Suthon Mongkhon Khiri
items.d: A modern temple complex (from 1977–1984) about 2.5 hours from Chiang Mai: a reclining Buddha about 85 m long, a mix of Lanna, Burmese and Khmer styles, 30+ golden stupas, carving in the ubosot, a museum of teak houses. Best to come in the morning or evening.

items.n: Crackdown on nominee ownership schemes: liability
items.d: The third phase of the operation against nominee owners (Phuket, Krabi, Phang Nga). Under the Foreign Business Act: up to 3 years and/or a fine of 100 000–1 000 000 baht, a daily fine of 10–50 thousand baht; AMLO may classify the schemes as money laundering.

A children's music school: professional English-speaking teachers who tell parents about progress after the lesson. Parking, a cafe with air conditioning and an air purifier for waiting, and a place with tasty matcha nearby.
A hotel in Chiang Dao from which the author and friends admired the views.
A cozy guesthouse in Chiang Dao: a homey atmosphere, tasty breakfasts, a campfire in the evening, fantastic views.
Great European food in Chiang Dao: cooked fast, cheaper than neighboring restaurants, even the sauces are praised.
A bar in Chiang Dao with craft beer and burgers (a smaller choice and pricier than the neighbors); you can play Dendy.
An Italian in Chiang Dao cooks thoroughly and slowly, like solid home food; there are few seats, better to book in advance.

items.n: Business inspections for Thai nominees in Chiang Mai
items.d: The campaign against foreigners using Thais as nominal owners has moved from the southern islands to Chiang Mai: illegal hotels and fictitious offices were found. Questions may also arise about buying houses through such schemes.
Free classic boxing sparring at Suthep Municipal Stadium: a regular friendly group, no aggression or hard hits, emphasis on technique and fitness. Beginners are welcome.
A chain of music stores (34 years; Bangkok, Chiang Mai, Phuket, Khon Kaen): instruments, accessories and goods for learning. Violins, violas and cellos of its own Custom brand, from 2500 baht.
A German restaurant with homemade sausages and pork knuckle; there is a buffet and ordering from the menu.

items.n: Soul Soak — Sound Journey in mineral pools
items.d: Every Friday at Sense Dhara Dhevi Wellness Club: a meditation with live gongs and singing bowls, listened to right in the thermal pools or the relaxation area.
A cafe with great music in the evenings and very tasty food, especially burgers.
Free dance fitness Zumba workouts on the 1st floor of Central Chiangmai Airport every 2nd and 4th Wednesday of the month; PUMA Palermo sneakers are raffled among participants.
items.h: every 2nd and 4th Wednesday of the month

items.d: A shop with used golf clubs: a big selection and nice prices.
One of the best tool shops: original well-known brands, English-speaking staff and professional advice.
A board game cafe-club with a huge choice; you can play all day, and the owner patiently explains the rules of every game. A great option for kids on holiday.
items.p: 100 baht adults, 80 baht schoolchildren — for the whole day

items.n: Kids' play zone at Maya Mall
items.d: A new paid kids' play zone on the 4th floor of MAYA next to the food court (the free playground was removed). A way to wait out the heat or rain.
items.p: 180 baht — 90 minutes; 399 baht — unlimited for the whole day

items.d: A kids' play cafe with hourly payment.
items.p: 10 minutes — 20 baht; 30 minutes — 50 baht; hour — 100 baht

items.d: A rare Bengal (leopard) cat has appeared on Doi Inthanon again; it was seen around km 36. Drivers are asked to go carefully so as not to hit animals.
A temple with a huge statue of Somdet Phra Buddhachan (To Prommarangsi); a beautiful view with the majestic Doi Luang in the background.

items.n: Sports betting is illegal in Thailand
items.d: Any sports betting in Thailand is illegal: players face up to 2 years in prison and/or a fine of up to 2000 baht, organizers up to 5 years and up to 100 000 baht. Only the state lottery and horse racing at certified racecourses are legal.

items.n: Guide to Chiang Mai districts for renting housing
items.d: Pros and cons of the districts: Nimman, CMU/Jed Yod, Old City, Santitham, Central Festival/Fa Ham/Ruamchok, San Sai, Hang Dong, Mae Hia, Riverside/Wat Ket, Mae Rim, Doi Saket. Tip: first rent for 1–2 weeks and drive around the districts.
The main attraction of Lamphun, one of the most revered temples of Northern Thailand with a golden chedi more than a thousand years old; it is pleasant to stroll around the old town.

items.n: Chiang Mai — Lamphun train for 5 baht
items.d: A 3rd-class train to Lamphun: 5 baht, ~25 minutes, views of rice fields. There: 06:25, 09:35, 15:35; back: 11:16, 14:22, an air-conditioned carriage at 17:30 for 50 baht. See the temples, the Hariphunchai museum and coffee shops.
items.p: 5 baht; return trip at 17:30 with air conditioning — 50 baht

items.d: The most atmospheric coffee shop in central Lamphun opposite Wat Phra That Hariphunchai: a small art gallery, a view of the temple complex, excellent coffee and homemade desserts.
A stylish coffee shop in a minimalist industrial style within walking distance of central Lamphun, often in roundups of the city's best cafes.
A national museum in Lamphun on the history of the ancient kingdom of Hariphunchai.
One of the oldest temples in Lamphun, linked with the legendary Queen Chamthewi.
A small, cozy European restaurant with beautiful presentation: steak with seafood, layered potatoes with tomatoes and caramelized onion, red wine sauce.
A hair care salon looking for models for training sessions: a free hair wash and scalp massage (75–90 min), curly and bleached hair preferred. Sign up via LINE.

items.n: Raw mountain honey from Chiang Rai
items.d: Natural forest honey from the 2026 harvest (April–May) from a mountain village in Chiang Rai province, raw and very aromatic. Order via direct messages, limited quantity.
A running club from a roundup of the coolest running clubs in Chiang Mai in 2026; there are clubs for beginners and experienced runners.

A new cafe with minimalist architecture opposite the gate of the CMU agriculture faculty, next to Blue Coffee. The HOLE Cafe chain is running a football prize draw from June 9 to July 19, 2026: 1 drink = 1 entry, receipt in LINE OA.
items.a: opposite the CMU Faculty of Agriculture

items.n: Company making healthy bread and desserts
items.d: Another company that bakes healthy bread and makes desserts (a Facebook page).

items.n: Electrical safety: water heaters and electric shock
items.d: After people died from a current leak in a water heater in Hang Dong: check the grounding and that the RCD works (TEST button), do not ignore tingling from the water, and do not use an electric shower during a thunderstorm. Do not touch the victim with bare hands: switch off the power first.

items.n: Half-day immersion in the jungle cuisine of the Akha people with Buti
items.d: A farm program 09:30–15:30: a walk among 20+ plants, cooking in bamboo, an Akha-style lunch, an Akha culture room, a tea ceremony. Suitable for vegetarians and families with children, small group, book in advance.
A salon with a facial massage for glowing, relaxed skin; special offer from 250 baht. Book by phone or via Line.
A clinic on the 2nd floor of Kad Farang Village: a 7-step deep facial cleansing (oxygen peel, vacuum blackhead removal, detox mask, head, neck and back massage) for 999 baht, 60 minutes.

items.n: Car rental with a driver (Pi Bo)
items.d: A four-door pickup with a driver for 1–4 people, first-class insurance: tours 08:00–18:00, transfers to the airport, the railway station and the Arcade bus station; help with photos. Overnight outside the city +400 baht per night.
items.p: 1300 baht per day (fuel not included); +400 baht per night for trips with overnight stays

items.d: Huay Lan Reservoir, 30–40 km east of the city (less than an hour's drive): quiet, views of green hills, especially after rain. Popular with locals for picnics and bike rides. There is no infrastructure, so bring your own food and mats.
A Czech-German sports bar where you can watch the World Cup night matches (for example at two in the morning).
A cozy quiet cafe with a small garden and birds in Mae Hia, opens early, lots of seats. A duck dish for 59 baht, cappuccino 35 baht, oat milk available.
A villa with its own pool in the Old City: a change of scenery without leaving town.
A restaurant in Hang Dong that makes tasty fried chicken and papaya salad.
A cozy cafe on the bank of the Ping River with greenery and desserts; with a drink you get a wooden blank to paint for free, extra blanks are 30 baht. Good for a rest with kids.
A cafe in the mountains where frozen macadamia and macadamia body oil are sold upstairs, and you can walk around the tree and the suspension bridge. Subscribers call the massaman beef here the best.
A 24-hour wholesale market for fruit, vegetables and herbs.
A relatively new quiet cafe where you can eat, have coffee and work: outlets at the tables. Food 80–100 baht, smoothies 65 baht.
An authentic non-touristy coffee shop with a river view, a favorite of a local masseuse; handmade coffee, open for about a year.

“No Escape” (2015) was filmed in Chiang Mai and Lampang, the key location being the Imperial Mae Ping Hotel, now InterContinental Chiang Mai The Mae Ping. Part of “American Gangster” (2007) was also filmed in Chiang Mai.

items.n: Caves and rafting in the rainy season: risks
items.d: After a rescue operation in a flooded cave (five saved, two not found), the author advises against going into caves and rafting in the rainy season: downpours, flooding, rockfalls after earthquakes.
Tickets for the Sky of Wishes lantern festival by Thantara Lanna are sold on Ticketmelon; the post does not give the date.
At Central Festival, opposite DIY, there are honeycomb smoking pods with outlets and individual space.

A temple about 700 years old among forest and misty mountains, Lanna architecture: naga staircases, a carved wooden ubosot, a 9-meter statue of the walking Buddha made from a single champi tree trunk. Transfer from the parking lot 800 baht round trip.
items.a: Mae Wang (Ban Khun Win, Mae Win)
items.p: transfer from the parking lot 800 baht round trip

items.d: A service delivering high-protein plant-based dishes from a chef to your home; order via direct message or a form.
items.p: 5 meals a week — 1000 baht; 10 meals a week — 1800 baht

items.d: The Minimal coffee shop chain has launched a loyalty card: after a purchase you are given a LINE contact, you scan it and collect stamps.

Since the start of 2026, 29 490 foreigners have been denied entry and 14 161 arrested; the APPS system checks passengers against a blacklist even before departure. Checks of student visas and the fight against nominee Thai owners of businesses have been strengthened.

items.n: DJ Selecta Rootmuang on Vinyl — TEMPO.Radio
items.d: A Sunday TEMPO.Radio broadcast: Northern Thai songs in Kam Mueang, traditional “so” singing and old parody songs on vinyl. You can listen live at Baan Samadhi.
A Thai herbal tea from dried pandan and jujube, which Thais call chuchubi; it is best steeped for about half an hour.
The masseuse the channel's author goes to; a new 20-minute head massage service has appeared, it kneads well.
Fragrant natural salt from Isan with 6 kinds of herbs is sold on the 1st floor of Central Festival.

items.s: cafe and homestay in the mountains
items.d: A cafe-restaurant and homestay with 4 rooms among mountains, ~1,5 hours from the Old City. Stay with breakfast and a shabu-shabu dinner. Local dishes: nam prik oop, yam bai miang, gaeng het. In the rainy season the mountains are in mist.
items.p: lodging 1900–2500 baht per night depending on the season and room

items.d: The largest building and household hypermarket (“HomePro on steroids”): Makita and DeWalt tools, building materials, plumbing, electrics, appliances, furniture, garden. Parking, help in English, HomePro bonuses.
A cafe with mountain views on the road to Nan after Phayao; the author advises not to drive past.
items.a: on the way to Nan after Phayao

items.d: A place before Magic mountains cafe on the road to Nan: simpler, free, but tasty and with the same views.
items.a: Highway 1148, on the way to Nan after Phayao

items.d: A campsite next to Magic mountains cafe on the road to Nan after Phayao.
items.a: on the way to Nan after Phayao

items.d: Doi Luang Chiang Dao mountain; in the rainy season the views are even prettier with the clouds.
You can always buy fresh Italian basil here, and sometimes cheap celery.
A Blue Zone cuisine restaurant on the farm-to-table principle: vegan and gluten-free dishes, not one dish over 500 baht. A chef with fine-dining experience. Booking is recommended.
items.p: no dish costs more than 500 baht

items.d: Full-cycle construction and renovation of condos, houses, bars and restaurants: foundations, walls, tiles, plumbing, electrics, air conditioners, painting, lock opening, furniture assembly, TV and curtain installation.
A home repair company, including fixing roof leaks before the rainy season; it also has separate garden and cleaning divisions.
The garden division of The Wizard Group: everything to do with gardening and lawns.
The cleaning division of The Wizard Group (repairs, garden, cleaning).
A recommendation of the “best doula” in Chiang Mai, a Facebook page.
A community and team for birth preparation: education, doulas, help with breastfeeding, support on all questions.
A remedy with cajuput extract works well for insect bites and burns (Lazada link); also Sudocream, which many pharmacies have.

A Saturday market from June to September 2026 in the shade of trees next to the cafe: art, handmade goods, local food, workshops. Free space for sellers (2 m, own equipment). You can come with children.
items.a: Rumpeng Road, near Wat Ram Poeng and Baan Kang Wat

items.d: Rich organic cocoa of ceremonial grade.
A national park home to Asian black bears and sun bears; in the Phanoen Thung area they are seen near roads, campsites and viewpoints. Do not get close or feed them, and do not leave food unattended.
A second-hand shop in 70s style; four racks of sparkly clothes with rhinestones and feathers, short and long, are back, to shine at a party.
A specialty coffee seller on Lazada: the grind is chosen for a specific brewing method, the bags have a valve for gas to escape, a seal sticker and the grind date.
A cozy city market on the first Sunday of every month: coffee and local food, crafts by makers, live music, handmade and vintage; in June the theme is Pride at Sanpakoi.
A restaurant with a new signature menu: Hokkaido scallops with truffle emulsion on squid ink, foie gras and other dishes.
A Japanese second-hand store: suitcases, blenders, yoga mats, bikes; the hangar has a lot of toys. The building you need is behind the first one, in the middle.
A nice petting zoo with a show; great to visit with kids.
A new shopping space that is planned to open in the Payup (Payap) area.

items.n: Best hotels in Thailand according to Tatler Asia
items.d: Tatler Asia's ranking of the best hotels in Thailand, with a hotel in Chiang Mai in first place; according to the author, you can go there just for the restaurant.

items.n: Chiang Mai International School (new campus near Payap)
items.d: CMIS is building a new campus near Payap University, moving from a cramped location next to Prince Royal’s; the area has historic ties to American missionary educational institutions.

items.n: Kha grass fields in Khao Yai National Park
items.d: In the rainy season, fields of white kha grass (หญ้าคา) bloom among green hills in Thailand's first national park, a beautiful place for photos; the park is 2,5–3 hours from Bangkok toward Nakhon Ratchasima.
St. Michael's church, which the author found on the map of Thailand while looking for ancient temples; the post does not give the location.
A temple far from Chiang Mai with unusual tiles, judging by the name in Lao style; there are almost no reviews.
A temple with delicate dusty colors and an unusual animal (probably a lion); there are almost no reviews.
A link to honey on Lazada that the author considers “normal” honey; it is not always in stock.

items.n: Liang Dong ritual of the spirits Pu Sae and Ya Sae
items.d: An annual animist ritual honoring the forest spirits — the guardians of Doi Suthep — asking for fertility and timely rains; the tradition is more than 100 years old.
items.a: Pu Sae and Ya Sae shrine on the way to Wat Phra That Doi Kham, Mae Hia Nai village

items.d: A serious contender for the best burger in the city; the coffee is professional too.

A space with a small stage and a coffee shop next to the Chamcha Market craft market; available for events and weddings. In May 2026 a free Play Space on weekends: jazz, world music, poetry, art, DJs.
A craft market at WerngChamchaa Play Space, open on weekends.
A studio in Bangkok with very beautiful silk kimonos, including embroidered models (Instagram).

items.n: Windfield French International School Chiang Mai Open Day
items.d: A chance to see the campus of the new French international school, meet the teachers and watch how children aged 2–12 study.
items.a: Windfield French International School Chiang Mai

items.n: Windfield French International School Chiang Mai
items.d: A new French international school in Chiang Mai for children aged 2 to 12 with a modern campus and a multicultural environment.
A new evening vintage market by the Ping River: authentic vintage and secondhand, vinyl, art objects, decor; it is planned to be held every Saturday and Sunday evening in future. Free entry.
items.a: Boon Yoo Parking Lot, near Wat Ket

items.d: A nice coffee shop in Mae Rim.
The first Tesla center in Northern Thailand at Central Chiangmai Airport: an introduction to electric cars and test drive sign-up; opening in June 2026.
A cafe that cooks tasty khao soi and yuzu coffee; many people value the breakfasts. There is a swimming pool.

items.s: cafe by a stream in the forest
items.d: A cafe in the middle of the forest by a stream in Ban Mae Kampong: warm wooden interior, a calm atmosphere, beautiful photo spots; coffee, caffeine-free drinks and fresh pastries.
A shop of clothes made of natural fabrics (Instagram); there are clothes for girls with a large bust.
Quality tailoring; if they do not take the order, they will recommend whom to turn to.
Tailoring that is quite budget-friendly.
A seamstress who sews fast and on a budget.
On the second floor of Warorot Market sit seamstresses who will fix anything on a budget.
A seamstress who handles linen well.

items.n: Seamstresses with more than 20 years of experience
items.d: Great seamstresses who have been working for more than 20 years.
A clothing shop, khao soi, coffee and a seamstress all in one place.

A seamstress and a laundry in one place.

Another seamstress from the roundup, with a Facebook page.
The roundup author's favorite seamstress — a cheerful craftswoman.
Sews clothes from scratch to a high standard, repairs and alters them to size, and repairs soft toys; speaks good English. The shop is open irregularly — arrange a visit in advance on LINE.
A cute furniture and decor shop (the owner is called Dao): from dishes to furniture, a huge choice of interior items; there are many other furniture shops nearby.
A moving company around Chiang Mai and all of Thailand: they work quickly and, if you wish, pack your things; they have large warehouses for storage.
A truck owner helps with moves around the city and constantly drives the Chiang Mai — Bangkok route and back; portfolio on the Facebook page.

A local contractor with 20+ years of experience and a team of engineers: roof and pump repairs, changing light bulbs, any work around the house to Western standards at Thai prices. They speak English.
A professional team for roof and house repair; you can contact them directly by phone.
Taxi and tour services around Chiang Mai around the clock, including inter-province cargo delivery.
A 7/11 store (outlet) that accepts batteries for disposal.

Cleaning: one-off, deep and regular cleaning of houses and offices; they help unpack and organize things and dispose of unneeded items. They also run Garden Wizards — lawn mowing.

items.n: Small appliance repair near Phra Pok (1)
items.d: A small workshop for repairing small household appliances — one of two on opposite sides of the road in the Phra Pok area; an alternative to the Amorn Electronic workshop.

Another handyman: roof repair, and you can also ask him to mow the grass.
An organization supporting people with disabilities: equipment, wheelchair repair, support and information.
Curtain washing, mattress, sofa and carpet cleaning, deep cleaning, including cleaning balconies and roofs of pigeon droppings; they work in Chiang Mai and Lamphun. Free cost estimate.
A cozy small family cafe with very good sourdough bread and shiopan.
A good inexpensive Western cafe in Saraphi, with a Japanese menu too: rice with picanha, fish and chips, pasta with bacon and 2 drinks came to 437 baht.
Makro has Australian grain-fed beef (brisket) at 265 baht/kg; a link to the product on MakroPRO.
Indian-Pakistani halal cuisine; the lamb, biryani and chicken curry are especially praised.

items.n: Cash on entry to Thailand: spot checks
items.d: Cash is spot-checked at major airports: for entry without a visa or on a tourist visa — from 20,000 baht per person or 40,000 per family, on Visa on Arrival — 10,000/20,000. Banking apps and cards may not be accepted; entry may be refused.

items.n: Chiang Mai flood risk zone map (CMFlood)
items.d: The CMFlood system shows the flood zones of the urban part of Chiang Mai for 5 water levels (4.30–5.30 m) at station P.1 by the Nawarat Bridge; the water overflows the banks at a level above 4.20 m.

items.n: Liang Dong ceremony of the spirits Pu Asa and Ya Asa
items.d: An annual ancient rite of the residents of Mae Hia in honor of the ancestral spirits Pu Asa and Ya Asa, with the sacrifice of a buffalo; held on the 14th day of the waxing moon of the 9th northern month (late May — June) at Wat Phra That Doi Kham, the exact date is announced closer to the event.
items.a: Mae Hia, Wat Phra That Doi Kham

items.d: An old upholstery workshop with a huge choice of fabrics and leather; the owner is a professional. Furniture covers, cushions, custom mattresses for your furniture, work with your own fabric.

items.n: Visa exemption back to 30 days: official decision
items.d: Thailand has officially scrapped the 60-day visa exemption and returned 30 days for 90+ countries; Indians now need a visa on arrival (up to 15 days). For long trips — a tourist visa in advance or a 30-day extension at Immigration Office for 1900 baht.
A shop with a selection of dark chocolate; there are coffee beans too.

A breakfast option in Nimman: the pork skewers are praised, the place is popular, with many orders through Grab, and it sells out quickly — better to come early. One of the few places open early in the morning.
A temple in Sukhothai Historical Park: three-meter walls with a secret passage and acoustics linked to the legend of the “talking Buddha” who inspired warriors.

A green space at Meta Mall: it is safe for kids to run and play, you can do yoga and stretching, walk dogs (pet friendly), and on the Skyline rooftop there are sunsets and DJ sets. You can hold your own event, convenient parking.
A snow town at a temperature of -10°C on the grounds of Chiang Mai Zoo: snow, photos, ice slides; suitable for the whole family.
Italian gelato with a big choice of flavors, including vegan ones (Vegan Mixed Berry, pistachio); the owner Stefano is responsive to customers’ requests. Delivery via TukTuk and GrabFood.
A branch of the Italian gelato shop 7 Senses in Hang Dong; vegan flavors available, delivery via TukTuk and GrabFood.

items.n: Which visa to choose after the visa exemption is cut to 30 days
items.d: A review of the options: 30 days of visa exemption + a 30-day extension for 1900 baht; a tourist visa 60+30 days and a border run (about 4000 baht by bus to Laos); a retirement visa from age 50; a student visa (up to 50 thousand baht a year); DTV (500 thousand baht, 180 days, extension 10 thousand).
items.p: extension 1900 baht, border run about 4000 baht, student visa up to 50 000 baht/year, DTV extension 10 000 baht

items.n: A small roundup of places in Nan
items.d: Eight links to places in Nan Province without names or descriptions.
A WhatsApp group for discussing visa questions.
Dr. Chatchai has run his dermatology clinic for many years; reviews are mixed, but there are results. Moles are not removed here.

items.n: Thai residency through work: an application experience
items.d: Residency through work requires 3 years of an uninterrupted work permit and an official salary from 80 000 baht with taxes paid. The application window is once a year (in 2026, March), 15+ items, ~150 sheets, photos at home and at work, an easy Thai exam; the card takes from six months.
Helps assemble documents for Thai residency for those who have worked in the country for 3 years with a salary from 80 000 baht; helped the post’s author through his Thai assistant.
A school where, according to the author, a month of classes is enough to prepare for the Thai language exam when applying for residency.

items.n: Visakha Bucha: the night pilgrimage to Doi Suthep and Wian Tian
items.d: On the evening of 30 May from ~16:00 the road to Doi Suthep is closed to cars: thousands of people walk 11 km (~3 hours) to the temple for the Wian Tian candlelit procession; there are songthaews for 50 baht. Free food and water along the way; alcohol is forbidden.
items.a: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep (start at the Kruba Srivichai Monument)
items.h: 30 May from 16:00 and all night; festival on 31 May

items.n: Water pump repair and water filtration systems
items.d: Sales, design, installation and maintenance of filtration and water supply systems, cartridges and spare parts, pump repair; free site assessment.
Another water pump repair company from the same recommendation.
A “handyman” for any home repair who also helps with moving; according to a review, he arrives on time and works unhurriedly and thoroughly.
An Italian restaurant with Italian-style sandwiches of 18 and 25 cm made from quality ingredients.

items.n: Parking and “No Parking” signs in Chiang Mai: fines
items.d: A parking ban can apply before the sign too; a red-and-white curb means no parking, yellow-and-white means short-term, “ตลอดแนว” means along the whole line. Fines are more frequent in Old City and Nimman: up to 2000 baht, payment by QR or at the police, the car is clamped.

A private hotel with just 3 rooms, 30 minutes from Mae Rim: a romantic atmosphere, a garden with a deck leading to the river, a chef’s table dinner in a glass pavilion, a luxurious breakfast. You can visit the restaurant without staying.
A branch of the Italian gelato shop 7 Senses at JJ Market; vegan flavors available, delivery via TukTuk and GrabFood.
The 7 Senses Gelato factory in Phuket: wholesale sales and full service.
A beautiful villa in a “manor house” style; booking via Agoda.

items.n: Long-term visas: Thai Elite, investor, marriage, guardian, retirement
items.d: A continuation of the visa review: Thai Elite from 600 thousand baht for 5 years; an investor visa for buying housing from a developer from 10 million baht; marriage and guardian visas (500 thousand baht in a bank); retirement 50+ (800 thousand baht), it is better to take “O” for 90 days and extend it locally rather than O-A.
items.p: Thai Elite 600 thousand baht / 5 years, 2 million baht / 20 years

items.d: A Telegram group for home food in Chiang Mai where you can find sauerkraut; according to a message, sauerkraut is also available at “Murka”.

items.n: New community complex in Nimman (Tan Park)
items.d: A community complex under construction, 1 minute from Nimman Road, is recruiting tenants: restaurants and cafes, wellness, fitness, education and other businesses. You need to send a business profile and a contact.

items.n: Teak board stand at Central Festival
items.d: A stand across from Tops at Central Festival: handmade designer cutting boards of teak (the black one is 600 baht) and other woods (the little fish is 400 baht); the designer is at the stand in person.
items.p: teak board 600 baht, fish-shaped board 400 baht

items.n: Restaurant and hotel with a view of the temple with a Buddha in pink rhinestones
items.d: A cafe-restaurant and hotel on the way to Bangkok with a view of the temple where the Buddha is covered in pink rhinestones.

items.n: Temple with a Buddha in pink rhinestones
items.d: A temple with a Buddha in pink rhinestones on the way to Bangkok; nearby is a cafe-restaurant and a hotel with a view of it.

items.n: House and condo cleaning from 350 baht
items.d: Professional cleaning of houses and condos: a starter package of 2 hours: cleaning, mopping the floors, a UV vacuum check, thorough bathroom cleaning; extra hours on the spot. Booking via direct messages or LINE.
A Japanese izakaya: fried fish in sauce, sushi don, kushikatsu, roast beef. The restaurant’s stamp gives 2 hours of free parking in the complex’s lot behind the restaurant.
items.p: from 8 baht (as stated in the post)

items.n: Namyang Kungfu (kung fu school in Pai)
items.d: A kung fu school in Pai that also sells elite high-mountain tea from trees about 1000 years old, picked by hill tribes; you can order by direct message.

A rooftop on the 9th floor of the ICON building by the city moat with a view of the sunset and Doi Suthep; Thai and European cuisine, a full bar, above-average prices. It can be hot when there is no wind; parking in the ICON building.
items.a: Old City (by the moat), ICON building

items.d: A cafe that sells sauerkraut, but it is not always available.

items.n: Gotu kola: research and where to buy
items.d: A retelling of an OHSU study on the effect of gotu kola extract on memory in mice with Alzheimer’s (phase I is under way in humans). In local pharmacies gotu kola is sold as powder and capsules, at markets as freshly squeezed or thawed juice.

On 19–20 May 2026 the cabinet decided to return to the 30-day visa exemption instead of the 60-day one; the effective date has not been announced, and the list of countries will be reviewed by the Foreign Ministry’s visa committee.
A clinic with new check-up packages; a snack box is included.
Hemp and ramie fabric with natural dyeing, 145 cm wide: breathable, durable, quickly becomes soft. Order via Facebook, LINE or Instagram.
items.p: 280 baht per yard, 380 baht per yard with natural dyeing

items.d: A seasonal package at a 5-star hotel in the Mon Jam mountains: a night with breakfast, a donburi lunch, a dinner with kurobuta pork, a private onsen in the garden for 45 minutes, a daifuku making class. Few rooms.
A cafe from the updated list of Chiang Mai's most stylish places of 2026.

items.s: cafe with a view of planes
items.d: A cafe where you can watch the planes; it is crowded at weekends, with parents coming with kids. It can be hot on the second floor.

items.n: Thermal mascara (removed with “stockings”) on Lazada and Shopee
items.d: Links to mascara that is removed with “stockings” (thermal mascara), including a brownish one, on Lazada and Shopee.

items.d: A cafe-resort in Chiang Dao from the author’s roundup.
A cafe-restaurant at a gorgeous hotel in Chiang Dao where you can eat and look at the gallery.
A great hotel in Chiang Dao for a family stay, “has everything”.

items.d: A guesthouse in Chiang Dao.
A restaurant and hotel right against the mountain: the food is very tasty; in the light cottages you can get cold at night.

items.n: Ashi Guesthouse Chiangdao บ้านอาชิ
items.d: A guesthouse near the Chiang Dao cave.
Bubble cottages in Chiang Dao; according to the author’s review, a bit dirty.
A resort and cafe: you can stay or have a coffee. The owner Joe is very hospitable, helps with renting mountain bikes and will find a guide for hiking trails.
A beautiful restaurant in Chiang Dao.
A coffee shop in Chiang Dao.
A glamping site in Chiang Dao, in the author’s words “an amazing place, 100 in one”.

items.d: A resort close to luxury; you can stop by the cafe: a lake, animals, golf, archery, many photo spots.
A place in Chiang Dao where “everything is beautiful”.
A place in Chiang Dao that holds fabric dyeing workshops; the author notes the amazing techniques.
A place in Chiang Dao for creative activities, “maybe Dao will inspire you to create something”.
A wooden guesthouse in Chiang Dao.
A cafe and rooms in Chiang Dao; very tasty food and drinks, the brioche with Nutella is praised.
A secluded villa with a very cozy interior, a maid, a seawater pool and floor-to-ceiling windows with a mountain view; there are occasional promotions.
A new boutique hotel in Chiang Dao, in the author’s opinion the most beautiful of all; it has a restaurant and even a gallery.

items.n: Cafe with a view in the national park (Chiang Dao)
items.d: A place with an amazing view in the park: the guards let us in without payment when we said we were going to the cafe. There is no internet at the top, so it is better to bring cash.
A Thai cafe in Chiang Dao that the roundup’s author calls a “Thai food bomb”.
One of the best khao soi, moderate prices.
A budget place with big portions and one of the best khao soi in town; it's small, and there can be queues.
A noodle shop: yen ta fo (noodles in a pink broth) for 40 baht and a clear soup with noodles and pork for 30 baht; prices have not been raised despite rising costs.
items.p: yen ta fo 40 baht, noodle soup with pork 30 baht

items.n: The Organic Yard by Mahasuk Farm
items.d: A shop of selected natural goods: fresh organic products, healthy food and snacks, home and lifestyle goods. Opened in a soft opening format.
A new atmospheric coffee shop on the grounds of a farm in Hang Dong.

items.n: ข้าวซอยแอนด์โค | ข้าวซอยเชียงใหม่ ช้างเผือก Khao Soi & Co
items.d: A place from the khao soi roundup.
Retro cameras sold via Instagram: you can calmly look everything over and order without searching a flea market.
A weekend brunch with barbecue, cold cuts and “the biggest cheese buffet” in Chiang Mai, more than 40 kinds of cheese; prosecco is included in the price.
A coffee shop and bakery: sourdough donuts with feta, bread and pastries on a starter collected around the world, desserts, coffee; even the butter for the toast gets praise. Good for breakfast.
A shop from the “heavy luxury” selection of vintage and second-hand (mentioned twice in the list).

items.n: Tasty mango varieties and where to buy them
items.d: Tips: the “pink lady” variety from Makro is very tasty; the “red emperor” is available at Makro, Rimping, Jing Jai and other markets; the “caramel” variety has been delivered to Rimping Hang Dong; cheap “wooden” mangoes ripen buttery and fiberless.
Lymphatic massage; it is advised to take two hours, there is a herbal sauna. Book in advance.
A salon that does lifting facial massage.
A decor shop more than 35 years old: three floors of interior goods.
A hotel in Chiang Rai; at the time of the post there was a discount on a 53 m² room with breakfast, rooms are being snapped up quickly.
Accommodation in the Mae Rim area with a 270 m² room; booking via Agoda.

A beautiful, secluded reservoir where you can go cycling on weekends; there are many cafes around.
