items.d: A hair salon recommended by a long-time client; the stylists themselves walk around with bright colored hair. One of the stylists has an Instagram.
They are looking for volunteers for a free 60-minute full-body lymphatic drainage massage (the new Lymphatic Drainage Physiologique protocol) in exchange for an honest review.

items.n: Phuang Mani durian (พวงมณี)
items.d: A small sweet variety with golden creamy flesh and a caramel taste, peak season in May; usually 150–200 baht/kg, tree-ripened costs more. Found at Rimping: an unusual taste, no fibers, but half the weight is seeds.
items.p: usually 150–200 baht/kg, tree-ripened up to 500–700 baht

items.n: Chiang Mai districts: where to live
items.d: An overview of 12 districts: Old City and Tha Phae for a first trip; Nimman for cafes and nomads; Santitham, Chang Phueak, Jed Yod cheaper and more local; Night Bazaar hotels and shopping; Riverside/Wat Ket calm; Hang Dong, Mae Hia, Mae Rim families and villas.

items.s: Russian groceries, cottage cheese and baked goods
items.d: A shop with bread, farmer’s cheese (tvorog), desserts and Borodinsky bread; orders can be made through the group. Fresh tvorog, casserole and sochniki from its own production.
A private hospital; at the time of the post there were big discounts on check-ups.

items.n: Dentistry and check-ups in Vietnam: price reviews
items.d: Reviews: on Phu Quoc a filling is about 11 euros, a crown 130 euros, 5 fillings in an hour; in Da Nang a $120 check-up includes 5 different ultrasounds, a chest X-ray, blood and urine tests.

items.n: Yi Peng lantern festival and Loy Krathong: tickets and information
items.d: A ticket-selling site for the lantern festival (Yi Peng Lantern Festival) and a kampatour page with details about the Loy Krathong and Yi Peng festivals.
A massage therapist who makes house calls (a Facebook page from the “Massage at home” selection).
A massage therapist who makes house calls (a Facebook page from the “Massage at home” selection).
A massage therapist who makes house calls (a Facebook page from the “Massage at home” selection).

Pop-up dinners by Earn (owner of a 12-year-old pasta restaurant, POHSOP and The Green Athlete) on Fridays–Sundays at a secret location: à la carte or a 7-course tasting set accommodating allergies. The pesto is praised.

items.n: DTV visa: what to do after the first 180 days
items.d: Options: once per entry, extend by 180 days at Immigration (requirements depend on the office) or leave and re-enter. On entry have the DTV approval, TDAC, 20 000 baht, an onward ticket, proof of accommodation and income; check the DTV stamp and the 180 days.
A designer clothing shop — “if you want something special”.
A farm with programs for children and adults: rice planting, egg collecting, photos with and bathing a buffalo, a mud slide, animal feeding, making Thai cakes; there is a restaurant.
items.p: morning 10:00–12:00 1250 baht (with lunch), day 890 baht; companions 600/200 baht; buffalo 120–150 baht, food 20 baht

items.d: A campsite with all-day entertainment: pond fishing, archery, marshmallows, open-air cinema, free bicycles, a separate children’s area with a slide; beautiful tents.
The guys clean air conditioners at 500 baht each, work quickly all over the city, but only in houses, not condos; they also sell used air conditioners. No contacts are given in the post text.
The largest sky lantern festival in Thailand at Mungmana Farm (San Pa Tong): 100 000 lanterns at once, Loy Krathong, Lanna dances and drums. Tickets sell out fast, sales will open soon.

items.n: New durian shop with durians from Chanthaburi
items.d: A new durian shop (opened on May 12, 2026), the owner speaks good English and brought 3500 kg from Chanthaburi; she plans to stay for the whole season.
Motorbike rental (a Facebook page).
Another option for cycling clothes, including one with a kitten print; a Facebook link.
An online shop of professional swimsuits by an Australian brand for the pool and sport: bright colors, excellent quality, period swimwear is available.
An online shop of beautiful swimsuits and sportswear.
An online shop of lingerie and swimsuits.

According to the author, a very beautiful restaurant with a gorgeous terrace and even an elevator to the second floor, in the Mae Hia area; rumor has it the opening of filming of the Chinese show The Chinese Restaurant (May 2026) took place nearby.

A private pool villa for 2 people in Mae Taeng (304 Moo 1, Kud Chang): breakfast, shabu dinner and rafting are included in the price, a grill, a net hammock, floating breakfast. There is only one house; cancellation is not possible, rescheduling once within 10 working days.
items.p: 5,900 baht per night (promotion, usually 7,500); extra bed adult 1,300, child 5–12 years 1,000 baht

items.d: According to the author, one of the best barbecues in the city.
A cafe on the grounds of a community of hearing-impaired people, who also serve the guests; in the city, but it feels like a forest, some tables are made from old sewing machines.

A weekly party on Wednesdays at The Moat House: salsa, bachata, kizomba, a playlist by DJ SiRi. Cash only at the entrance, no outside drinks. Siri also gives private Latin lessons, teaches DJing and stages wedding dances.

items.n: Homemade Vietnamese banh mi in Saraphi
items.d: Homemade Vietnamese baguettes, fresh baking every day: banh mi with pork and lemongrass, caramelized chicken, char siu, Vietnamese sausage, with egg. On the third ring road by the Ping River, next to Wat Tamnak.

items.n: Burmese stall with chickpea tofu at the Kad Farang night market
items.d: The Burmese seller has a huge piece of chickpea tofu for 40 baht (you can choose it not fried in batter — he makes different dishes from it on the spot) and the famous Burmese salad with fermented tea leaves.
items.h: the market runs mainly on Wednesdays and Saturdays

items.s: family restaurant with a play area
items.d: A family restaurant and cafe with a kids' play area that hosts children's birthday parties; in May 2026 it had foam parties on weekends (9–10, 16–17), 50 baht entry with no time limit.
The club plays at the Hai Ya courts seven days a week from 8:00 to 13:00 (3 courts), provides balls, nets and rental rackets; all levels are welcome, Haiya is a good place to start.
A pickleball center with many good coaches.
A pickleball center with many good coaches.

items.n: Reclub app for finding sports and partners
items.d: The Reclub app shows sports activities near you (not only pickleball) and helps you find players.
A cafe with capybaras, entry 400 baht. The name is not given in the post.
A new seafood cafe with seafood from Surat Thani, everything fresh; crab curry and crab fried rice.
Another crew for cleaning and installing air conditioners, the same price — 500 baht. No contacts are given in the post text.
Mini golf and classic German cuisine — a place for families and friends. Access is partly difficult because of roadworks: go by Google Maps (Hangdong Minigolf) or follow the detour signs.
items.p: mini golf: adults 100 baht, children 50 baht

items.d: A new 5-floor creative space studio. From May 9, 2026 (from 16:00) and daily until the end of the month, a family art event: a free mini gallery and artwork swap, you can draw on the spot.
A railway park where people run, walk dogs and do fitness; by the parking lot, roughly from 18:00 to 20:00 (in two sessions), there are free aerobics classes for all ages.
On aqicn.org you can view the history of the air quality index in Chiang Mai by smog season and compare years.
Organic tomatoes from Mae Taeng for sale; free delivery within 15 km of Saraphi District for orders from 450 baht.
items.p: 130 baht/1 kg, 450 baht/4 kg, 1 000 baht/10 kg

items.d: An elephant sanctuary in Pong Yaeng (Mae Rim), near Panviman.
A popular place in Mae Rim near Panviman; the post does not specify what exactly it is.
A sweet cafe in a Japanese village style with big grounds, near Mon Jam on Pong Yaeng mountain.

A five-star hotel in Mae Rim: a huge green territory, several pools, a warm jacuzzi, a spa, sun loungers with a view of the lakes, a good breakfast, a kids’ corner; guests are driven around the grounds in carts. There were good discounts, the price includes breakfast for two.
A beautiful glamping site in the Mae Rim area, not far from Panviman.
A cute white hotel in Mae Rim.
A gorgeous “bubble” (a transparent dome for sleeping) in Mae Rim. The name is not given in the post.
A place to grab a bite near Panviman. The name is not given in the post.
A pleasant campsite as an alternative to a hotel in the Mae Rim area. The name is not given in the post.
A place with roses; it is worth going in the blooming season. The name is not given in the post.

Another cozy hotel in the Mae Rim area. The name is not given in the post.

According to the author, the best place for back problems, muscle pain, insomnia, headaches, sciatica and joint problems.

The physiotherapist Maxwell worked with one of the best neurosurgeons in the UK. The description seems to belong here too: physiotherapy through Pilates, recovery after surgeries and injuries, two branches in the city.
Another good physiotherapist (สิริคลินิกกายภาพบำบัด).
A physiotherapy clinic from the selection of recommendations for back and joint pain.

A rehabilitation clinic (doctors Dew and Nat), also very cool according to the author.
A daily evening kayaking tour: 6 km and more than 2 hours of calm paddling, single and double kayaks; in May 2026 a 2-for-1 offer.
A new retro-style cafe in the Old City (in the square) with the atmosphere of a small American town of the 70s.

items.n: Crab curry stall at Central Festival
items.d: A stall in Central Festival closer to Amazon and the exit on its side; the crab curry and crab rice are praised.
A home baker makes vegan gluten-free bread from buckwheat flour and ground flax, without vinegar, with vegetable oils; the author orders regularly. Order via Facebook.

items.n: AOT airport fee increase from June 20, 2026
items.d: AOT raises the fee for international departures from 730 to 1 120 baht per person from June 20, 2026 at 6 airports, including Chiang Mai; it is usually included in the ticket price. The fee for domestic flights stays 130 baht.

A shop of Monthong durians from Chanthaburi (grade A flesh, no chemicals): they sell peeled sets and fresh lots and publish prices on Facebook, free delivery within the city. Payment only after receipt.

items.n: Coconut stall at Hang Dong Market
items.d: A stall at Hang Dong Market: a 1,5 l bottle of fresh coconut water for 70 baht — cheaper and fresher than in shops.
Weekly padel events; there is an event for beginners with a free training session with a ball-feeding machine. You can join through the WhatsApp group.
A salon where the author takes a mix: a foot massage, then face, and at the end a massage of the back of the neck, ears and head. The post does not give the name.
A beautiful art studio near Kad Farang; opening on Thursday, May 7, 2026 at 18:00.

items.n: Bike shop with repair and coffee
items.d: A bike shop: a sale of cycling clothes, bike sales and repair, plus good coffee. The post does not give the name.
A yakiniku place with premium kinds of meat; the fish is excellent too.
A lab clinic in San Sai; for blood tests — “definitely” here.
A clinic praised by old-timers, surgeries included. The post does not give the name.
An ENT doctor at Bangkok Hospital; the reviewer is thrilled — she has the patience even for a difficult patient.
A doctor who speaks excellent English.
A small office, by the review — like a general practitioner: they advise on health and test results, including for children; they speak English, many good reviews.
A restaurant on the grounds of a luxury boutique hotel in an old 19th-century teak building; piano is played in the evenings. Suits a romantic dinner, breakfast and a special occasion.
A WhatsApp chat for those learning AI programming, agents and workflows: to share knowledge and optimize processes.
A vegan place that added massaman curry with chickpeas to the menu. The post does not give the name.
A French bakery, by the author’s account some of the best bread and baguettes in the city: everything is sourdough, the flour is from France; also pâté, jam, butter and desserts. Available on Grab.
A durian shop where in the 2026 season sales grew from 1 to 2 tons a day; the most popular variety is Monthong, you can check the taste and get a replacement.

A coworking from the summer list of places to escape the heat. The post does not give the name.
A sauna from the summer list of places to relax. The post does not give the name.

items.n: A pool, a restaurant and pigs
items.d: A pool, a restaurant and pigs; worth a visit with kids and for colorful photos in a glamorous “grandma’s village” atmosphere. The post does not give the name.

items.n: A place for sunset, barbecue and live music
items.d: A place where you can watch the sunset and grill barbecue to live music. The post does not give the name.

items.n: A glamorous place by a pond in the city
items.d: A glamorous place by a pond within the city, from the summer list. The post does not give the name.

items.n: A water park with adrenaline slides
items.d: By the author’s account, the most adrenaline-inducing water park in the area. The post does not give the name.
A place where you can relax in a river on a budget. The post does not give the name.

items.n: A place to ride with music and sunset
items.d: You can ride to your heart’s content and tone up to good music, find like-minded people, watch the sunset and grill barbecue; the glass noodle salad is praised. What kind of riding it is and the name — not given in the post.

items.n: Clean water, free bikes and a night in a tree
items.d: You can swim in clean water, ride bikes for free and stay overnight in a treehouse. The post does not give the name.

items.n: A dam with rafts for kids
items.d: A family place by a dam: kids ride rafts, parents sit under shelters, eating and drinking. The post does not give the name.

items.n: A farm with loungers over the water
items.d: A cool atmosphere: a farm and loungers over the water, you can sit in a hammock net, eat and feed the fish. The post does not give the name.
Rafting from the summer list of water activities. The post does not give the name.

Mala Tang is a spicy Chinese build-your-own soup: you choose the ingredients yourself, they are cooked in a broth with chili and Sichuan pepper; the fried version without broth is Mala Xiang Guo. The list has 5 places in Chiang Mai.
A malatang place where students like to hang out. The post does not give the name.

items.n: Malatang with stir-fried mala and tomato broth
items.d: The stir-fried mala (Mala Xiang Guo) and the tomato version are especially praised here. The post does not give the name.
A popular malatang place with queues: while you wait for the soup, women get a manicure, there is a show, and long-haired guests are given a hair tie. The post does not give the name.
A “glamorous” malatang place from the list. The post does not give the name.
One more popular malatang place from the list. The post does not give the name.

items.n: Where to buy durian in Chiang Mai and how to choose
items.d: Cheapest at Hang Dong Market; durians are sold at almost all night markets, at Mae Hia and at Jing Jai Market; at the Night Bazaar and the CMU night market cut durian is sold, a bit pricier. The best variety is Monthong, buy in the morning, the fruit should be slightly firm.
A durian outlet from the list where pleasant service is praised. The post does not give the name.
A wholesale market where you can find very good, usually large and tasty durians, but the prices are not the lowest. The post does not give the name.
A place where you can buy durian cheaply in the morning. The post does not give the name.
An outlet near Hang Dong Market: a big choice of durians and good prices, from 99 baht. The post does not give the name.

items.n: Durians: you can come and taste
items.d: A place that is convenient to come to and try durian. The post does not give the name.
By the author’s account, the most wholesale fruit market, which also sells durians. The post does not give the name.

A temple in the middle of Kwan Phayao lake, more than 500 years old, reached by boat; for the province’s 50th anniversary in 2027 a large-scale restoration of the temple and the pier is under way. The lake has a beautiful embankment without wires.
A recommendation of where to find a good kitchen knife: two Lazada links.
A place for gastronomic experiences; the author advises booking in advance, as prices are going up soon.

A little-known museum: a traditional wooden Lanna complex on 27 rai with 20+ houses of padauk, teak and mahogany, the main house on 208 columns; on May 10 a Kad Mua traditional food market and a cart ride.

Repair of iPhones, iPads and phones (screens, batteries, back covers without replacing the body); free delivery of the device there and back within the center. Behind Thanin Market, Wiang Bua alley, opposite Kin Wan Mala, there is parking.
A very beautiful coffee shop with Turkish coffee and an atmosphere from “Aladdin”.

The largest and most modern sports complex of the province in Mae Rim District: popular for walks and morning/evening runs, Doi Suthep is visible; a full set of facilities, the tennis court was renovated last year.

items.n: Thai restaurant with a view of rice fields
items.d: A restaurant of northern and traditional Thai cuisine that grew out of the Khok Nong Na Model project: a view of rice fields and the sunset over the On Tai community, a kids’ playground, dogs are welcome. The post does not give the name.
A new burger place that already has many fans.
According to the author, one of the best shops for meat delicacies and more; the post has a promo from the shop. The name is not given, there is a map link.
A spa that, by the author’s account, also offers Yam Khang fire massage, but in a more comfortable and refined setting.
A review of RTC buses: cold AC, clean and spacious, there is a bus tracking system, a single fare of 30 baht for the whole route.

A restaurant with a rose garden (more than 3000 roses), a Western barn-style building, a Zen garden and a tea house behind a torii gate; coffee and tea. Sri Boon Ruang Soi 4 off Mahidol Rd, opposite Region 5 Police HQ, near the Nong Hoi intersection.
A city park in the center of Chiang Mai: you can relax, have a picnic on a blanket or walk in the shade of big trees.

items.n: Chiang Mai Provincial Administrative Organization Park
items.d: A spacious park for walks, runs and bike rides; quiet, with a view of Nong Ho and Doi Suthep.
A big lake with pavilions and restaurants by the water; there are zones with King Kong figures, Swiss windmills, sheep and a view of Doi Suthep.
Classes for kids aged 6–11: an art and creativity class, a cooking class and digital drawing in Procreate. The post does not give the name; there is a map and Facebook.

A traditional northern practice: the healer wets the foot with herbal oil, touches a red-hot plowshare and passes the heat to the body through the foot. The post names these places: Ban Rai Kong Khing, Baan Hom Phaya, Fah Lanna Spa.
A community tourism village about 30 minutes south of the center; according to the post, the best-known place for authentic Yam Khang fire massage.
Another place that does traditional Lanna Yam Khang fire massage.
They make two-layer wooden items with engraved text or images and through-cut work: keychains, medals, souvenirs; also leather and handmade items to order.
A cafe with Italian ice cream and its own baking.

items.n: House for rent near Meechok Plaza
items.d: A new two-storey house of 180–200 m² (2 bathrooms, 2 kitchens, 2 living rooms) about 300 m from Meechok Plaza / Ruamchok market, for living or business. No pets; deposit of 3 months + 1 month in advance.

items.n: Tourist Police app Police i lert u
items.d: A free app of the Royal Police (Google Play, App Store) for calling the Tourist Police in case of an accident, theft, assault or fraud; Russian is available, GPS and photo sending. Hotline 1155 around the clock.
Motorhomes by a stream in the Doi Saket area, 45 minutes from the center: for 2–3 people, a private bathroom, free breakfast, every one has a view of the stream.
items.p: from 1 190 baht for 2 people, Friday–Saturday 1 390 baht (until May 31, 2026)

items.n: Professions forbidden to foreigners in Thailand
items.d: A list of 27 professions reserved only for Thai citizens (per the Ministry of Labour): including driving, hairdressing and beauty services, Thai massage, guiding, street vending, secretarial work, legal services.
A new coworking place (a cafe) where some yoga classes are also held.

items.n: Live Band Karaoke at Lecker Café & Bistro
items.d: A new weekly event at Lecker Café & Bistro: karaoke with a live band on Fridays from 20:00, starting May 1, 2026.
T-shirts with a Hanuman design inspired by the mosaic of the Wat Arun temple: 100% cotton 220 GSM, DTG printing. A gift idea; also sometimes found in Central.

items.n: La bibliothèque de l’EFEO Chiang Mai
items.d: A French library on the bank of the Ping River: a large collection of books on Thailand, Asia, Buddhism, culture and history, old trees and quiet; also suitable as a place to work.

A dance studio: jazz, tap, ballet and contemporary dance for beginners and pros; led by Laura Peterson, a former teacher and professional dancer from the USA. The first lesson is free, with plenty of parking.

The Ministry of Digital Economy and Society and the Department of Land Transport decided not to extend the license of the ride-hailing platform Bolt: the company did not improve driver recruitment and vetting on time (April 2026).

items.n: Hang nok yung farang trees in bloom by the moat
items.d: From March to May, hang nok yung farang trees (“French peacock tail”) with bright orange flowers bloom lushly along the city moat, a pretty spot for a walk and a photo shoot.
items.h: in bloom from March to May

items.d: A weekly evening at Sense Dhara Dhevi Wellness Club: thermal wellness, a sound journey, a live DJ set and a demonstration of Lanna fire foot massage Yam Khang. The grounds also have a coffee shop with desserts and an Italian restaurant.

items.n: Smog and PM2.5 in Northern Thailand
items.d: An overview of the smog problem: the season is usually January–April, the main sources are forest fires and agricultural burning; PM2.5 penetrates the lungs and blood, and heart and lung diseases are increasing. Residents have to rely on masks and air purifiers.
Big durians at 129 baht per kg (late April 2026); in a few weeks the season will get better, with more fruit, lower prices and higher quality. The name is not given in the post.
You can build your own seafood bowl; tables by the river, you can spread a mat and have a picnic; there is a trampoline and a playground for kids. The name is not given in the post.

A restaurant with British pies (steak and kidney, cheese, vegetarian with massaman), artisan bread with garlic and rosemary and mint ice cream from its own garden. Delivery and takeaway are available.
A place of worship for those born in the Year of the Dog: their stupa is considered to be in the Tavatimsa heaven, so they usually come to Wat Ket Karam.
A cozy place for breakfast.
Isan cuisine in the city center area: juicy pork neck, tom yum, nam tok, you can sit with friends over beer. Opposite is a Thai dessert shop, with street food and Thai bars with live music around.
Not far from Withilarb; good pad thai and yum woon sen (a spicy glass noodle salad).
An Isan place in the city center area: lots of snacks and beer, the staff speak good English.
An Isan restaurant popular with local Thais; it has existed for several decades.
An Isan restaurant popular with local Thais; it has existed for several decades.
Excellent ribs; a relaxed place to sit with beer and a grill.
A place you can come to work: air conditioning, quiet, almost no people and very comfortable armchairs. The name is not given in the post, there is a map link.
A recommendation of some of the best ready-made roti for home cooking, for example with massaman curry; Lazada links.
A clinic for facial skin care and treatment (including Botox): reasonable prices, a big choice of procedures, no pushing of extras. Dr. Ratika is gentle and speaks good English.
A recommended driving school that processes documents quickly. The name is not given in the post, there is a map link.
A Facebook group where you can find housing for the short, medium and long term; many authentic listings.
A coffee shop in the Old City (in the square), sometimes open from 6:30 in the morning; the owner Woody makes coffee to your taste and is happy to chat. All ratings are 5.
A 24-hour National Parks Department hotline: call if you see an injured wild animal or a forest fire being set.

A gym in Chang Khian (~2.5 km from Nimman, by Huay Kaew Rd and Canal Rd): machines, a boxing zone, a studio for trainers; no contracts and no automatic renewal. Opening on 4 May 2026, open day on 2 May 09:00–16:00.
items.p: single visit 200 baht, week 600 baht, month 1,200 baht; founding member 600 baht for 30 days, then 1,000 baht/month

items.d: A classic of northern cuisine: green chili peppers stuffed with chopped pork and herbs, battered and deep-fried, with a tangy sauce; not very spicy. Look for them at evening markets.
The Thai word farang (falang) means white foreigners, comes from the Persian Frank and is usually not considered racist; it also means guava.

A famous northern curry of pork (sometimes beef) without coconut milk, with ginger and garlic, slightly sweet, sour and spicy; connected with Lanna culture and Myanmar. The post lists 8 places where it is tasty.
One of 8 places where, according to the post, hung lay (a northern pork curry without coconut milk) is cooked well. The name is not given in the post.
One of 8 places where, according to the post, hung lay (a northern pork curry without coconut milk) is cooked well. The name is not given in the post.
One of 8 places where, according to the post, hung lay (a northern pork curry without coconut milk) is cooked well. The name is not given in the post.

One of 8 places where, according to the post, hung lay (a northern pork curry without coconut milk) is cooked well. The name is not given in the post.
One of 8 places where, according to the post, hung lay (a northern pork curry without coconut milk) is cooked well. The name is not given in the post.
A recommendation of nail polishes: less harmful, long-lasting, with pretty semi-transparent layers; the same brand has handy wipes for removing nail polish. Lazada links.

items.n: Major Cineplex Central Chiang Mai Airport
items.d: The Major cinema in the Central Chiang Mai Airport mall after its renovation (April 2026): a big GLS hall with comfortable seats, and LASERPLEX 4K laser projectors in all halls.
A new trendy place: tasty food, cocktails, live music and the atmosphere of a New York loft.
According to the author, the best tom yum in Chiang Mai; the soft-shell crab with salt and pepper, gaeng hang lay (northern curry) and pomelo salad (som-o) are also praised.
Chiang Mai Zoo: on 14 April 2026 a calf was born to the hippos (the fifth family member); photo zones were set up for visitors in the hippo area.
Yulia bakes homemade pastries to order (honey cake, kulich with coconut cream or lemon curd and more), order a day ahead. Pickup from Santitham or Grab delivery at the buyer’s expense.
items.p: kulich ~430 g: 300 baht (with coconut cream), 390 baht (with lemon curd)

items.d: A sale on Friday mornings: sour Royal Project plums (suitable instead of cherries in pies), and at the entrance a stall with rice and flowers: brown broken rice 3 kg for 60 baht, golden mountain flax 80 baht.
items.p: rice 3 kg — 60 baht; mountain flax — 80 baht

items.d: A cafe opened by a former monk: you can learn meditation, get recommendations for meditation centers and track brain waves through an app.

items.n: Infinity Medical Clinic Central Chiangmai Airport
items.d: A clinic in Central Chiangmai Airport; an underarm care program: 8 laser hair removal sessions + 8 masks + 8 vitamin treatments for 1 999 baht (with online booking).

items.n: Infinity Medical Clinic Central Festival Chiang Mai
items.d: A clinic in Central Festival; an underarm care program: 8 laser hair removal sessions + 8 masks + 8 vitamin treatments for 1 999 baht (with online booking).
A center for prevention and health recovery: in-depth medical examinations with biochemistry analysis under the supervision of doctors. On the Chiang Mai–Lampang Superhighway, before Makro.

items.n: Medical Trend Lab Center Bo Sang
items.d: A laboratory and check-up center in Bo Sang (San Kamphaeng): test packages from 690 baht (Starter) to 2 390 baht (Supreme) and 4 590 baht (Beyond, for men/women, with tumor markers and hormones).

items.n: Medical Trend Lab Iblis Sahaklinik Branch
items.d: A branch of the Medical Trend laboratory opposite Chiang Mai 1 bus station: annual test packages from 690 baht (Starter) to 4 590 baht (Beyond).
A branch of the Medical Trend Lab chain in Hang Dong near Kad Farang: annual test packages from 690 baht (Starter) to 4 590 baht (Beyond).

items.n: House for rent in San Pa Tong
items.d: A house with 2 bedrooms and 1 bathroom on a 400 m² plot in San Pa Tong: the Mae Kan river behind, a rice field in front, 80 m to the main road, a 7-Eleven 200 m away, about 35 minutes to the airport. No pets, move-in from May.

items.n: Paying by Thai QR through SberBank Online
items.d: In the “SberBank Online” app you can pay for purchases in Thailand by Thai QR: the amount is converted to rubles, available at 6+ million points. You need app version Android 16.10 / iOS 17.0 or newer.
A pastry shop; the post praises the Hummingbird Cake as delightful.

items.n: Fermented tea leaves for lahpet thoke
items.d: Leaves for the Burmese salad lahpet thoke can be ordered on Lazada or bought at the Chinatown night market in the first stalls next to the 7-Eleven.

An international football academy for boys and girls aged 4–14: licensed coaches, weekly matches and tournaments, free kit, training at different venues around the city. A free two-week trial program.

items.n: Book club for newcomers in Chiang Mai
items.d: A small book club for those who have recently moved or feel lonely: they read a little, talk a lot, meet new people; most people come alone. Join through the group at the link.

items.n: A pretty place for a cup of something (near the jewelry store and silk)
items.d: A place not so much for eating as for looking at pretty things and having a cup of something; touristy, with a huge jewelry store and Thai silk next door.
A huge jewelry store and a Thai silk shop in a tourist spot: tourist prices (silk pillowcases are cheaper on Lazada), but you can walk around and take photos.
A Hong Kong/Chinese restaurant with delivery: fish soup with mala, bean sprouts and noodles (the mala doesn't overpower the taste); by prior arrangement they cook to individual request.
A salon that fixes cracked heels: a foot spa/pedicure session of about 70 minutes, promo price 299 baht until the end of the month (April 2026).

A new shady public space on the bank of the Ping River by Rattanakosin Bridge, opposite the Wang Singkham ice factory (Chang Moi); on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays 9:00–12:00 volunteers give free haircuts.
A beautiful brunch cafe with a homey atmosphere: Beef Wellington, Egg Royale, a Changmoi katsu bagel.
An interesting Jiaogulan herbal tea, which can be found at local organic farms, at Warorot Market and other markets, and also on Lazada.

items.n: Hulled hemp seeds from the Royal Project
items.d: Royal Project hulled hemp seeds with a nutty taste: protein, omega-3/6/9; add to smoothies, oatmeal, salads. Store in the refrigerator. Order by phone in Chiang Mai.

items.n: “8 Peng” festival at Wat Sri Luang Chae Son
items.d: An annual festival with the bathing of the relic at Wat Sri Luang Chae Son temple (Mueang Pan, Lampang) on April 30 – May 1, 2026: a unique procession of 40+ masked “Phi Khon”, bung fai rocket launches, ramwong until midnight.

A good cat hotel in Mae Hia: basic room 250 baht/day, cats are let out to walk in the corridor several times a day, photos and videos are sent, a round-the-clock camera, cats are washed and dressed up.
A stylish boxing studio, accepts beginners and experienced boxers; the first class at a 50% discount.
One of the worthy places for breakfast in the center, the tea is especially praised.
Google Maps now lets you check air quality, handy in smog season.

items.n: Arsenic and heavy metals in the Kok, Sai, Ruak and Mekong rivers
items.d: High arsenic content has been found in the rivers of the north (Kok, Sai, Ruak, Mekong) because of illegal mines in Myanmar; heavy metals have also been found in vegetables. Fish is officially safe to eat, but it is advised not to eat the innards.

items.n: Turkey: where people buy it every year
items.d: Turkey imports are currently banned, but it can be found: a place where the author buys turkey every year (prices and a contact were in the photo); a farm without reviews with a phone number on the map is also mentioned.
A relatively new branch of the After You pastry shop in Nimman with cool desserts; parking is a problem.

items.n: Nomad Friendly District in the Wat Ket area
items.d: A government-supported project: to make part of the Wat Ket area a zone for nomads with open coworking spaces, bike paths, a maker space and events (a Baltic midsummer festival in June, CosmoLocal CNX in September). The idea's author is John H, founder of Alt_ Chiang Mai.
The Anantara resort in Chiang Mai, which the author shares as a beautiful place.
Sushi that “never lets you down”; from a list of places to order via Grab.
For those who want something spicy and rich; from a list of places to order via Grab.
Recommended for dinner; from a list of tasty places to order via Grab.

items.n: Songkran days in the Lanna tradition
items.d: Songkran in Lanna: Sangkhan Long is cleaning and purification, Wan Nao is preparation and sand stupas, Wan Phaya Wan (Wan Thaloeng Sok, 15.04) is the real New Year, a temple and the “dam hua” rite; on Pak Pi Day people eat jackfruit curry for luck.
A relatively new spa salon, the acupressure massage is praised.
They make jackfruit curry with black pepper and curry with meat and jackfruit; it is better to order directly via LINE, cheaper than via Grab, and delivery is free nearby.
Chicken noodles, from a list of tasty places to order via Grab.
Very tasty beef noodles, there are noodles with stewed buffalo; from a list of places to order via Grab.
Very affordable desserts; from a list of places to order via Grab.
A sourdough bread bakery: you can order delivery, sit in, or take a sourdough bread baking workshop.

A beautiful, not very crowded temple with pleasant music; at Songkran you can set birthday candles, flags by the sacred tree and pour water over the feet of the Buddha statues. A way to celebrate quietly without the bustle.
A place with a pool by a lake with geese and a view of the horizon: in the evening you can swim, order food and sit; there is an almost empty gym.
Northern Chinese cuisine: lamb skewers and hotpot with lamb vertebrae (cheaper than at the other place mentioned), homemade noodles, the beef burger with cumin is praised.
A children's clinic (pediatrician) in the Hang Dong / Nong Khwai area, open on holidays; you can come in to rest in a room with clean air on days of heavy smog. Booking by phone or Messenger.

items.n: Children at Songkran in smog season: a checklist
items.d: Risks: heat stroke, PM2.5 and dirty water (skin, conjunctivitis). Check the AQI before going out, wear a water-resistant N95 mask and change it when wet, rinse the nose with saline solution, with allergies go indoors with an air purifier.
A budget place that cooks fast and tasty: vegan options, meat, curries, desserts, smoothies; the cafe has a cooking school with cooking classes.
A small coffee shop where an elderly couple makes the coffee; one minute's walk from Coconut shell.
A healthy food cafe opposite Coconut shell: smoothie bowls, oatmeal, dishes with bone broth, protein and vegan options.
A Friday evening market of minimalist and cozy goods at Jing Jai Market (in front of Tops Green); on Fridays at 18:30 a free Random Dance.
items.h: every Friday (except the first Friday of the month) 16:00–21:00

items.d: A farm in Lamphun with Jersey cows and A2 milk; the products are sold at several points across Chiang Mai.
A sales point at the gate of the CMU Faculty of Agriculture where you can buy THE JOURSEY milk.
A store on Charoen Prathet Road that sells THE JOURSEY farm milk.
A Huay Kaew milk shop opposite Chiang Mai Zoo, one of the points that sell THE JOURSEY milk.
A store on Ratchawong Road that sells THE JOURSEY farm milk.
A coffee shop behind Chiang Mai University, one of the points that sell THE JOURSEY milk.
A Chinese restaurant in Hang Dong; not on Grab because of the 35% commission, order via direct messages or WhatsApp.
A pharmacy on Suthep Road south of Chiang Mai University; the pharmacist Nathan speaks fluent English, takes orders on LINE and delivers medicines quickly (under an hour).
A selection of Thai remedies from Lazada for cracked heels, a moisturizing product with glycerin and herbal extract (also sold at markets) and a nano heel file.

items.n: Chom Na Cafe (Chom Na Cafe Chiang Mai)
items.d: A cafe in the San Kamphaeng district where crispy pork on a hot skillet is recommended.

items.n: Workshop: a natural pearl and shell keychain
items.d: A workshop on making a keychain from natural pearls and shells in your own style; sign up via direct messages.
A brow and nail salon in the Phra Sing area (105, room 2, Ratchaphakhinai Road): brow or lash tinting 250 baht, brow waxing 250/400 baht; book in advance.
items.p: brow/lash tinting 250 baht; brow waxing 250/400 baht

items.d: Delivery of a whole 5–6 kg salmon to your door, cut to order (sashimi, steaks, pieces); a nam yam sauce, soy sauce and wasabi come as a gift.

items.n: Songkran at Tha Phae Gate: what to expect
items.d: A Thai person's view of Songkran in the center: it is fun only by the water and by the stage, few points to fill up water and few toilets, nowhere to sit, terrible traffic jams, you can really only get there by bike, there is no parking.

A clinic in Hang Dong (Star Avenue 5): removal of moles, papillomas, keratoses, milia with a CO₂ fractional laser from 99 baht per spot, the procedure takes about 20 minutes, done by a doctor; free consultation.

items.n: Pi Mai Mueang traditions (Lanna New Year)
items.d: Days of the Lanna Songkran: 14.04 Sangkhan Long is cleaning and washing hair with turmeric; 15.04 offerings are prepared and sand stupas built; 16.04 Phaya Wan is the temple and tung flags; 17.04 Pak Pi is the rite of respect for elders, jackfruit curry.

A district in Nong Khai province on the Mekong, nicknamed “the Chiang Mai of the northeast”: in the 16th century people from Chiang Mai who accompanied a Lanna princess and the Emerald Buddha settled here.
After discussions of cutting the visa-exempt stay to 30 days, the Thai authorities kept the option of staying 60 days without a visa to support tourism (April 2026).
A children's play area on the second floor of Big C, 290 baht for the whole day.
A restaurant with a playground, designed especially for small children, with no loud music or chaos.
Children's gymnastics with an air purifier in the hall: you can get a membership and choose between hammocks, hoop and regular gymnastics. A coffee shop next door (until 17:00) and a gym for parents.

items.n: Open Decks Night at Keo Park
items.d: An open DJ night in the Keo Park garden: 45 minutes each, sign-up on the spot, playing on the FLX-4; food and cold drinks, free entry.
A summer tennis camp for children: groups of up to 8 children, you can sign up for one day or the whole week, the focus is on confidence and enjoying the game.

A market in a shady coconut garden with dishes from fresh coconut and local food, a photo zone on a bridge over a canal, a large parking lot. Entrance from the Chiang Mai–Phrao road by the PT gas station before the Ruamchok intersection.

A traditional northern toffee-like sweet with coconut and longan in a banana leaf, a good edible souvenir. Look for it at Coconut Market, Warorot Market, night markets (Sunday Market, Chiang Mai Gate); a small pack is 50–100 baht.
A seller of kalamae with longan without preservatives, with pieces of longan instead of part of the sugar; made and shipped daily, free delivery, wholesale from 5 kg.
items.p: 110 g — 50 baht (3 pcs 140); 120 g — 65 baht (3 pcs 190); 500 g — 220 baht; 1 kg — 390 baht

items.n: Open salsa, bachata and kizomba classes
items.d: Every Sunday an open salsa, bachata and kizomba class 20:00–21:00 with no experience needed, then a social dance with DJs until 23:00. Entry: the elevator by the clock tower to the 3rd floor, on the left; tickets at the DJ table.
items.p: class + social dance 100 baht; social dance only 80 baht

items.d: An ordinary reservoir in Lop Buri where banks washed out by rain form an unusual textured landscape, a good place for photos; the shape changes every year, in the rainy season it may go under water.
A dental clinic in the Chang Phueak area, about 150 m from Rajabhat Chiang Mai University; root canal treatment from 5 000 baht, an individual plan and modern equipment.
The fee at Thai ATMs for cash withdrawals with foreign cards has risen to 350 baht, including at SCB and KBank; you can compare cheaper ways to transfer and withdraw money on monito.com.

items.n: Proof of funds on entry to Thailand
items.d: Entering under visa exemption or on a tourist visa requires at least 20 000 baht per person or 40 000 baht per family, and 10 000 baht with a visa on arrival; officials increasingly ask specifically for cash. Without it, entry may be refused.
items.p: 20 000 baht per person / 40 000 baht per family; VOA — 10 000 baht

items.d: A concentrated mask for damaged and dry hair with argan, sesame and almond oil and avocado oil; it does not weigh the hair down and lasts about 2 months. Sold through Facebook.
A cute shop of desserts, Chinese pastries and Thai sweets, convenient for choosing a gift; you can take nice photos.
A vineyard where in the harvest season you can pick grapes yourself, weigh and buy them; three varieties, a playground, a cafe in the garden, fresh grape juice.

items.s: children’s place with an air purifier
items.d: A place for children with air purifiers from a smog season selection.

items.d: A place for children with air purifiers from a smog season selection.

items.s: children’s place with an air purifier
items.d: A family restaurant for families with small children: no charge for the play area, with a trampoline, climbing frames, a yard and a room for groups; free socks. Upstairs there's massage for parents; spacious and not crowded.
items.p: play area free with a food order; a free drink for a review

items.d: A place for children with air purifiers from a smog season selection.

items.s: children’s place with an air purifier
items.d: A place for children with air purifiers from a smog season selection.
A gym with a wide choice of workouts in an enclosed space that is safe in the smog season; there are workouts for children.
A place from the updated list of Chiang Mai's most stylish places of 2026.
An aqua fitness studio: low-impact workouts in water for burning fat and recovery and for knee pain, with an individual approach.
A cafe with home baking in a green garden in Mae Rim, using the original recipes of The Baguette bakery from Hua Hin: meat, chicken and apple pies, tarts, cinnamon rolls, a croissant with sai ua.
Aquarium is a place for children with air purifiers from a smog season selection.

A large Play Space with educational toys and zones; during school holidays 3 hours cost 250 baht, a whole day 350 baht. There is Play Care 1:1 with a personal attendant (book at least a day ahead).
items.p: 3 hours 250 baht, all day 350 baht; Play Care 1:1: 3 hours 650 baht, all day 950 baht

items.n: Wednesday Play Nights at The Banyan Café
items.d: Every Wednesday by the river at The Banyan Café (Buri Sriping Riverside Resort & Spa): live 70s–90s music from Blue Brother 19:30–21:00, then DJ Yingza 21:30–22:30.
A currency exchange with one of the best rates in the city in the author’s opinion.
A currency exchange with one of the best rates in the city in the author’s opinion.
A currency exchange with one of the best rates in the city in the author’s opinion.

In hot weather centipedes (Thai: takap) appear in houses, come up through drains and hide in dishes and shoes; the bite is very painful. Advice: check shoes and things before picking them up; according to the author, they avoid surfaces treated with Dettol.
Help for foreigners: Thai driving licence, vehicle tax renewal, opening a bank account, immigration services, dealing with government offices and everyday issues. Based in San Sai.
A budget sushi restaurant run by an elderly, experienced Japanese chef; the juicy, huge mackerel is praised.
A Japanese second-hand shop with branded and other items: jackets, swimsuits, pants, hats, a large selection for boys. 5% off from 2000 baht, 10% off from 3000 baht; open even on holidays.
items.p: 5% off from 2 000 baht, 10% off from 3 000 baht

items.d: Another Japanese second-hand shop that had 30% off from 500 baht, including on furniture; open even on holidays.
A clinic of Thai and Chinese medicine and physiotherapy: lymphatic drainage facial massage, acupuncture, cupping, gua sha, electrostimulation, osteopathy, therapeutic massage.

A seasonal powder from 10+ kinds of wild mountain plants (moringa, mulberry, chamuang and others) without sugar, salt or glutamate; it can be drunk as a broth or used as a natural flavor enhancer. A batch of about 200 jars.

items.n: Chiang Mai bars with a clean ingredient list
items.d: Bars made in Chiang Mai with a natural composition and no chemicals; sold at Tops (often discounted), at Rimping and in various cafes.
An interesting temple in the Phu Ruea district of Loei province, the starting point of the Phukhrang Trail.
A studio of traditional Thai Sak Yant tattooing; they pay attention to healing and use the natural care product Pure Thai Naturals Skin Shield Aftercare. Designs, prices and booking on the website.

The author’s favorite hotel on Koh Chang: 1500 baht a night, a terrace, a jacuzzi in the room, two pools, its own bay, live music on the beach in the evening, an air-conditioned business area, a good breakfast, staff who love children.
A cafe near Mercury Hotel on Koh Chang, in the author’s words the best on the island for range and prices, and they adapt to requests; a huge smoothie for 50 baht.

A massage salon on Koh Chang that the author recommends warmly: the therapist Ning works on the pelvis through the abdomen, and the techniques differ from ordinary massage; the second therapist is a strong ladyboy for deep muscle work.
A cheaper good hotel near Mercury on Koh Chang; from it you can walk to the grounds of Mercury.
A viewpoint on Koh Chang that is especially good at sunset.
An ice cream place on Koh Chang that the author recommends for an evening walk.
A restaurant from the Michelin guide on Koh Chang with flowers in its decor, recommended by a subscriber.
An abandoned hotel on Koh Chang that you can visit for a walk.
A shop on Koh Chang with everything needed for daily life and the beach.
A vegan cafe on Koh Chang where everything is cooked fresh.
A great beach on Koh Chang, very atmospheric for evening walks; a house with a view of the bay is for rent nearby.
A place on Koh Chang that the author recommends as a pleasant spot to sit.

items.n: House for rent with a bay view (Koh Chang)
items.d: A house of about 70 m² with a view of the bay and the sea on two sides, its own kitchen and bathtub, a little over 1000 baht; a carved hotel and an atmospheric beach are nearby.
A very beautiful carved hotel on Koh Chang next to the beach; there are cabins with a terrace on the second floor, and it is romantic to watch the stars.

items.n: Vegan restaurant with a library (Koh Chang)
items.d: A superb vegan restaurant on Koh Chang with a library (there is a Russian book); very tasty, but the food takes a long time.
In the author’s opinion, the best Indian food on Koh Chang, very tasty.

items.n: Coffee shop with billiards and board games (Koh Chang)
items.d: A coffee shop on Koh Chang with billiards and board games.
A Turkish restaurant on Koh Chang, recommended by the author.
A place with good smoothies on Koh Chang.
A decent hotel on Koh Chang: rooms by the sea cost more, across the road about 800 baht per room; there is a restaurant on the beach, the food is worth the money, a good view.
items.p: about 800 baht per room across the road from the sea

items.n: Hotel by the marina with two pools (Koh Chang)
items.d: A relatively new hotel on Koh Chang with rooms of about 70 m²: a pool by the sea and on the roof, two gyms, a zipline for children on the beach, a marina and beach club nearby, a pleasant restaurant. A car is advisable.
A place with Thai food on Koh Chang, recommended by the author.
A coffee shop on Koh Chang, recommended by the author.

items.n: Hotel for a holiday with children (Koh Chang)
items.d: A place on Koh Chang that is very decent for a holiday with children, but is behind Mercury Hotel for the convenience of places to walk to.

items.n: Restaurant with a shop on the Trat – Chiang Mai road
items.d: A stop on the way from Koh Chang to Chiang Mai: a spacious shop, the restaurant cooks quickly and fresh, tasty smoothies, lots of greens with the dishes.

items.n: Koh Chang – Chiang Mai by car in one day
items.d: They drove from Koh Chang to Chiang Mai by car in a day: the first ferry at 6:30, the ferry costs 120 baht per car + 80 baht per adult, from Trat to Chiang Mai about 13 hours with stops, the gas stations on the way work.

items.n: Special Express No. 14 train Chiang Mai – Bangkok
items.d: An alternative to the CNR night train with older carriages: 1st- and 2nd-class sleepers, 2nd- and 3rd-class seating, a dining car; 16 stops, 12 h 50 min on the way. Tickets from 310 baht (3rd class) to 1 946 baht (1st class).
items.p: from 310 baht (3rd class) to 1 946 baht (1st class); 2nd class lower berth 838 baht (1 038 baht on CNR)

items.d: Ten iconic Shakespeare scenes in one performance at the open-air Heritage House & Garden venue, with the option to come early for a picnic; scenes in the original language, parental guidance is recommended. The date is not given in the post.
items.p: Early tickets — 300 baht; regular price — 375 baht

items.n: How to volunteer to fight forest fires
items.d: Registration of volunteers to fight forest fires through a Google form, information by phone; you can support by a transfer to the Mirror Foundation (SCB 507-410183-8) or through taejai.com with a tax deduction.
A popular historic temple with an ancient chedi that holds the ashes of King Muang Ketklao and Queen Visuttithewi; 50 years ago it was abandoned and was restored only after the 1990s.
A new physiotherapy clinic near Bus Terminal No. 3 (Arcade): pain relief, rehabilitation, posture analysis; professional physiotherapists and clinical equipment; first-month promotions.
items.p: Walk-in — from 690 baht; posture and movement analysis — 390 baht (first-month promo)

items.d: A 24-hour veterinary clinic with no days off, specializing in exotic animals, also dogs and cats; doctors on duty 24/7.
The largest PEA electric vehicle charging station in the north: 5 chargers of 180 kW, one of 120 kW and one of 25 kW; in front of the PEA Region 1 building, Chiang Mai–Lamphun road (Ban Den).
items.p: 180/120 kW: peak 5.90, off-peak 4.90 baht/kWh; 25 kW: peak 4.90, off-peak 3.90 baht/kWh

items.d: Raw and pasteurized milk directly from the farm owner for coffee shops, restaurants and private buyers; free delivery in Chiang Mai, San Sai, Saraphi and Hang Dong (Baan Tawai).
items.p: Raw milk: 30 baht per kg; pasteurized: 35 baht per kg

items.d: An air conditioner cleaning service — especially relevant in the PM2.5 smog season, when dust builds up inside.
Freshly picked premium figs from the farm delivered to your door; the largest and sweetest fruit are selected for the boxes.

items.n: PM2.5 smog: how to protect yourself and where to go
items.d: In the smog season (February–April): an N95 mask, less time outdoors, an air purifier, closed windows, more water. There are Pollution Clinics in Nakornping, Fang, San Sai, Sanpatong, Chomthong; online consultation at pollutionclinic.nopparat.go.th.

A quiet place with rare old Thai desserts and tea, a green garden, air purifiers in the PM2.5 season, private rooms for gatherings and birthdays; Santhisuk lane next to Chiang Mai Grandview Hotel, opposite The Vidi Condominium.
Craft chocolate; for Easter 2026, a white chocolate egg with orange jelly and lava sauce in a mini tin (limited quantity).

items.n: 300 baht fee for foreigners arriving in Thailand
items.d: The government announced a 300 baht fee for foreign tourists arriving by air; the fee for entry by land and sea is postponed for now; the exact start date as of April 1, 2026 has not been announced.
One of the biggest wholesale clothing centres in Ruamchok, with retail too: Hawaiian shirts at 100 baht each (bought for a whole team for Songkran), underwear, socks.
A “secret” dental clinic in Vietnam with a huge number of reviews and a high rating; the post does not give the name, only a map link.

A café-gallery with a creative community: Sketch Club on Wednesdays 15:00–17:00, Sound Journey on Thursdays, Not So Serious Bar on Fridays and Saturdays from 18:00; in April, workshops on floristry, watercolour, candles, soap making, perfumes and ceramics.

items.n: Ko Luang Waterfall (น้ำตกก้อหลวง)
items.d: A waterfall with blue water in Lamphun province, only 500 metres’ walk through the forest; a shady atmosphere and wild nature.
A small market of hill tribe crafts in the “Lao Cho” alley in the Kad Luang area: embroidery, ethnic fabrics, souvenirs, wholesale and retail.
Care for cats and dogs at your home or condo without moving the pet: feeding, water, cleaning, play; photo reports on the Facebook page.
A recommended pet sitter in Northern Thailand: looked after two dogs for 3 months, responsible, neat and patient; free from early April 2026.

A hotel in nature in Mae Rim, about an hour from Chiang Mai, cool all year round: a stream, ducks, a pool with a view, a Pool Suite with a warm tub, afternoon tea brought to the room; a child under 10 stays free with breakfast.
items.p: child under 10 free with breakfast (1 person)

items.d: A Japanese restaurant with seasonal ingredients: you can try hamaguri, excellent wagyu and very fresh produce.

A clinic for thorough extraction of closed comedones “to the end” and YAG laser hair removal; a promotion on the extraction — 250 baht instead of 500; branches in Kad Farang Village and Ruamchok (Chiang Mai) and in Lampang.

A rite of ordaining boys as novices among the Tai Yai (Shan) people in Mae Hong Son (Mueang, Khun Yuam, Pai) and Chiang Mai: usually in March–April, 3 days — a procession of dressed-up “luk kaew”, receiving guests and the ordination at the temple.

A Japanese izakaya with affordable prices in the Chiang Mai Culture Center (Wua Lai, opposite the Airport intersection): sushi, donburi, sukiyaki, kushikatsu from 5 baht, most dishes under 100 baht; a bar counter and parking, with a jazz club nearby.
items.p: most dishes under 100 baht, kushikatsu from 5 baht

items.d: A hotel on Koh Chang that sharply cut its prices in March 2026 because of the drop in tourists; you can drive to Trat, and from there a ferry takes you across together with your car.
Spacious villas in a good location on Koh Chang, prices dropped in March 2026; booking through Agoda.
A cocktail bar in Saraphi with a “cocktails cheaper than gas” promotion.
items.h: Monday – Saturday: from 17:00 until late evening

items.d: Dance classes for children: Jazz, Ballet, Hip-Hop and Cover Dance, suitable for any level, even with no experience; a free trial class.
A coffee shop in Phrae where a girl does creative activities with children and often films videos with them.

A weekly ecstatic dance at Vivid Dance Studios (2nd floor): ambient, tribal, house and world music from DJ Jodo, danced barefoot and in silence, with no alcohol or phones; questions go to the organizer, not the studio.
A second-hand showroom where expats sell items they cannot take with them: over 2 000 items — antiques, collectibles, art, furniture, audio equipment; some at sale prices, bargaining possible.

items.n: Morning yoga by the Ping River — Ping Pura Riverside
items.d: Morning yoga with a professional instructor by the Ping River at a Lanna-colonial style hotel, open to non-guests too; only 10 spots a day; the beautiful reception hall is good for photos.

items.n: Group for seasonal organic fruit and vegetables from farmers
items.d: A Facebook group with special prices on seasonal organic fruit and vegetables directly from farmers in Chiang Mai and Lamphun; useful for vegan and vegetarian restaurants too.

items.n: Electric tram: Red Line (Mae Hia — Royal Park Rajapruek)
items.d: The Red Line stretch from the Mae Hia Samakkhi intersection to Royal Park Rajapruek (~5 km, 5 stations, 2 Park & Ride lots) will be built in 2028–2031, with passenger service opening in 2032.

A Bangkok hotel convenient with children: a pool with slides and a bar, a big fridge, kitchen and washing machine in every room, rooms with a jacuzzi and floor-to-ceiling windows, a shop on the ground floor, good breakfasts, a top location.
A small cozy coffee shop across the road from the Jasmine Grande hotel in Bangkok; the barista does everything from the heart.
The author’s favourite vegan and vegetarian café in Bangkok, not far from the Jasmine Grande hotel.
A highly rated Italian restaurant across the road from the Jasmine Grande hotel in Bangkok.
A barbecue restaurant in Chiang Mai run by a Texan; dogs are welcome.

items.n: Services for tracking petrol availability at gas stations
items.d: Two web utilities on Google Script and the site cm-pump.com for checking which gas stations in Chiang Mai have petrol (relevant during the fuel shortage in March 2026).

items.n: Home helper: pets, ironing, cleaning, cooking
items.d: A listing for home help: pet care, ironing, cleaning and cooking; contact through Facebook.

items.s: cafe on the way to Bangkok
items.d: A pleasant café a little off the highway on the way to Bangkok: air conditioning, lots of greenery, spacious, fresh food, good coffee, and the waiters speak good English.

items.n: Park across the road from S Cafe
items.d: A park opposite S Cafe with a Thai coffee shop on its grounds and room for a walk — a stop on the way to Bangkok.

The place where rivers meet (the Ping, Wang, Yom and Nan): sometimes you can see two rivers of different colours. Entry is free, you need to sign in the registration book; on the way back there is a bridge with an elevator.
A flower café with Thai desserts not far from Passan, a great place for photo shoots.
A temple on the way to Bangkok, about an hour before the city: lots of monkeys that you can feed.
A festival of the culture of 10 hill tribes (Karen, Hmong, Lahu, Akha, Lisu) at the Highland People Discovery Museum: exhibitions, performances, a fair of local products, craft workshops.
A free museum of the peoples of the highlands, the venue of the Highland Ethnic Festival.

items.n: Volunteering in Mae Na Chang village
items.d: The Karen village of Mae Na Chang near Chiang Mai is looking for volunteers to build a homestay and paint houses: free accommodation in a shared room and meals, work of about 3 hours in the morning and 3 hours in the afternoon.

Chiang Mai has been named one of the most accessible cities for remote workers in 2026; a real budget of ~$900–1500 a month. Where to live: Nimman — lifestyle and coffee, Old City — atmosphere, Hang Dong — calm, nature, families.
A Saturday evening vintage market at Think Park: second-hand clothing, handmade items and accessories.
A water park in Saraphi with slides: you can spend the whole day, drinks and food are available on site, and you can stay overnight — there is accommodation.

items.n: Rules and incentives for solar panels (2024–2026)
items.d: Installing rooftop solar panels has been simplified: home systems up to ~10 kW often need no licences, a tax deduction of up to 200 000 baht (until about 2028), the รง.4 licence has been abolished for businesses, and surplus power can be sold or credited.

items.n: Sai ua — a spot for northern sausage
items.d: A place that, in the author’s words, may have the juiciest sai ua in Chiang Mai: browned to a crispy crust, a bright aroma of herbs, 90% meat. Sai ua is a Northern Thai pork sausage with lemongrass, kaffir lime and chili.
A studio with Thai cooking workshops, classes in traditional crafts (painting and bamboo work) and small cultural events, without tourist crowds.

items.n: Bank of Thailand rule on cash withdrawals of 5 million baht or more
items.d: From April 1, 2026, when withdrawing cash of 5 million baht or more, you must state the purpose of the withdrawal or provide supporting documents (anti-money-laundering measures).

A pop-up by young Akha and Karen people with traditional highland food made from village ingredients, many dishes without fish sauce, sugar or MSG; in the Baan Pawkhrua kitchen studio, 4/2 Soi 3 (Samlan), Phra Singh.
items.h: daily 12:00 – 20:30 (last order until 19:00); the text also says Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays

items.n: Public transport development in Chiang Mai
items.d: The map shows the Chiang Mai City Bus routes; within a month (from spring 2026) AWC buses should start running, and by the end of 2026 the provincial administration (อบจ.) buses and Green Bus, with stops, display boards and digital maps promised.
A mom’s recommendation: a simple clinic, Dr. Artima is attentive and professional, speaks excellent English, and both times they got an appointment the same day.
A clinic where they got the Japanese encephalitis (JE) vaccination; appointments can be booked a day ahead.

items.n: Mae Suai Dam: bamboo raft rafting (แพเปียก)
items.d: A traditional way to relax at the Mae Suai dam: a bamboo raft floats slowly along the channel, you can eat, drink and swim, with cafes around; 35+ operators in zones A and B, book directly; ~110 km from Chiang Mai via highway 118.
items.p: Raft for up to 6 people — 800 baht; 7 people or more — 120 baht per person; mat / seat cushion — 200 baht per day

items.d: March to May is the season of mango with sticky rice; the best variety is Nam Dok Mai, sweetest in April. Where to try it: Khao Niao Mamuang Pa Tan, Mae Varee, Sunday Walking Street; better to buy after 18:00.
A place popular with locals for mango sticky rice, often with queues in the evening; very thick coconut milk and sweet mango.

items.n: Mae Varee Mango Sticky Rice (Chiang Mai)
items.d: Mango sticky rice in the classic style with consistent quality.
A small cozy coffee and milk cafe: mango bingsu and other mango desserts, coffee; dogs welcome.

items.n: Mural about Chiang Mai’s history by the Mae Kha canal (Tha Phae Inn)
items.d: A student mural about the history of Chiang Mai on the wall of the Tha Phae Inn hotel by the wooden bridge over the Mae Kha canal near Tha Phae Gate; a new photo spot.
An eco-community: they grow a food forest and rent out space for workshops; there is a waiting form for accommodation, and volunteers and short-term guests are not accepted right now.

A cafe in the mountains with elephants: if you arrive a little before opening, you can see the elephants walking to the cafe themselves; a basket of fruit for 100 baht is optional, you can pet them and take photos; the place is criticized for elephant riding.

items.n: Nam Bo Noi Village (บ้านน้ำบ่อน้อย)
items.d: A small, little-known traditional Karen village near Huai Tom (landmark: Wat Phra Bat Huai Tom): houses with leaf roofs, a sacred spring, weaving; 1.5–2 hours by car from Chiang Mai.
A natural place with water; better to come before the rainy season while the water is not muddy; you can swim. Entry is free, you need to fill in a form, and there is a snack stall at the start.

A mountain trail race in Chiang Dao and Wiang Haeng, distances 16, 40, 75, 100 and 200 km, elevation gain up to 7 761 m, time limit up to 54 hours; part of the UTMB Index and the iTRA National League.
The buzzworthy spicy “Doctor Jack’s tears shrimp”; located opposite the Ping Phayom hotel, open daily from 17:00 until everything is sold out.
items.h: Open every day without days off from 17:00 until everything is sold out

items.n: เจดีย์มรรค ๘ (Atthapanya Patipanuson)
items.d: The Chedi of the Eightfold Path at Wat Phra Chao Ton Luang: an octagonal stupa 25 m tall without columns, stained glass, a Buddha statue of Carrara marble, and a small museum of Luangpu Plian’s relics under the stupa.

The temple now charges entry and the grounds are being actively cleaned; the quiet library has a second floor and books on Buddhism; shoes are removed in the caves, and there are bats on the ceiling, so better to bring socks.

A functional medicine clinic (88/25 Moo 3, Tawangtan, Saraphi): Urine Organic Acids Test for metabolism, gut and vitamin deficiencies; in March 2026 a free sleep support program with TCM doctor Dr. Neon and physiotherapist Pupae.

The tradition of worshipping the stupa (phra that) of your birth year: for example, Rat is Wat Phra That Si Chom Thong, Ox is Lampang Luang, Goat is Doi Suthep, Rooster is Hariphunchai, Elephant is Doi Tung; the post has links to temples for all 12 signs.

items.n: Wat Phra That Si Chom Thong
items.d: The sacred stupa for those born in the year of the Rat (the tradition of worshipping the stupa of your birth year).
The sacred stupa for those born in the year of the Ox (the tradition of worshipping the stupa of your birth year).
The sacred stupa for those born in the year of the Tiger (the tradition of worshipping the stupa of your birth year).
The sacred stupa for those born in the year of the Rabbit (the tradition of worshipping the stupa of your birth year).
The sacred place for those born in the year of the Dragon; some believe that what should be venerated is not the stupa but the Phra Buddha Sihing Buddha image.
The sacred stupa for those born in the year of the Snake: Mahabodhi Temple or Wat Ched Yot.
The sacred stupa for those born in the year of the Horse: Shwedagon Pagoda or Wat Phra Borommathat Tak.
The sacred stupa for those born in the year of the Goat (the tradition of worshipping the stupa of your birth year).
The sacred stupa for those born in the year of the Monkey (the tradition of worshipping the stupa of your birth year).
The sacred stupa for those born in the year of the Elephant (the tradition of worshipping the stupa of your birth year).
A bakery with coffee: daily pastries made with French butter and flour, Belgian chocolate and Japanese matcha, sourdough bread; delivery via Grab.

items.n: Phra Mae Guan Yin Maha Pothisat พระแม่กวนอิมมหาโพธิสัตว์
items.d: A quiet Chinese temple “like something from an old postcard”; kids enjoy walking through the tunnel through the mouths of a tiger and a dragon, where scenes from the Buddha’s life are painted.
A cafe with exotic animals in Chiang Rai, interesting for kids.
A villa with views of rice fields and tasty breakfasts.
Offer: an hour and a half in the herbal sauna and a free scrub.
items.p: promotion: 1.5 hours of herbal sauna + free scrub

items.d: A men’s barbershop where they pour you coffee during the haircut.

The masseuse Tep (addition to post #2284): anti-cellulite massage with ginger oil, and she also worked on the sciatic nerve and did a belly massage; when booking, say “anti-cellulite with ginger oil” or oil per the price list.
The temple has a Ho Trai (library of sacred texts) from 1903: a two-story building in a mixed Chinese, Lanna and Burmese style with stucco, mirror mosaic, carving and jataka paintings on the balcony.
Royal Park Rajapruek: the skywalk zone is especially beautiful closer to sunset, a good place for a photo shoot.
A relatively new place from the well-known Madei Slowfish: food from fresh ingredients, sourdough bread with homemade butter, a varied menu and a special menu.

items.n: Pet Sister: home nanny for pets
items.d: A side job caring for small and medium-sized cats and dogs while owners travel: feeding, playing, cleaning; communicates in English.
A cosmetology clinic with a doctor of more than 15 years’ experience (practice in the US and Bangkok); according to a follower’s review she does fillers well, and also laser hair removal.
Freediving lessons with the CMAS instructor Fai, you can learn even without swimming skills; group and individual training every week, photos during the lessons are free.
items.p: BASIC FREEDIVE — 4900 baht; POOL COURSE — 6900 baht; PERSONAL FREEDIVE — 8900 baht (individual, 4 days); REFRESH SKILL — 2200 baht

items.n: Halyn Matcha Cafe ハリンティー
items.d: A cozy homey cafe with a large choice of Japanese matcha (ceremonial and organic from different regions), 10+ matcha fusion drinks and Japanese desserts; pet-friendly, large parking lot, EV charging, air purifiers.
A restaurant with slow-smoked meat and steaks; open evenings from Thursday to Sunday.
items.h: From 6 to 10 pm, Thursday to Sunday

items.d: A board game club with clean air, everyone is welcome; according to reviews, the atmosphere is such that people return to Chiang Mai for it.
A shop of adaptogenic mushroom extracts without sugar or alcohol, even with Siberian chaga.
At the market you can buy dried cordyceps to brew like tea, and reishi, at prices much lower than in Moscow.
A pleasant atmospheric bar in a former dye workshop for aesthetes and lovers of privacy, with music kept at a carefully judged volume.

items.n: Why the Wat Ket area was the richest
items.d: 120–150 years ago Wat Ket on the Ping River was the main port and center of the teak trade, home to Chinese and Burmese merchants and European missionaries; when roads arrived, trade moved away.

items.n: Why Chiang Mai has teak houses rather than stone ones
items.d: There was a lot of teak, it is durable and resistant to moisture and termites, wooden houses withstand earthquakes and heat better; stone was rare, and brick and concrete came only in the 20th century.
A colonial teak house in the Wat Ket area on the Ping River with four big columns and “gingerbread house” style carving.
A larger colonial teak house in the Wat Ket area on six columns with gingerbread carving, a symbol of the wealth of merchants in the river trade era.
A palace from around 1913 linked to Princess Dara Rasmi, in a mixed Thai and European style; now a museum with royal furniture, clothing and items from the Lanna era.

A museum of the history of the Wat Ket area in one of the oldest teak houses (130–150 years old): old photos of Chiang Mai, trade items, belongings of missionaries and merchants; the temple for those born in the year of the Dog is nearby.
The most beautiful carved teak house in northern Thailand (around 1897) in the gingerbread style, combining Victorian and Lanna styles; a museum with 19th-century furniture and interiors.

items.n: The Blue Jasmine x Jim Thompson
items.d: A restored Japanese sleeper train, a mobile boutique hotel with a Jim Thompson interior; a 9 days/8 nights tour Bangkok → Ayutthaya → Uthai Thani → Sukhothai → Chiang Mai, about 6 trips a year, up to 37 passengers.
items.p: Classic cabin from ≈195,000–245,000 baht; Premium cabin about 270,000–313,500 baht; Premium Suite (with butler) up to ≈310,000–413,500 baht per person

items.d: A social enterprise supporting refugees from Myanmar: Shan, Thai and Burmese food, cocktails, beer, wine; hosts music nights.
A very beautiful spa center, in the list of 50 refuge spots from smog.

items.s: coffee shop chain with air purifiers
items.d: All Roastniyom coffee shops have air purifiers, a pleasant place to sit and work in smog season.
A farm and cafe where you can spend time with elephants in nature; celebrities who value privacy choose such places.

items.n: Mae Wang Elephant Cafe at River

items.n: Feline parvovirus outbreak: advice for pet owners
items.d: Vet clinics are packed because of the same virus that killed the tigers: it is better to keep animals at home and get the combined vaccine. It is also advised to cook chicken and pork well.

items.d: A visa run to Laos through the small Ban Huak border crossing: mostly no tourist fees, the border is open until 18:00; 20 km away is a quiet village with guesthouses on Google Maps. A bus from Chiang Mai to Chiang Khum, then a songthaew for 80 baht.
items.p: Songthaew from Chiang Kham to the border 80 baht

items.n: Kaeng Ko — the flooded Wat Ban Khao Ko temple

items.n: Tea house with a small garden
items.d: A beautiful tea house: vegan curry, ceramics at the entrance, rooms full of flowers and paintings, a small garden in the yard and an unusual tea service.

items.n: Warm clothes for the cool season
items.d: At the end of November the mornings in Chiang Mai are around 15 degrees; the author ordered warm merino wool socks, insulated boot-slippers and a fleece jacket from SHEIN, and the socks turned out to be very warm.

A concert by the Belgian pianist Jonas Dept on a rooftop with a view of the city and Doi Suthep at sunset; seats are limited, booking is required. According to the author, the next concert is at the same place on January 9.
A simple, unpretentious Turkish cafe: the author likes the combination of falafel, hummus and salad; a friendly waitress put cartoons on for the children.
A small shop near Royal Project with inexpensive home goods: mattresses, cotton bedding sets, sets made of Japanese cotton, towels.

About 100 flavors of homemade ice cream, including vegan ones made with coconut milk and unusual ones like mango sticky rice and Thai barbecue; reasonable prices.
A Japanese second-hand shop with porcelain, dishware and New Year decorations; the author found Pyrex glassware, items with no price tag are sold by weight (the glass cost 80 baht).
items.p: dishes without a price tag — by weight

items.d: A regular (not second-hand) shop with Japanese goods.
The park where the 2025 flower festival took place; even without the festival it is a pleasant place for picnics and walks.
Two serums on Lazada for combination skin: they absorb quickly, suit heat and humidity, are free of silicones and alcohol, and can be applied under powder.
A yoga studio: about 10 classes a week with 4 teachers (ashtanga, power, vinyasa, sound healing, relax), teachers with excellent English. They arrange student visas with unlimited classes.
items.p: annual pass — about 50 baht per class; student visa 60 000 baht a year
